Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand is visiting Long Island Friday to discuss new bipartisan legislation that would expand the U.S. Small Business Administration’s microloan program. Gillibrand was making a stop at Farmingdale State College to say that the Mircoloan Modernization Act would make it easier for entrepreneurs to access capital to grow their business. The new legislation would be of benefit to women and minority business owners, along with other entrepreneurs, who struggle with access to capital because banks often deny them loans to start and grow a business.

Gillibrand said the act would raise the total limit on outstanding loans to intermediary lending organizations, allowing for more loans to be made to women, minority and other business owners. It would also expand the number of opportunities for more hands-on training assistance so that more small business owners can succeed. Women receive less than 5 percent of conventional small business loans, yet they own nearly 40 percent of businesses across the nation, according to the U.S. Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship. And loan denial rates for minority firms were nearly three times higher than those of non-minority-owned firms, U.S. Department of Commerce reports.

This bipartisan legislation was sponsored by Sen. Deb Fischer (R-NE) and has passed in the House of Representatives. The bill is also cosponsored by Senators Tim Scott (R-SC), Chris Coons (D-DE), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Joe Donnelly (D-IN), and Gary Peters (D-MI).

Image-based counting aims to infer the number of people, vehicles, or any other objects present in images. It has a wide range of applications such as traffic control, environment survey, and public safety. Most existing research focuses on learning a model from a single dataset. Only [3] and [20] propose to train a model on multiple datasets simultaneously in a multi-task setting. In this paper, we propose a method to incrementally learn to count new objects or to count in a new domain. This has the advantage that it does not require collecting data on a single server for training. Moreover, annotators can focus on just labeling instances of a single class (typically annotated with a single point), which reduces the annotation effort required for adding new classes.

Continual learning (CL) addresses the problem of training a model from a non-stationary distribution. It is important because data in the real-world might not be jointly available (e.g., due to data privacy or legislation). Moreover, often the previous data cannot be revisited due to privacy or storage restrictions. Researchers have explored continual learning in many tasks, e.g., classification [15, 16], segmentation [2, 8], and object detection [30]. However, continual learning for counting systems, to the best of our knowledge, has not yet been studied.

One of the main challenges of continual learning is catastrophic forgetting. After training on new data, models tend to forget the knowledge extracted from previous data. In the past few years, people tried to alleviate this issue by using replay examples [26, 38], expand networks [40], and regularization [15, 16]. As one of the most promising methods, regularization can be further categorized as weight regularization [15] and data (or functional) regularization [16].

Twenty-five years ago, something very uncommon happened on our planetary neighbor, Mars. NASA launched a shuttle named "Viking 1" into space, designed to take pictures of planets and to scout for possible landing sites for its sister ship, Viking 2. As Viking 1 captured images, it spotted a shadowy likeness of a human face. This face, with an enormous head nearly two miles from end to end, appeared to be staring back at the cameras from a region of the Red Planet called Cydonia. These are some of the intriguing details about the "Human Face."

Even though I am a scientist at NASA, some of my colleagues and I, who are also scientists, agreed it was probably just another Martian mesa, common around Cydonia. This one, however, had unusual shadows, making it resemble an Egyptian Pharaoh. I was discussing the "Face" with a colleague, John, who believed it was created by aliens. I told him that we had unveiled the image for the public, noting, "a huge rock formation... which resembles a human head... formed by shadows, giving the illusion of eyes, nose, and mouth."

One of the primary challenges of the boundary element method (BEM) is efficiently approximating the singular integrals that arise in boundary integral equations (BIE). A common strategy to address this issue is to superimpose known solutions onto the unknown fields to eliminate the singularities (Cruse, 1974; Liu and Rudolphi, 1999; Liu, 2000; Klaseboer et al., 2009). This technique is known as the nonsingular, regularized, or desingularized BEM. It is applied to linear elasticity (Scott et al., 2013; Taus et al., 2019), Stokes flow (Taus et al., 2016; Harmel et al., 2018), and the Helmholtz equation (Simpson et al., 2014; Peake et al., 2015), among others. Klaseboer et al. (2012) extended the nonsingular BEM to fluid mechanics, considering the Stokes equations for viscous flow, the Laplace equation for potential flow, and the Helmholtz equation for free-streamline flow.

While the nonsingular BEM avoids the use of singular integrals and is frequently employed in recent studies, it necessitates additional integrals and the knowledge of analytical solutions, and is less efficient and more complex to implement (Khayat and Wilton, 2005).

Pioneer power theories for analyzing electrical systems were developed by Steinmetz, Kennelly, Heaviside, and others by the end of the XIX century [1] , [2] , [3] . Nowadays, these theories remain a topic of discussion and debate regarding their accuracy and physical interpretation [4] . Some were formulated in the frequency domain, like those by Budeanu [5] and Czarnecki [6] , while others, like those by Fryze [7] , Akagi [8] , and Depenbrock [9] , were formulated in the time domain. Recently, Lev-Ari [10] and Salmerón [11] have made notable contributions to the field by utilizing the Hilbert Transform (HT) and tensor algebra, respectively. These theories aim to elucidate the power-transfer process between complex electrical systems and establish mathematical concepts related to fictitious powers, such as reactive power, which hold significant engineering value. However, existing proposals lack the capability to separate current components in the time domain under conditions like voltage distortion, asymmetry, load non-linearity, or their combinations, as highlighted in the literature [4] , [12] .

In this paper, a new approach is introduced to address these limitations, utilizing geometric algebra (GA) and the Hilbert Transform (HT) as mathematical tools. GA, a versatile tool, can model various physical and mathematical problems [13] , and, when applied, can separate current components, particularly those of engineering significance, in systems, irrespective of the number of phases, including single-phase, as emphasized [14] , [15] .

In this paper, we consider the computation of the following nonlocal Helmholtz equation:

\[Lu(x) = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}} u(x) - u(y) \gamma(x, y) \, dy\]

where \(f(x) \in L^{2}(\mathbb{R})\) has a bounded support Ω f, and \(k\) is a constant related to the traditional wavenumber for the local Helmholtz equation. The kernel function \(\gamma(x, y)\) satisfies \(\gamma(x, y) \geq 0\) and \(\gamma(x, y) = \gamma(y, x\).

While most works focus on simulating nonlocal problems with free or fixed boundary conditions on bounded domains, there are applications where simulating in an infinite medium is more suitable, such as wave or crack propagation in the whole space. However, dealing with unbounded spatial domains poses computational challenges as traditional methods like finite element and finite difference methods lead to an infinite number of degrees of freedom. One successful approach to overcome this challenge is the artificial boundary method (ABM), which introduces an artificial boundary to limit the domain of interest and designs absorbing boundary conditions (ABCs) to absorb waves at the artificial boundaries.

PML (Perfectly Matched Layer) is a popular and effective method for solving wave scattering problems. Recent progress has been made in adapting PML for nonlocal problems, including nonlocal PMLs for peridynamics. Different approaches have been proposed for applying PML to nonlocal problems, such as treating the nonlocal kernel as a convolution or introducing new complex-valued operators.

The goal of this paper is to develop PMLs as ABCs for nonlocal Helmholtz equations with various kernels and wavenumbers in multiple dimensions. We extend the strategy developed in previous works to derive nonlocal PML equations directly from the weak form of the nonlocal Helmholtz equation. Two types of nonlocal PML modifications for 2D equations are introduced, one involving stretching the Cartesian coordinate and the other stretching the radial coordinate in polar coordinates.

The paper is organized as follows: In Section 2, we derive nonlocal PML equations using complex coordinate transforms. Section 3 studies the efficiency of our PMLs in 1D for specific kernels. Section 4 truncates the nonlocal computational region with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions, and introduces AC schemes for solving the resulting truncated problems. In Section 5, numerical examples in 1D and 2D are presented to analyze the "numerical reflections" caused by PML modifications and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

Semantic layout manipulation involves editing an image by altering its semantic label map, such as changing the semantic layout or adding and removing objects, as shown in Figure 1. This technique has numerous practical applications in image editing, including photo editing [1], image retargeting [2], restoration [3], composition [4], and image melding [5]. However, it remains relatively underexplored due to the complexities of predicting intricate, non-rigid spatial deformations and the domain gap between the input image and the target semantic layout. The key challenge is to develop an effective method for transferring visual patterns from the input image to the target semantic layout.

Earlier methods [2], [6], [7], [8] in image synthesis allowed users to designate semantic regions for guided image manipulation. These techniques employed non-parametric modeling of patches [6], [8] or patch-based copy-pasting strategies [2], [5], [7], [9], [10] to create new images. While effective for generating stationary textures or repetitive structures, they struggled to generate new semantic structures.

Recently, advancements in deep generative models, such as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), have significantly improved structure-guided image manipulation. Champandard et al. [12] developed a semantic-aware loss on a pretrained classifier [13] for semantic-guided artwork generation. Zhu et al. [14] optimized the latent code of a generative model for layout-constrained image generation. More recently, guided inpainting methods [15], [16], [17] have been introduced for manipulating natural images. These approaches mask certain regions of images and generate new pixels to align with user-provided edge scribbles. In the realm of semantic layout manipulation, recent work [3] extends inpainting networks by incorporating semantic label maps in the missing region as inputs. Despite promising results, this approach faces limitations: 1) it discards pixels within the masked region, potentially losing important visual details useful for manipulation, and 2) it lacks a spatial alignment mechanism to handle significant layout changes.

Conversely, methods utilizing attention-based warping [18], [19] have shown promise in global reference-based layout editing. Zhang et al. [18] introduced a cross-domain correspondence network to warp input images to desired layouts. Zheng et al. [19] proposed a spatial-channel attention method to align multi-scale visual features with a new layout. These methods can manage dramatic layout changes due to explicit warping. However, global layout editing does not consider contextual information from the input image or user manipulation intentions. Applying global warping for local tasks can inadvertently modify surrounding image content, which is undesirable. Moreover, the warping schemes of [18], [19] are computationally intensive, limiting them to low-resolution warping [18] or application to individual regions independently [19], which can result in a loss of visual details in the warped image. To address these challenges, we extend the guided image inpainting framework to include a warped version of the original image as an additional information source for local manipulation tasks.

Telemedicine is an increasingly popular treatment method in the medical field due to its high efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and safety. Compared to traditional medical care, telemedicine enhances treatment efficiency by facilitating prompt feedback between doctors and patients. It utilizes technologies like computer-aided pose assessment to provide precise and objective patient information, reducing the need for therapist supervision and in-person visits, thus cutting down on rehabilitation costs. Additionally, telemedicine provides opportunities for individuals with limited mobility or disabilities to receive care at home, reducing the risk of exposure to unhygienic conditions and infections.

In order to deliver remote services effectively, certain constraints need to be met, such as optimizing computing power on personal devices, ensuring high precision, and achieving real-time performance. For instance, an attention cube is introduced in Fig. 1 to enclose the target and gray points represent attention points on each surface, with darker colors indicating higher weights.

Telemedicine finds extensive application in predicting movement disorders, diagnosing movement disorders, and sports rehabilitation training. Human pose estimation (HPE) plays a crucial role in reconstructing the 3D human body skeleton for these purposes. While sensor-based methods have limitations like requiring attachment to the patient's body, learning-based HPE technology, driven by advancements in deep learning and computer vision, offers a non-contact and easily calibrated alternative. To address the accuracy and latency issues of existing methods, a novel Attention Cube Regression Network (ACRNet) has been proposed to provide a unified and efficient network for multi-view depth image-based estimation work.

ACRNet revolutionizes the estimation process by utilizing an attention cube to gather information from all surfaces and estimate the 3D positions of human joints, improving accuracy and efficiency. By integrating feature maps from various viewpoints and utilizing dynamic weights based on cross similarity, the network achieves precise joint position regression. This approach ensures that informative attention points are emphasized while less relevant points are disregarded for accurate results.

Validation tests on the ITOP dataset showcase ACRNet's superior performance compared to existing methods in front-view settings, with comparable results in top-view settings. The model also boasts high running speeds, achieving 92.3 FPS on a single NVIDIA Tesla V100 GPU, enabling real-time operation. Furthermore, a new medical multi-view upper body movement dataset (UBM) from healthy subjects was collected and assessed, demonstrating consistent improvements over existing baselines. Overall, ACRNet emerges as a fully differentiable multi-view regression network tailored for telemedicine, enhancing the estimation of 3D human joint positions.

Janice lazily scratched her butt as she gazed at the tall, cloaked figure in the hallway. Through her tousled black hair, she studied him closely, noting the snow dripping onto her doorstep. Her eyes lingered momentarily on the cloven hooves peeking out from beneath his cloak, surrounded by a growing puddle. Odd, considering it was New York City in July. But then again, she wasn't a meteorologist.

Stretching and yawning, she turned away, closing the door sleepily. It was only 2 p.m., far too early for whatever this guy was trying to sell. "Sorry, I'm not interested."

A hoof wedged forward, preventing the door from closing, and a red hand with large claws pushed it open. Goat-like eyes met Janice's annoyed gaze. "What the hell. Get out." The slim girl leaned against the door, but it refused to budge against the creature's strength. "I told you I'm not interested."

The creature hissed, "What did you do, Janice?"

"I don't know, but right now I'm trying to get you out of my apartment. Leave, or I'll call the cops!"

The creature laughed. "Cops? Do you even know who I am?" The heavy wooden door suddenly dissolved into hot ash. Janice stood there awkwardly, realizing that no barrier remained between her and the intruder.

With a small, frustrated noise, she let the doorknob drop into the dust and strode into the kitchen. "Whatever. You owe me for that door. It was... at least $3,000. Yeah, that sounds right."

"What? That door was only $800 at most. Where did you get a number like that?" He paused, then shook his head angrily. "No, it doesn't matter. I'm here because you ruined Hell. It's like Christmas down there."

Janice stomped back into the room, holding a bottle of whiskey. "You don't say. How did little old mortal me manage that?" She took a swig before pouring a glass. She glanced back at the creature. "You're not getting any."

"I don't care. I followed the clues—"

"Ah, a good old-fashioned Nancy Drew..."

"AND I believe you're behind Hell freezing over."

Janice rolled her eyes, gesturing impatiently in his direction. "How do you know Hell froze over? Are you a devil or something?"

This represents one of the lengthiest periods of low volatility in the 21st century.
In a prior article discussing the Z(30) volatility indicator, it was noted that the indicator was approaching a significant level of 0.85 points.
The Z(30) is essentially a moving average of the coefficient of variation for the S&P 500, based on the SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (SPY). The following table displays the percentile of this indicator based on historical data.
The most recent update was in late March, and since then, over the past seventeen trading days, the indicator has dipped below 0.85 points and has yet to rise above this particular threshold.
I stressed the significance of the 0.85 level because over the past 4,320 trading days since early 2000, the indicator has been below 0.85 points for only 256 days.
The current scenario is even more intriguing with the recent seventeen consecutive days below the 0.85 mark, marking it as one of the lengthiest periods of low trending for this indicator.
In recent years, there have been only four instances where the indicator remained at such low levels for an extended time.
Between the latter part of January and mid-February 2017, the market took a pause before surging above 2,300 points and has not dipped below since then, marking an 18-day consecutive point on the graph.
From mid-August to mid-September 2016, the market remained relatively stable around 2,180 points, followed by volatile days due to concerns over an impending interest rate hike, making it a 20-day consecutive point on the graph.
The 22-day point dates back to February 2007, a time marred by a significant market decline fueled by worries stemming from Asia and Europe.
The longest period of market calmness, lasting 35 days, occurred between May and June 2015, only to end abruptly due to concerns regarding Greek debt.
The subsequent graph illustrates the trend of Z(30) compared to SPY from 2013 to the present.
It will be fascinating to observe whether this low volatility period persists and breaks the 2015 record or if it is disrupted by a significant move, either upwards or downwards, leading to a break in this streak.
I will continue to monitor and provide updates.

I have strong reservations about driverless cars, primarily because I believe they pose significant risks. Driverless cars may actually be more prone to accidents compared to when a person is behind the wheel. Although it is reported that "their cars have driven more than half a million miles without a crash," this statistic only assures safety for a limited period. As these all-computerized vehicles age, they could become more hazardous, effectively asking for trouble.

Moreover, driverless cars are not truly driverless. As noted, "Google cars aren't truly driverless." The idea of a driverless car might provide a false sense of security, leading individuals to become complacent and less attentive to the road. If a car suddenly signals a driver to take control, a driver might not be prepared, especially in complex traffic situations, which increases the risk of accidents.

The cost of driverless cars is another major concern, making them inaccessible to the average consumer. Even without considering the price of the car itself, the associated expenses are significant. The article mentions the need for smart roads, which, "although they worked surprisingly well, required massive upgrades to existing roads, something that was simply too expensive to be practical." Additionally, the cars rely on complex systems, such as the LIDAR, to replicate the skills of a human driver, further driving up the cost.

Would you buy a car that could drive you around without you having to do anything? Personally, I would not. There are too many things that could go wrong. We all know that technology can break down at times, as even our computers fail for no reason. So why let a car, which could end your life in a split second, drive you around? I wouldn't want to take that risk.

The passage "Driverless Cars Are Coming" explains that even with autonomous technology, the driver has to take over at times. They mention, "the cars can steer, accelerate, and brake themselves, but all are designed to notify the driver when the road ahead requires human skills, such as navigating through work zones and around accidents." But what if, one time, the car did not notify the driver, or the driver fell asleep? This could end the driver’s life, and potentially, someone else’s, too. Although the passage states, "the car can handle driving functions at speeds up to 25 mph, but special touch sensors make sure the driver keeps hold of the wheel," I know plenty of people, mostly teenagers, who would disconnect the wheel sensor. So, why take the chance, risking lives, for the sake of a driverless car?

If we are going to have driverless cars, they need to be safer before anyone can, or should, drive them.

This campaign follows a series of events that sparked concerns about press freedom, including police raids on the homes of journalists and media organizations. The question raised by these front pages is clear: When the government conceals the truth, what are they hiding?

The campaign coincided with Australian Federal Police Commissioner Reece Kershaw's testimony before a Senate committee investigating police matters. Kershaw emphasized the importance of police independence and freedom of the press, pledging to address the concerns raised by news editors. The police have established new guidelines for investigating unauthorized disclosures, aiming to balance security concerns with press freedom.

The media campaign highlights instances of government secrecy, such as the refusal to disclose abusive practices in nursing homes or the extent of agricultural land sold to foreign entities. News Corp. Australia's executive chairman, Michael Miller, underscored the need for transparency, stating that citizens should be wary of government attempts to limit access to information.

Australian media organizations argue that press freedoms have been compromised by over 70 counterterrorism and security laws enacted since the September 11, 2001 attacks. In response, the government initiated a parliamentary inquiry to examine the impact of law enforcement and intelligence powers on press freedom. This ongoing dialogue reflects a broader debate about the balance between national security concerns and the public's right to information.

In this evolving landscape, the Australian press continues to advocate for greater transparency and accountability from the government.

Accurate estimation of object pose (translation and rotation) is crucial for autonomous robots to grasp and manipulate objects in an unstructured environment. Even small inaccuracies in the belief of the object pose can generate incorrect grasp configurations and lead to failures in manipulation tasks. Strategies based on vision sensors are commonly used for estimating the pose of the object, but there is residual uncertainty in the estimated pose due to incorrect calibration of the sensors, environmental conditions (occlusions, presence of extreme light, and low visibility conditions), and object properties (transparent, specular, reflective).

Tactile sensors in combination with robot proprioception provide high fidelity local measurements regarding object pose. However, mapping entire objects using tactile sensors is highly inefficient and time-consuming, which necessitates the use of active data collection for object pose estimation. Furthermore, due to the extremely low sparsity of the tactile data, novel techniques are required for performing pose estimation. Typical batch registration methods for pose estimation such as ICP or its variants have low performance when sparse data is available that arrive sequentially as is the case with tactile measurements. Hence, filter-based approaches are generally preferred for sequential data.

A probabilistic method was proposed to perform registration given sparse point cloud, surface normal measurements, and the geometric model of the object. While tactile data can be collected in a randomized manner or driven by a human-teleoperator, active touch strategies that allow for autonomous data collection and reduction of redundant data collection are required. Several works have used information gain metric based on the uncertainty of the object's pose to determine the next best touching action to localize the object.

In the literature, the next best action selection is based on expected information gain via metrics such as Shannon entropy, Kullback-Leibler divergence, mutual information, and so on. However, a number of other related information theoretic metrics remain to be explored in the robotic domain. In this article, we empirically evaluate various information theoretic criteria for selecting the next best action in the context of tactile-based localization. We use our novel probabilistic translation-invariant Quaternion filter (TIQF) for pose estimation. TIQF decouples the estimation of rotation and translation and estimates rotation using a linear Kalman filter. We empirically evaluate the following criteria: (a) Kullback-Leibler divergence, (b) Shannon entropy, and (c) mutual information, to determine the most effective approach for tactile-based pose estimation.

Stephanie said, "Superman is close by. If we call him, he can be here within a few minu -- -" 

"No thanks." 

"What about Batman?" 

"Nope." 

"Flash? Iron Man? Spider-Man?" 

"Not interested, ma'am," the boy said weakly. 

"Uh.... You do know he's killed kids, too, right? You're not asking for a good guy." 

"That's not my problem. He hasn't killed me. He's not responsible for my cancer." 

Stephanie grabbed her notes and swiftly exited the room. She was met at the end of the hall by her boss, Jeremiah Lincoln, who had been running the "Meet Your Heroes!" organization for a solid decade.

لن يصل التحديث الجديد، نظام أندرويد 11، إلى جميع الهواتف في نفس الوقت. ستكون هواتف غوغل بكسل أول من يحصل على التحديث، بينما ستكون نوكيا من أوائل الشركات التي ستتبنى التحديث، تليها ون بلاس، شاومي، وأوبو. في المقابل، ستستغرق سامسونغ، هواوي، وإل جي وقتاً أطول لتكييف الميزات الجديدة مع واجهات المستخدم الخاصة بها.

من أبرز المزايا الجديدة لوحات عائمة تشبه الفقاعات، تعرض تنبيهات بوصول ردود أو رسائل في الدردشات فوق التطبيقات الأخرى، مما يسمح بالرد السريع دون الخروج من التطبيق الحالي.

يُستخدم نظام أندرويد في حوالي 2.5 مليار جهاز حول العالم. ولضمان تقديم تحديث شامل وفعّال، تُركّز الميزات الجديدة على أدوات التواصل، حيث تتجمع التنبيهات والمحادثات والدردشات في شريط جديد يظهر طولياً على الجانب الأيمن للهاتف. بالإضافة إلى ذلك، تم تطوير أداة لمساعدة المستخدمين في إدارة العديد من تطبيقات المراسلة مثل فيسبوك ماسنجر، أندرويد ماسنجر، تويتر، واتساب، وتليغرام.

كما يُقدّم النظام الجديد ميزات قوية لتبسيط استخدام الهاتف الذكي، مع تسهيل إعداداته. يمكن للمستخدم استدعاء عناصر التحكم لجميع الأجهزة المتصلة من مكان واحد عن طريق الضغط المطول على زر الطاقة.

تتضمن الميزات الجديدة أيضًا تحسينات في الخصوصية، وأداة لتسجيل الشاشة محليًا (native screen recording)، والتي تغني عن استخدام تطبيقات خارجية لتلك الوظيفة. سيسهل التحديث إعطاء الأولوية لمصادر رسائل الدردشة عبر تطبيقات متعددة، والتحكم في أدوات المنزل الذكي.

تشمل مزايا الخصوصية الجديدة القدرة على منح تطبيق ما صلاحية الوصول لمرة واحدة فقط، بدلاً من الوصول المستمر. وهذا يتضمن التحكم في استخدام الميكروفونات، الكاميرات، ومعلومات الموقع.

Driverless cars are a promising concept, but they have their drawbacks. They are more susceptible to accidents than cars driven by humans. One significant vulnerability of driverless cars lies in their complex sensor systems. The rooftop sensor is especially critical, and if it sustains any damage, the car is unable to operate autonomously. In such a scenario, the passenger would need to take control and drive the car. Malfunctions, especially on highways, could lead to car accidents and related incidents. Furthermore, issues of sensor privacy must also be carefully considered.

Privacy is another major concern, as manufacturers are contemplating the use of cameras to monitor drivers' focus on the road. This invasion of privacy, with manufacturers surveilling occupants, raises significant ethical issues. Privacy, along with the need to invest in a car that still requires human intervention, is a critical concern.

Despite the advancements, driverless cars still demand human intervention, particularly in navigating through construction zones and managing unforeseen incidents. Manufacturers have implemented systems to alert drivers to potential issues, suggesting that, in practice, the driver still plays a pivotal role.

In the article "The Challenge of Exploring Venus," the author discusses why Venus exploration is fraught with danger but also why it captures scientists' curiosity. The article delves into the potential risks and rewards of such an endeavor, shedding light on Venus's composition and its intriguing history. Through a combination of data-driven insights, Q&A exchanges, and a historical perspective on past explorations of Venus, the author presents a compelling argument.

Data-based information plays a crucial role in outlining the hazards associated with exploring Venus. For instance, the author highlights that temperatures on its surface can soar above 800 degrees Fahrenheit, while atmospheric pressure exceeds that experienced on Earth by 90 times (Paragraph 3). These extreme conditions underscore why human missions to Venus would be perilous, making exploration seemingly unfeasible. By providing such detailed facts, not only does the author bolster their argument but they also educate readers about the complexities that make NASA's interest in Venus so profound.

The use of question-and-answer segments further reinforces the dangers inherent in exploring Venus. By addressing common queries like "Why are scientists even discussing further visits to its surface?" (Paragraph 4), the author demonstrates their expertise while engaging readers' curiosity. This approach not only lends credibility to their claims but also fosters trust among readers who seek comprehensive insights into potential missions to Venus.

Moreover, drawing upon historical accounts of previous explorations enriches the narrative and strengthens the author's assertions regarding Venetian exploration challenges. The mention that "Venus was probably covered largely with oceans and could have supported various forms of life" (Paragraph 4) underscores how changes over time have altered our understanding of this enigmatic planet. Such historical context not only deepens readers' appreciation for ongoing research efforts related to Venus but also underscores NASA's evolving strategies for possible future exploratory missions.

In conclusion, through a judicious blend of data analysis, interactive dialogue with readers via Q&A sections, and an examination of historical precedents in exploring this celestial neighbor we call home – Earth –the author effectively argues that embarking on missions to explore Venus remains an incredibly daunting task fraught with uncertainties and risks.

Notre pays doit accueillir les Jeux Olympiques de la Jeunesse en 2022. Dans ce contexte, il est crucial de réfléchir à la situation des sports au Sénégal. Depuis l'Indépendance, le pays a participé à de nombreuses compétitions sportives internationales sans remporter de trophées majeurs. La seule médaille d'argent a été décrochée par Dia Ba aux Jeux Olympiques de Séoul en 2000. Malgré les talents présents dans diverses disciplines, les succès sont rares.

Il est essentiel de repenser la politique sportive pour espérer des victoires aux JOJ 2022. L'athlétisme étant au cœur de ces jeux, il est nécessaire de détecter et former des talents dans toutes les disciplines. Les tournois de l'UASSU constituent une opportunité pour repérer les futurs champions. Les écuries de lutte regorgent également de potentiels champions, qu'il convient d'encadrer pour exceller dans diverses épreuves.

La coopération avec des pays amis pour bénéficier d'entraîneurs de haut niveau est primordiale. Il est impératif d'investir dans la détection et la formation des talents, notamment en encourageant les compétitions organisées par l'UASSU. Il est temps d'agir pour ne pas revivre une déception aux JOJ.

Par ailleurs, la performance des équipes nationales, comme les Lionceaux, est également à revoir. Les éliminations sans gloire soulignent la nécessité d'améliorer la gestion des matchs et de briser la malédiction des quarts de finale. Une réflexion profonde sur les enjeux sportifs nationaux est urgente pour atteindre le succès tant attendu.

En conclusion, il est crucial d'agir rapidement pour mettre en place une stratégie sportive efficace et prometteuse. Les JOJ 2022 offrent une opportunité unique de briller, mais cela nécessite un engagement fort et des actions concrètes. Il est temps de valoriser les talents locaux et de viser l'excellence sur la scène sportive internationale.

A wave of challenges awaits health insurance shoppers as the Affordable Care Act's primary enrollment period kicks off this Wednesday with new deadlines, escalating prices, and fewer support options.

Nicolas Moriello, a broker from Delaware, describes the prevailing sentiment as one of confusion. Among the issues he often clarifies with customers is the continued existence of the Obama-era law. Even former President Barack Obama took to Twitter to remind individuals to select coverage for the upcoming year.

Despite funding cuts and repeal attempts, the health care law endures, obliging most Americans to secure health insurance. State-based marketplaces or exchanges, including HealthCare.gov, offer a range of plans with subsidies, though escalating prices and limited choices prevail in numerous markets due to political discord over the law.

Here's what's new, what remains unchanged, and essential considerations for seeking coverage in 2018:

**Less Time to Decide:** The enrollment window has shrunk by half, commencing on November 1 and concluding on December 15 in most states, unlike the previous year when enrollment extended past the holidays. To avoid last-minute rushes, it's advisable not to delay shopping, considering the time-consuming search process and potential website slowdowns.

**Fewer Helpers Available:** Finding assistance may be more challenging with reduced funding for navigator positions and cessation of programs offering aid in libraries and urban areas. Agents may also be scarce due to commission reductions. HealthCare.gov provides a "Find Local Help" option and a helpline for queries.

**Prices: Expect Hikes:** Premiums for silver plans are soaring by an average of 34%, pushing the monthly bill for a 50-year-old single shopper from $554 to $743. Gold coverage prices are rising by 16%, while bronze plans see an 18% increase. Price changes will vary across markets.

**More Financial Assistance:** Tax credits, based on silver plan costs, are expected to rise, benefiting those with lower incomes. Some credits may cover the entire bronze plan bill, which typically involves a high deductible. Customers ineligible for tax credits should explore options beyond ACA marketplaces for potential savings.

**Don't Overlook Compliance:** The ACA mandates most Americans to purchase compliant coverage, or face penalties potentially exceeding $1,000. The IRS enforces this requirement, urging filers to disclose coverage status in tax returns.

**Shop Thoughtfully:** Avoid solely focusing on price when selecting a plan. Consider factors like deductibles, co-insurance, network coverage, and medication inclusion to ensure comprehensive and suitable coverage.

In the modern age, technology has advanced significantly, leading to remarkable innovations such as driverless cars. These vehicles, capable of navigating without human intervention, have both benefits and drawbacks. However, the disadvantages currently outweigh the advantages. Driverless cars pose risks due to their lethality, legal complications, and time-consuming manufacturing processes.

One of the primary concerns about driverless cars is their potential danger. They are not fully tested and can cause severe injury if not handled properly. As highlighted in paragraph 9 of the article "Driverless Cars Are Coming," manufacturers believe that more states will adopt these vehicles once they are proven more reliably safe. This statement underscores their current instability and indicates that further testing is necessary to ensure user safety.

Additionally, utilizing driverless cars for testing purposes presents legal challenges. According to paragraph 9 of the article, "in most states it is illegal even to test computer-driven cars." This legal restriction complicates efforts to identify shortcomings in the technology and hinders its marketability. Moreover, there is an ongoing debate over liability in case of a malfunction: if someone gets injured due to a technological failure, who should be held accountable—the driver or the manufacturer? These issues highlight how legal obstacles impede progress in developing this innovation.

Another significant drawback is the extensive time required for production. The development process is lengthy; as noted by the author in paragraph 5 of the article, "within 10 years" sensor technology evolved sufficiently just to detect dangers like skids or rollovers accurately. Such protracted timelines make it challenging for companies to bring complete products swiftly into consumer markets.

In conclusion, while driverless cars offer exciting possibilities for consumers—such as increased convenience—their negative aspects currently overshadow potential benefits due largely due largely because they are unsafe at present levels (due?)

Avec le beau soleil, le parc du Mont mosan, situé sur les hauteurs de Huy, devrait être en fête tous les jours. Cependant, malgré le confinement, la vie continue : les otaries continuent d'être entraînées en attendant les prochains spectacles. Mais les travées du parc animalier de la Sarte restent désertes depuis le début du confinement, sans un seul visiteur. Le patron, Jean-Marc Vanberg, exprime un vibrant espoir que le parc ne soit pas classé parmi les activités générant un rassemblement de masse. Malheureusement, il n'en sait rien et s'interroge clairement. «Je n’ai aucune information», déclarait-il hier, quelques heures après l'annonce de la Première ministre Sophie Wilmès. «On ne sait absolument rien, on n’est tenu au courant de rien…»

La situation est critique pour le Mont mosan. Jean-Marc Vanberg ne mâche pas ses mots : «On ne saura plus tenir encore longtemps. Ce ne sont pas les 5000€ de prime qu’on peut recevoir qui vont nous permettre de nous en sortir.» Les animaux aquatiques comme les otaries, les phoques, et les manchots ne peuvent pas être laissés sans soin. Ils doivent être nourris, surveillés, et cela a un coût, alors qu’il n’y a plus de rentrée financière. Après l'hiver, la belle saison aurait dû permettre à Jean-Marc Vanberg et à son équipe de rouvrir le Mont mosan. Ce n’est pas le cas. Pourtant, «il faut qu’on rouvre le plus rapidement possible», insiste-t-il, non seulement pour les animaux, mais aussi pour le personnel.

Déjà, tout le personnel du restaurant Le Cortina, repris par le Mont mosan, est en chômage économique. «On va commencer à faire pareil pour le personnel du parc.

▲日本印尼在「2加2会谈」上签署协定，加大两国安保基础。（图／路透）

日本与印尼今天在东京举行「外交及国防部长会议」（2加2会谈），签署由日本提供防卫装备及技术的协定。双方同意加强安全保障领域合作，牵制扩大海洋行动的中国。这是日本与印尼之间第2度召开外交国防部长会议（2加2会谈），上一次是在2015年12月。

日本方面由外务大臣茂木敏充、防卫大臣岸信夫出席；印尼方面由外交部长勒特诺（Retno Marsudi）和国防部长普拉伯沃（Prabowo Subianto）出席。在举行这场2加2会谈前，日本首相菅义伟先接见勒特诺与普拉伯沃举行会谈。菅义伟表示对中国海警局开始实施海警船可动武的海警法等举动感到忧虑。

今天的2加2会谈上签署了日本提供舰艇等给印尼的「防卫装备品暨技术转移协定」，这是继与美国、英国、菲律宾、马来西亚等国签署后，第10国与日本签署这类协定。茂木在会谈后的联合记者会上强调，签署上述协定将成为日本与印尼两国间扩大安全保障合作的基础，将是共同应对区域威胁的象征。

印尼有意提升海军实力，日本考虑对印尼出口舰艇、飞机等。双方针对实现「自由且开放印度太平洋」战略构想达成共识，并针对中国扩大行动的东海及南海局势进行讨论。

A Acuario le fascina lo raro, lo exótico, lo diferente, lo novedoso y lo distinto; siempre tiene que “dar la nota”. Es rápido, inteligente, independiente y sociable y tiene mucha visión de futuro, aunque a veces le cuesta el “aquí y ahora”. Es bueno para trabajar en equipo aunque es individualista y desapegado. Le gusta lo híper-moderno y, aunque no lo podamos creer, tiene muy claro el valor del dinero y es muy ahorrativo.

Deep learning has become a powerful tool for big data mining in Earth Observation (EO) [1]. However, supervised deep learning methods are notoriously data-hungry, requiring large amounts of high-quality labeled data to avoid overfitting. Despite the abundance of Remote Sensing (RS) images, obtaining accurately annotated labels poses a significant challenge due to the expensive, laborious, and time-consuming nature of the annotation process, which often involves domain experts and field surveys.

Nevertheless, there are many sources of labels from which we can easily obtain large amounts of labeled data with minimal efforts. For instance, Volunteered Geographic Information sources like OpenStreetMap (OSM) collect label information from individuals in a volunteer capacity and make it freely available [2]. Another approach is to design automatic labeling tools, such as AutoGeoLabel [3], to generate labels rapidly for RS images from high-quality data sources, e.g., LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) data. Additionally, various land use land cover products, including Google's Dynamic World [4], ESA's World Cover [5], and Esri's Land Cover [6], offer rich information for EO. However, these label sources often result in unreliable labels, such as noisy labels due to insufficient human annotation. For example, [7] documents human uncertainty in the classification of local climate zones. As reported in [8], deep learning models are known for their large number of parameters and capability of learning complex functions, yet vulnerability to label noise. This also applies to segmentation tasks [9]. Therefore, these readily available labels require special considerations when applied to real-world scenarios. Beyond model training, noisy labels may significantly affect the evaluation of methodologies as well [10].

While learning from noisy labels (LNL) has been extensively studied for image classification tasks, few approaches have been developed for image segmentation tasks. Existing LNL methods for segmentation tasks mainly borrow ideas from LNL for classification and semi-supervised segmentation methods. In classification tasks, the entire image is treated as a single sample unit and can be considered to have approximately similar levels of uncertainty. Thus, random flipping can be used to simulate label noise for classification tasks. In contrast, the sample unit in segmentation tasks is a pixel, and neighboring pixels are interconnected through spatial dependencies [13]. As a result, pixels located near boundaries are more difficult to define. From this perspective, we can classify pixel-wise label noise into two categories: assignment noise and shape noise. Assignment noise occurs when objects are labeled incorrectly, while shape noise refers to inexact object delineation caused by phenomena such as coarse annotations. Inaccurate co-registration of image-mask pairs is another common source of label noise, mainly leading to shape noise with misaligned boundaries [14]. Generally, assignment noise incurs more severe damage on model training than shape noise does.

As regards the ideas borrowed from the semi-supervised learning domain, self-training methods are naturally related to the noisy label problem, where pseudo labels generated by the classifier itself inevitably incur some inaccurate assignments [17]. Following this paradigm, [18] - [20] correct possibly wrong labels in the training set by means of high-confidence or low-uncertainty predictions. To make these methods effective, the questions of when and how to correct the labels should be considered. In semi-supervised scenarios, only a small part of the accurately labeled patches is available at the beginning. The training set is gradually expanded via adding pseudo labels as training continues, during which the impact of bad pseudo labels can be offset to some extent by the advantages brought by training size expansion. LNL settings do not confer this advantage since the classifier originally has access to a large number of labels that are not as accurate as expected. Therefore, manually setting the warm-up length as in [19] can easily lead to an early or late start of correction, risking correction effectiveness degradation when model predictions are not reliable enough. Liu et al. [21] propose an adaptive method for label correction initialization in which the training accuracy curve is fit on an exponential function and the change in its gradients is monitored. While promising, this method has a sensitive threshold setting to noise rates, and the fluctuation of accuracy curves makes the detection results unstable. In terms of how to correct, current correction criteria usually take softmax/sigmoid outputs as confidence indicators [20]. The threshold is either predefined by users or flexibly adjusted in an image-wise fashion [19], more or less ignoring the spatial dependencies among pixels. One further possibility is to determine data and model uncertainty, e.g., via Bayesian Neural Networks, for sample selection [22]. Yet a major challenge is the lack of ground truth to evaluate the estimated data uncertainty when developing such methods to address real-world problems.

In this work, we study building footprint identification from aerial imagery to develop a novel methodology to handle, among other types of noise, incomplete label noise, in which a given set of building outlines is known to miss a subset of existing buildings (false negative), but annotated buildings are assumed to have accurate outlines.

Infomédiaire Maroc – Une conférence internationale intitulée « Les États généraux des entreprises et des entrepreneurs citoyens » se tiendra le week-end prochain à Essaouira, à l'initiative du réseau international « Thinkers and Doers ».

Environ 100 leaders internationaux, décideurs, experts, penseurs et intellectuels de renom sont attendus à cette conférence, placée sous le haut patronage du Roi Mohammed VI et du Président français Emmanuel Macron, selon un document officiel.

Organisée en partenariat notamment avec le Groupe OCP, la CDG, et l’Association Essaouira-Mogador, cette conférence servira de plateforme d'échanges de bonnes pratiques. Elle mettra en avant les logiques et processus d'engagement nécessaires pour transformer une entreprise et aligner la dynamique économique avec les attentes sociétales.

La conférence d’Essaouira offrira l’opportunité de collaborer pour dresser un état des lieux de la mutation économique et technologique, opérer un changement positif à l’échelle internationale, et formuler un plaidoyer et des solutions visant à accélérer le mouvement des « entreprises citoyennes », engagées et responsables.

« En accueillant Thinkers and Doers à Essaouira, nous espérons que les dirigeants d’entreprises, les entrepreneurs engagés, les acteurs économiques, ainsi que les responsables politiques, pourront prendre le temps d’échanger et de réfléchir ensemble à cette question fondamentale de la transformation de nos sociétés et à la réponse que nous pouvons apporter aux défis et archaïsmes auxquels nous sommes collectivement confrontés », a déclaré André Azoulay, conseiller du Roi et président-fondateur de l’Association Essaouira-Mogador.

Il a ajouté : « Si les solutions imaginées par vous, les entreprises engagées et les entrepreneurs créatifs, permettent de dessiner de nouvelles perspectives, il est crucial que ce nouvel ordre mondial, revisité et réconcilié avec la modernité des valeurs universelles, soit également pensé et développé au sein de l’entreprise et par les entrepreneurs. »

« C’est pour soutenir et promouvoir cette dynamique du "changement positif" que Dar Souiri ouvre ses portes, et que l’École d’Essaouira accueillera pendant deux jours les 100 personnalités venues d’Europe, d’Afrique, d’Asie, pour s’associer à ces premiers « États Généraux de l’Entrepreneuriat Citoyen », a conclu Azoulay.

La rencontre d'Essaouira fait suite à celles organisées pendant un an à Tunis, Paris, Londres et Dubaï, réunissant entreprises et entrepreneurs lors d’un cycle de conférences internationales intitulé « Follow the Leaders ».

Les travaux de la conférence d’Essaouira seront sanctionnés par l’adoption d’une feuille de route baptisée « Déclaration d’Essaouira », qui sera soumise à l’appréciation des prochains sommets du G20 et de l’Union Africaine (UA).

El número de mujeres asesinadas a manos de sus parejas o exparejas en lo que va de 2019 se ha elevado a 45. La mujer asesinada este lunes por su exmarido en Las Palmas de Gran Canaria es la última víctima confirmada. El agresor la atacó con dos cuchillos en la vivienda en la que trabajaba como empleada de hogar y luego se quitó la vida. Según la estadística oficial, desde el año 2003 ha habido un total de 1.020 mujeres asesinadas.

La mujer asesinada en Las Palmas de Gran Canaria es la víctima número 45 del año, según ha confirmado la Delegación del Gobierno para la Violencia de Género. No había denuncias previas y tanto la víctima como el agresor no tienen descendencia. El año pasado, se registraron 48 asesinatos de mujeres por violencia de género.

En Canarias, este año han muerto siete mujeres a causa de la violencia machista, además de un niño que fue asesinado junto a su madre. También se está investigando un posible noveno caso en La Laguna (Tenerife), donde se encontró el cadáver de una mujer el pasado 1 de septiembre y su expareja, un hombre con varias denuncias por malos tratos a otras mujeres, se suicidó. Canarias se sitúa como la segunda comunidad autónoma con más feminicidios en el ámbito de la pareja, solo superada por Andalucía con nueve asesinatos machistas.

Tras conocer este nuevo caso de violencia machista, el presidente del Gobierno en funciones, Pedro Sánchez, ha exigido que las instituciones utilicen todos sus recursos en la lucha contra esta violencia. Por su parte, el Gobierno de Canarias y otras instituciones han mostrado su más enérgica repulsa y condena ante este feminicidio. También se ha convocado para este martes concentraciones de condena en las sedes del Gobierno de Canarias y la Delegación del Gobierno en las islas.

En un comunicado, la directora del Instituto Canario de Igualdad ha afirmado que "la coeducación permanente es el antídoto para frenar esta lacra social". Es necesario unir esfuerzos y no fracasar en esta lucha.

When it comes to the topic of driverless cars, I am against the idea. While there might be some perks to them, I think the risks are too significant. Driverless cars might hurt us more than help us, and here's why.

Firstly, accidents are a primary concern with any type of car. With driverless cars, there are more potential points of failure than in human-driven vehicles, such as issues with wiring or sensor malfunctions. If an accident is caused by a driverless car, who would be held accountable? As discussed in certain narratives, would it be the owner or the manufacturer? Moreover, traffic laws currently assume that a safe car has a human driver; therefore, several existing laws would need amendments and numerous new ones would have to be enacted.

Another issue is the loss of driving experience if all cars become automated. Many people enjoy learning how to drive but won't have this opportunity if only driverless cars exist. What will individuals do if they ever need to drive and haven't learned how? An electrical malfunction could leave most people stranded since they wouldn't know how to operate their vehicles manually. Additionally, several jobs that rely on drivers—such as taxi drivers, truckers, and pizza delivery personnel—could disappear with widespread adoption of autonomous vehicles.

Furthermore, transitioning entirely to driverless cars could have considerable socioeconomic impacts. It would leave many individuals jobless and require extensive retraining for those working alongside these new technologies. The cost to produce these advanced vehicles is another factor; manufacturing them would likely entail spending hundreds of millions of dollars that might be better allocated elsewhere.

Driving has been an essential skill ever since Ford introduced the Model T. Since then, the use of cars has only become more prevalent in society. People rely on cars for commuting, traveling on vacations, and chauffeuring others. While driving, individuals could engage in more productive activities, such as preparing for their destination, completing homework, or enjoying leisure activities. The legitimacy of developing driverless cars is underscored by the daily routines people navigate and the convenience these cars could provide, once the necessary laws are enacted to make them a reality.

Today, people's lives are filled with demanding tasks, such as work, school, and extracurricular activities. A significant amount of time is spent driving, time that could be allocated to more productive pursuits. Advances in sensor technology, as discussed, have paved the way for the possibility of cars that can nearly drive themselves. As companies like Tesla, Audi, Mercedes-Benz, and Nissan make strides toward creating fully autonomous vehicles, individuals still face numerous challenges, aside from driving, that technology could alleviate. Hence, the development of self-driving technology, which could reduce the driver's workload, would be highly beneficial to society, freeing up valuable time.

In the article "Making Mona Lisa Smile," it is claimed that the Mona Lisa appears predominantly happy in the painting, a conclusion reached through computer software analysis.

I don't believe this is very valuable for students because while some individuals might genuinely feel happy, the computer could interpret their emotions differently due to how they control their expressions.

The computer aims to determine your mood by scanning facial expressions; however, people have different ways of reacting based on how they feel.

What if the computer identifies you as mostly happy when, in reality, you are angry, sad, or confused? Although such technology might be applicable in certain situations, I fail to see its usefulness in a school setting. 

Most of the time, young kids and teenagers will express how they feel and explain why without prompting.

I don’t see the need for a machine in schools to determine someone’s mood or help students recognize their own emotions. 

The computer could easily be deceived into believing your mood is opposite to what you actually feel. If it relies on facial movements alone, one could simply smile at it and make it think they're happy. While there may be instances where this technology works effectively, is there any proof that people can't create different expressions to confuse or trick it into perceiving an inaccurate emotional state?

Although I don't find this kind of technology particularly beneficial for personal life assessment purposes right now—I do find its concept intriguing nonetheless.

The software appears accurate when analyzing genuine emotional expressions—or perhaps neutral faces—but there's nothing guaranteeing its reliability should someone alter their expression or behave differently than usual.

I believe that as computing technology advances over time—and once methods are developed ensuring computers can no longer easily fall prey—to misleading cues—this tool has potential value across various applications eventually someday being accurate enough much more consistently useful future contexts overall.

Topic models have been a fundamental and prevalent research area for decades, aiming to discover latent topics from a document collection and infer the topic distributions of documents (Churchill and Singh, 2022). Various topic modeling scenarios have been explored, such as hierarchical, dynamic, and cross-lingual topic modeling (Griffiths et al., 2003; Blei and Lafferty, 2006; Mimno et al., 2009). Current topic models can be categorized into two types: conventional topic models employing probabilistic graphical models (Blei et al., 2003) or non-negative matrix factorization (Lee and Seung, 2000), and recently popular neural topic models (Zhao et al., 2021a). Due to their effectiveness and interpretability, topic models have inspired various downstream tasks and applications (Boyd-Graber et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2023c). However, despite these significant achievements, quick utilization and fair comparisons of various topic models remain a formidable challenge. The challenge lies in their unsystematic model implementations as well as inconsistent dataset and evaluation settings across papers, even within a paper (Hoyle et al., 2021).

In response to this challenge, several topic modeling toolkits have been proposed, but they commonly exhibit incompleteness. Early toolkits (McCallum, 2002; Qiang et al., 2020; Lisena et al., 2020) often lack necessary steps in the modeling lifecycle (e.g., pre-processing and comprehensive evaluations), critical topic modeling scenarios, or recent neural topic models. The latest toolkit is OCTIS (Terragni et al., 2021), which integrates more features, but it solely focuses on basic and hierarchical topic modeling and lacks the latest neural topic models (It only includes two neural topic models after 2018). These issues pose hurdles to the evaluations, comparisons, applications, and developments of topic models.

To address these issues, in this paper, we propose TopMost, a Topic Modeling System Toolkit. In contrast to existing toolkits, TopMost comprehensively includes the most popular topic modeling scenarios: basic, hierarchical, dynamic, and cross-lingual topic modeling. It covers the entire lifecycle of these scenarios with datasets, pre-processing, model training, testing, and evaluations.

敬鹏大火造成消防员不幸罹难，对于外界质疑消防署「状况外」的声音，消防署副署长江济人日前强调没有救错栋，但误指出移工罹难位置，引发关注。消防署长陈文龙昨日对此回应，表示如果从结果来看，移工确实不在三厂，但由于当时信息不完整，因此不认同「救错栋」的说法。

陈文龙进一步解释，关于救错栋导致消防员不幸殉职的说法，罹难的消防员在晚上9点半到达现场后，发现三厂的5楼有冒烟，并传出有人受困，所以首先从三厂1楼进入。随后才接获通报称移工住在二厂4楼。由于二、三厂是连通的，并且最初传出的讯息是三厂有人受困，所以不能说这是错误的决定。

陈文龙强调，由于初期信息不清楚，「没有救错栋的问题，因为三厂确实有起火，也传出有人受困」。尽管从结果来看，移工确实不在三厂，但考虑到消防员初期信息不完整且三厂已经起火冒烟，因此他们的行动有其理由。

至于江济人提到移工是在敬鹏三厂罹难，但被发现的地点是二厂，陈文龙为江济人解释，称可能是他一时口误导致错误。

A shopper at 7-Eleven captured a disturbing moment when a man launched into a racist tirade, blaming Asian people for the coronavirus. Sungmin Kwon, an Asian man, recorded and shared the terrifying incident on Facebook. He reported that while he was purchasing snacks at the 7-Eleven in New York City, a man in the queue behind him began a "disgusting racist rant," accusing Asians of causing the pandemic, describing them as filthy, and claiming they did not belong in the country.

In his Facebook post, Mr. Kwon explained, "I called him out on his nonsense, and he approached me." The man then attempted to kick Mr. Kwon while hurling racial slurs. Mr. Kwon continued, "That's when I took my phone out, and he began to assault me. He did push me to the ground, but it didn't hurt."

The 23-year-old expressed his frustration, noting that racism was becoming increasingly exhausting and lamenting that such incidents still occur. Mr. Kwon also shared a photo of the man's license plate.

The New York City Police Department's Hate Crimes Task Force is investigating the incident. Detective Sophia Mason reported that officers responded to a 911 call regarding a dispute at the Queens convenience store around 8:30 p.m. on Saturday. She informed NBC News that a 23-year-old man told police an unknown individual had yelled at and shoved him, causing alarm and annoyance. The suspect, who made "anti-Asian and derogatory remarks," fled in a grey Jeep Cherokee, and no injuries were reported.

In one of the videos, the man can be heard yelling, "Get the f*** outta here." Mr. Kwon also recorded himself, stating, "He just assaulted me. This man had just assaulted me." He later told the Daily News that he felt it was crucial to speak up and demonstrate that such behavior would not be tolerated.

Racism against Asian Americans has surged during the coronavirus pandemic, with the Anti-Defamation League recording numerous incidents. Recently, an Asian woman exercising in a California park was subjected to racist abuse by a woman who threatened violence and shouted, "Go back to whatever f**king Asian country you came from." This disturbing incident, captured last Wednesday, went viral after the woman's friend posted it on Twitter.

Have you ever struggled to read and understand a person's emotions, finding it impossible to truly grasp what they're feeling? Designed to decode emotions using "some new computer software that can recognize human emotions" (1), FACS has already been tested on the Mona Lisa painting by Leonardo da Vinci, providing insights into the emotions she might be expressing. This system has the potential to be incredibly valuable in classrooms, aiding the study of human anatomy and psychology, and helping individuals to better understand one another.

Emotions are often incredibly difficult to interpret, especially when they're coming from others. Typically, unless one has a close personal relationship, it can be challenging to determine how a person is feeling based solely on their appearance. Understanding emotions, however, can be beneficial, fostering better communication, enabling timely support, and preventing misunderstandings. A program like FACS, which provides the most accurate emotional percentages, can be a crucial tool. For instance, the analysis of the Mona Lisa revealed she is "83 percent happy, 9 percent disgusted, 6 percent fearful, and 2 percent angry" (1).

(Washington) Une loi interdisant l’immense majorité des avortements est entrée en vigueur au Texas mercredi, sans intervention de la Cour suprême des États-Unis pour faire respecter un droit qu’elle a elle-même reconnu il y a près de 50 ans. Charlotte PLANTIVE Agence France-Presse.

La loi, signée en mai par le gouverneur républicain Greg Abbott, interdit d’interrompre toute grossesse une fois que les battements de cœur de l’embryon sont détectés, soit après environ six semaines de grossesse, alors que la plupart des femmes ne savent même pas qu’elles sont enceintes. Elle ne prévoit pas d’exception en cas de viol ou d’inceste, mais seulement si la santé de la femme enceinte est en danger. Plus de 85 % des avortements pratiqués jusqu’ici au Texas ont lieu après six semaines de grossesse, selon les organisations de planification familiale de l’État qui ont fait état mercredi de leur profond désarroi.

La haute juridiction, que l’ancien président Donald Trump a solidement ancrée dans le conservatisme, n’avait toujours pas tranché dans la soirée, deux jours après avoir été saisie en urgence par les détracteurs du texte. Sans attendre sa décision, le président Joe Biden a fustigé une loi « radicale », aux dispositions « honteuses », et a promis de « protéger » le droit des femmes à avorter.

« Je me suis réveillée triste, inquiète, sonnée », a déclaré lors d’un point-presse Amy Hagstrom Miller, directrice de l’organisation Whole Woman’s Health qui gère quatre cliniques au Texas. L’une d’elles, à Fort Worth, a réalisé des avortements jusqu’à 23 h 56 mardi soir, mais a dû s’interrompre alors qu’il restait des patientes dans la salle d’attente. « Les médecins pleuraient et me demandaient : qu’est-ce qu’on peut faire pour elles ? », a raconté Mme Miller. « Les patientes sont effrayées, confuses, en colère », a ajouté Vanessa Rodriguez qui supervise les centres d’appels de Planned Parenthood au Texas. « On fait de notre mieux pour essayer de les aider… on cherche des rendez-vous au Colorado, dans l’Oklahoma, le Kansas, le Nouveau-Mexique… »

À l’inverse, les opposants à l’avortement jubilaient. « C’est un moment historique dans le combat pour protéger les femmes et les enfants », a commenté Marjorie Dannenfelser, présidente du groupe SBA List, tandis que l’organisation LifeNews tweetait un photomontage d’un fœtus le pouce levé, en signe de satisfaction.

Avant le Texas, douze États ont légiféré pour interdire les avortements dès que les battements de cœur de l’embryon sont perceptibles. Ces lois ont toutes été invalidées en justice, parce qu’elles violent la jurisprudence de la Cour suprême qui a reconnu un droit à avorter tant que le fœtus n’est pas viable, soit vers 22 semaines de grossesse. Mais le Texas a formulé sa loi différemment : il ne revient pas aux autorités de faire respecter la mesure, mais « exclusivement » aux citoyens, encouragés à porter plainte au civil contre les organisations ou les personnes qui aideraient les femmes à avorter. Le texte prévoit que ces citoyens perçoivent au moins 10 000 dollars de « dédommagement » en cas de condamnation. Les détracteurs du texte y voient une « prime » à la délation, mais ses défenseurs ont déjà mis en place des formulaires sur l’internet pour déposer des « informations anonymes ».

Pour des raisons de procédure, ce dispositif rend plus difficile l’intervention des tribunaux fédéraux qui ont refusé jusqu’ici de se saisir des recours contre la loi. Les défenseurs du droit à avorter ont donc dû s’adresser directement à la Cour suprême. Mais, contrairement à ses habitudes, la haute juridiction n’est pas intervenue à temps pour empêcher le texte d’entrer en vigueur. Cela envoie « un message fort », a commenté l’historienne du droit à l’avortement Mary Ziegler sur le site Scotusblog.

I can't imagine a future where everyone is driving driverless cars. Can you? Imagine a world that only involves computers. No teachers, no parents to tell us what is best, no books and writing. Using computers for everything isn't always the answer. It is important to also use old-fashioned ways to determine emotion no matter how much someone dislikes it. Using the Facial Action Coding System, we aren't able to figure out others' emotions by ourselves. It assumes someone's emotions just by the way someone is showing their face, and it can have technical difficulties that may provide false information.

To begin, it is important that we use context clues to determine someone's emotions. Using a computer app can take away from someone trying to figure out facial emotions by themselves. Sometimes, it can be useful to figure out expressions by ourselves. This can help us with everyday people. We can't carry a computer everywhere we go and use it to determine if someone is sad, angry, happy, excited, etc. If we figure out these expressions by ourselves, we can apply those skills when it is necessary. Moreover, some people hide their emotions, causing us to believe something that may be false. For example, some depressed people hide the fact that they are very upset and hide it with a smile. If the Facial Action Coding System were to try and tell the emotions of that person smiling, it would give a completely different set of emotions than the person is really feeling. There isn't much someone can do to fix the fact that misjudged faces can lead to false emotions. 

Lastly, computer programs aren't always correct. They can have technical difficulties and give out the wrong information. Programs can mess up and give the total opposite of what is being presented.

Just because someone is disabled doesn't mean they should be deprived of the opportunity to drive a car. Autonomous cars could potentially prevent many accidents and minimize damage to property and individuals.

Autonomous cars are capable of driving themselves, only requiring human intervention in specific situations, such as in construction zones or near accidents. Otherwise, a person with a disability could operate the vehicle. Autonomous cars have the potential to make transportation easier and safer for everyone.

Los Mossos d'Esquadra están investigando el asesinato de una niña de 13 años que fue encontrada muerta en su casa en Mataró (Barcelona). También están intentando localizar al hermano de la víctima en un caso en el que todas las posibilidades están siendo consideradas.

Según informaron fuentes cercanas al caso, el cuerpo de la chica fue descubierto poco después de las 22:00 horas del domingo en un apartamento de esta localidad catalana. La madre, quien según algunos vecinos se encontraba fuera del país, alertó a unos amigos después de no poder comunicarse con sus hijos durante varios días.

Los Mossos d'Esquadra han iniciado una investigación para determinar las circunstancias de la muerte de la menor, ya que por el momento no se descarta ninguna teoría, de acuerdo con las fuentes.

Después de que la madre, de origen ruso, contactara a sus amigos, estos acudieron al apartamento de la familia. Tras lograr entrar, encontraron el cuerpo de la chica con una herida causada por un arma blanca.

La jueza encargada del juzgado de instrucción número 3 de Mataró se presentó en el domicilio junto con un equipo judicial, un abogado de la administración, el fiscal y el forense para llevar a cabo el levantamiento del cadáver, según informó el Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Cataluña (TSJC).

La jueza ha ordenado que el caso se mantenga en secreto hasta que se obtengan los resultados de la autopsia y se determine la causa exacta de la muerte.

En el marco de la investigación para esclarecer las circunstancias de este incidente, los Mossos d'Esquadra han tomado declaración a varios vecinos y están tratando de localizar al hermano de la víctima, quien también es menor de edad, según las fuentes.

Vietnamese national Doan Thi Huong, charged with the murder of Kim Jong Nam, was escorted by police as she arrived at a Sepang court in Malaysia on April 13, 2017. (Lai Seng Sin—Reuters)

Two young women accused of murdering Kim Jong Un's estranged half-brother are set to face trial on October 2 in a Malaysian court. This case, laden with international intrigue, pits these two migrants, who assert their innocence, against an unyielding legal system.

Doan Thi Huong, 29, from Vietnam, and Siti Aisyah, 25, from Indonesia, entered the High Court in Shah Alam, near Kuala Lumpur, with heads bowed. They wore flak jackets over brightly colored Malay dresses, which flickered through a wall of armed guards as they were ushered inside. If convicted, they likely face the death penalty.

"We will ensure that the rights of the accused are respected and that they receive a fair trial," Huong's lawyer, Hisyam Teh Poh Teik, assured reporters outside the courthouse. Both suspects intend to contest the charges, although the judge declined to hear a plea on Friday. "They are definitely not guilty," Huong's counsel maintained.

The women were apprehended after being captured on security cameras, appearing to smear a substance on Kim Jong Nam's face at Kuala Lumpur International Airport. The defendants, both migrant workers in the capital, claim they were tricked into the act. Their lawyers argue that the women believed they were participating in a harmless television prank, offered around $100 to douse a stranger with what they thought was baby oil or water.

Kim died about 20 minutes later, after exposure to VX nerve agent, an internationally banned chemical weapon. The women had already left the scene, while four suspected accomplices—all North Korean—disappeared into the bustling terminal and caught flights abroad. Three other suspects took refuge in the North Korean embassy before being sent back to Pyongyang in exchange for nine Malaysian nationals held as diplomatic hostages.

One North Korean man was briefly detained by Malaysian authorities but was released due to insufficient evidence. Only Aisyah and Huong currently face trial for what is being considered a bold, public political assassination. Aisyah's lawyers have called the case a "trial by ambush," claiming the prosecution withheld evidence that could bolster their defense.

Some of this evidence was handed to the defense on Friday morning, but lawyers for both suspects claim they have not received all requested materials, including some remaining CCTV footage and statements from the three North Korean men who have since returned home.

"We believe the main suspects are the four North Koreans who fled the country... All we have is evidence that [the two women] had no intent — they thought it was a prank," said Aisyah's lawyer, Gooi Soon Seng.

South Korean officials quickly blamed Pyongyang for Kim's death, while Malaysian authorities have been more cautious. North Korea denied involvement and initially claimed the victim was not related to its Supreme Leader. Kim Jong Nam, a son of North Korea's former leader Kim Jong Il and his favored mistress, had been living in Macau under the assumed identity of Kim Chol, the name on the falsified passport he held at his death.

The North Korean government has previously ordered killings, including of family members. Experts suggest Kim Jong Un may have had reasons to eliminate his sibling, while the motives for Aisyah and Huong appear less clear.

"She is just an ordinary girl from Indonesia," Seng said of his client Aisyah, who worked as a masseuse at a hotel spa in Kuala Lumpur, spoke little beyond her native language, and rarely traveled. "I cannot say how confident I am, but I believe that justice will prevail in the end."

La Corte Suprema de Justicia de Colombia condenó hoy al senador oficialista Bernardo Miguel Elías a seis años y ocho meses de prisión por los delitos de cohecho y tráfico de influencias. La constructora brasileña Odebrecht realizó los pagos de sobornos, según informaron fuentes judiciales.

La condena es anticipada debido a que el senador aún tiene pendientes procesos por los delitos de concierto para delinquir y lavado de activos, que están siendo evaluados por la Corte. Esta instancia decidirá si cierra los casos o llama a juicio a Elías, según confirmaron fuentes del alto tribunal a Efe.

El senador admitió el pasado 13 de diciembre ante la Corte Suprema de Justicia su culpabilidad por los delitos de cohecho y tráfico de influencias, al haber favorecido una modificación del contrato de la carretera Ocaña-Gamarra, en el noreste del país, a favor de la multinacional brasileña en el marco del proyecto Ruta del Sol II.

Aunque el exlegislador aceptó los dos delitos mencionados, se declaró inocente de concierto para delinquir y lavado de activos.

La abogada defensora Silvia Rugeles explicó el pasado mes de diciembre que Elías aceptó su responsabilidad en el tráfico de influencias debido a que permitió que Eleuberto Martorelli, expresidente de Odebrecht en Colombia, y Luis Fernando Andrade, exdirector de la Agencia Nacional de Infraestructura (ANI), se reunieran en su casa para discutir la construcción y ejecución del contrato de la carretera Ocaña-Gamarra.

Elías se encuentra detenido desde el pasado mes de agosto en la cárcel La Picota de Bogotá.

Este contrato fue otorgado a Odebrecht por el Instituto Nacional de Concesiones (Inco) en 2012, luego de que la constructora brasileña pagara sobornos por valor de 6,5 millones de dólares a varios funcionarios del Gobierno, incluido el exviceministro de transporte Gabriel García Morales.

García Morales, arrestado en enero del año pasado, fue condenado a seis años de prisión por haber recibido 6,5 millones de dólares de Odebrecht.
