With the increasing prevalence of graph data across numerous domains, solving graph-related tasks using machine learning has gained significant attention. Many traditionally NP-hard tasks, such as Traveling Salesman Optimization (Xing & Tu, 2020), Graph Edit Distance computation (Wang et al., 2021), and Maximum Common Subgraph detection (Bai et al., 2021), have recently been approached through learning-based methods. These methods utilize search strategies to explore the large solution space and employ reinforcement learning (RL) to develop effective search policies from training data, thus eliminating the need for hand-crafted heuristics commonly used by traditional solvers. This learning-to-search paradigm (Bai et al., 2021) also allows for training RL agents without requiring any pre-solved instances for supervision.

One particularly challenging task, Subgraph Matching, involves detecting all occurrences of a small query graph within a much larger target graph and has significant applications, including graph database search (Lee et al., 2012), knowledge graph query (Kim et al., 2015), biomedical analysis (Zhang et al., 2009), social group finding (Ma et al., 2018), and quantum circuit design (Jiang et al., 2021). A concrete example of Subgraph Matching application is protein complex search in protein-protein interaction networks, which is used to determine if interactions within a protein complex of one species exist in others (Bonnici et al., 2013). Despite the task's importance, the design of a neural network architecture under the RL-guided search framework for Subgraph Matching remains unclear.

Current Subgraph Matching algorithms, due to the NP-hard nature of the problem, rely on backtracking search, with several techniques developed to reduce the extensive search space (Sun & Luo, 2020; Kim et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2022). However, these techniques, primarily driven by heuristics, often fail to find any solution on large target graphs within a reasonable time, a phenomenon we refer to as solution sparsity, even though they may perform well on small graph pairs. This solution sparsity necessitates the development of models with sufficient capacity, able to run efficiently, and, when used, RL, to address the lack of reward, which we term as reward sparsity, for the RL agent (Silver et al., 2017).

Osteoporosis is a common skeletal disorder characterized by decreased bone mineral density (BMD) and bone strength deterioration, leading to an increased risk of fragility fracture. All types of fragility fractures affect the elderly with multiple morbidities, reduced life quality, increased dependence, and mortality. FRAX is a clinical tool for assessing bone fracture risks by integrating clinical risk factors and BMD. While some clinical risk factors such as age, gender, and body mass index can be obtained from electronic medical records, the current gold standard to measure BMD is dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA). However, due to the limited availability of DEXA devices, especially in developing countries, osteoporosis is often under-diagnosed and under-treated. Therefore, alternative lower-cost BMD evaluation protocols and methods using more accessible medical imaging examinations, e.g., X-ray plain films, are highly desirable.

Previous methods aiming to use imaging obtained for other indications to estimate BMD or classify osteoporosis have been proposed. La stratégie du cluster protection s'aligne sur la stratégie de protection de l'Équipe Humanitaire Pays adoptée en avril 2018 et renforce le plan de réponse humanitaire 2017-2019, qui comprend deux objectifs stratégiques directement liés à la protection. Les pôles humanitaires (Nord-Est, Centre-Est, Sud-Est et la région du Kasaï) élaborent des plans d'actions régionaux en cohérence avec cette stratégie. Ces plans régionaux visent à prioriser les interventions de protection et les activités de coordination, en lien avec les plans opérationnels semestriels adoptés dans chaque pôle. Un plan de travail est élaboré par le cluster protection national pour définir les priorités en termes de coordination afin de soutenir la mise en œuvre de ces plans d'actions régionaux et de la stratégie nationale du cluster protection ; il inclut également les actions du cluster protection prévues dans le plan d'action de la stratégie de protection de l'Équipe Humanitaire Pays.

Stratégie de Protection de l'Équipe Humanitaire Pays
Priorité 1 : Les populations sont protégées par des actions de prévention ou de réduction de la violence, ainsi que par l'atténuation des risques en matière de protection.
Priorité 2 : Les populations touchées par les violences, en particulier les plus vulnérables, bénéficient d'un accès à une assistance multisectorielle adaptée et appropriée.
Priorité 3 : L'environnement protecteur est renforcé pour garantir leurs droits et réduire leur exposition aux crises et aux conflits.

En los tiempos acelerados en que vivimos, el aburrimiento tiene mala prensa. Hay que estar entretenido, ocupado. Sin embargo, los especialistas aseguran que las horas vacías permiten y estimulan la imaginación y la creatividad.

La actual cuarentena forzosa agudiza esta problemática, porque las actividades habituales de una familia -trabajo, escuela- están suspendidas o limitadas y hay que estar cara a cara todo el día. Como nunca, se plantea el desafío del qué hacer y cómo llenar las horas libres.

Lo que sigue es el contenido de una nota publicada en este mismo medio hace una “eternidad”: en 2013, cuando nadie podía prever esta pandemia y mucho menos que millones en el mundo se verían obligados a confinarse en sus casas. Pero los conceptos vertidos por los expertos entonces consultados son más pertinentes que nunca y se ven incluso actualizados por la excepcionalidad de las circunstancias que vivimos. Pasen y lean.

### Por qué es bueno que su hijo se aburra

“Es bueno aburrirse en la escuela”, afirma, provocador, Jean-Paul Brighelli, docente y ensayista francés, autor de varios textos críticos sobre la educación. “Nada más formador que el aburrimiento, siempre que no sea constante”, sostiene. “El aburrimiento es la vía libre a la imaginación. ¿Qué hace el alumno que se aburre? Divaga. Una sana ocupación”.

¿Quién no ha conocido el aburrimiento siendo niño? Por no tener con quién o a qué jugar. A veces, uno hasta se ha aburrido en compañía de otros niños o de sus hermanos. Nada más viejo y clásico que el “me aburro” infantil. Lo que ha cambiado, dicen los especialistas, es la forma en que los adultos perciben y reaccionan ante ese aburrimiento. Vivimos en una sociedad hiperactiva y competitiva, en la cual no hay tiempo que perder. La productividad es un valor y el ocio está mal visto. No tener nada que hacer significa una pérdida condenable de tiempo.

Y esa concepción se aplica a los niños. Es frecuente que, pese a la doble escolaridad, se los llene de actividades en el tiempo libre que les queda. Esta excesiva programación de su jornada impide que los chicos aprendan a organizar por sí mismos su tiempo libre, a decidir qué hacer y a pensar sus propios juegos. De este modo, cuando más adelante se vean confrontados a tiempos muertos, no sabrán qué hacer. Aprender a jugar solos les hace desarrollar una autonomía que les permitirá funcionar sin tener que depender constantemente de terceros.

Over the past few decades, there has been a significant increase in efforts to develop efficient uncertainty quantification approaches for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with random inputs. Typically, these random inputs arise from a lack of precise measurements or a limited understanding of realistic model parameters, such as permeability coefficients in diffusion problems and refraction coefficients in acoustic problems [38, 11, 12].

Designing a surrogate model or calculating statistics, such as the mean and variance, for PDEs with random inputs, is of great interest, particularly when the inputs are high-dimensional. The Monte Carlo method (MCM) and its variants are among the direct methods for computing these statistics [5, 13]. In MCM, numerous sample points of the random inputs are generated based on their probability density functions, and for each sample, the corresponding deterministic problem is solved using existing numerical methods. The statistics of the stochastic solution are then estimated by aggregating the results of these deterministic solutions. While the Monte Carlo method is straightforward to implement, it converges slowly, typically requiring a large number of sample points, and does not provide a surrogate model, which limits its applications.

To enhance efficiency, the stochastic collocation method (SCM) and the stochastic Galerkin method (SGM) have been developed, which are generally more efficient for solving PDEs with moderate-dimensional random inputs [37, 38, 39, 40, 32, 41].

Thomas Wayne Capenhurst, a Dixon man, pleaded guilty in a Sacramento federal court on Monday to the conspiracy to bomb his brother's home in Suisun City in 2018. According to U.S. Attorney McGregor W. Scott, Capenhurst pleaded guilty to both the conspiracy charge and malicious use of explosive materials.

Court documents revealed that Capenhurst had offered $10,000 each to co-defendant Robert McGraw and another man to place pipe bombs at his brother's Blue Jay Drive residence. On February 17, 2018, McGraw placed a pipe bomb on the front porch of the home and ignited the fuse before fleeing, resulting in an explosion that caused damage to the property.

Fortunately, despite the family of five being present in the house at the time of the incident, no injuries were reported. The investigation into this case was conducted by various law enforcement agencies, including the Suisun City Police Department, U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, and the FBI's Solano County Violent Crimes Task Force, among others.

Robert McGraw is set for a status conference on October 5, while Thomas Wayne Capenhurst is scheduled for sentencing on January 4 by U.S. District Judge Kimberley J. Mueller. Capenhurst could face a prison sentence of five to 20 years and a $250,000 fine for malicious use of explosive materials, as well as a maximum penalty of five years in prison and a $250,000 fine for conspiracy. Assistant U.S. Attorney Ross Pearson is leading the prosecution in this case.

The doors are stuck. There is no light. Where there were houses before, now there is only mine. I have done everything to get out, but no more. I am alone, and I cannot take it anymore. I lay in the dark, scrolling through Reddit one last time, hoping someone figured it out. But there are no new comments. I am alone, and I have decided to escape the only way I can. I turn my music on, lay in my bed, and reach for the pills. I put as many as I can swallow in my mouth and take a drink. I repeat this process three more times, and then I wait.

Laying there, feeling the pills drain my life, I suddenly hear a noise. Struggling, I lift my head, and a face swims into view in front of me. I gasp, my eyes widen, and it's harder to stay awake, but I fight with all my strength. More faces come into view, and I can hear them now. "Where did she get the pills, dammit?" "I don't know, she has been acting out for days, clawing the windows and doors, screaming, and crying out." "Well, go get the doctor now!"

I feel myself beginning to slip away as my mind tries to grasp what is happening. I can feel their hands on me, fighting for my life with machines, pumping my stomach. But I know it is too late.

All I can really recall before it happened is the incessant ticking of the clock in my room. My roommate keeps it there, and I swear it's just to annoy me—"

"Listen, son, that's not what I'm interested in. What I want to know is how you managed to kill an entire mafia hit squad with this."

The detective held up a plastic bag containing a slightly oversized, cast-iron button. It had a bit of blood on it, but otherwise, it looked quite ordinary.

"Sir, I'm getting to that. Anyway, this clock is incredibly irritating. I get up from my bed, and suddenly, I'm... somewhere else."

"Son, are you high?"

"No, really, I swear, that's what happened. Now, let me finish."

The detective sighed, then nodded, signaling me to continue.

"So, I find myself in this massive, museum-like building, with all these incredible, legendary weapons. You know, like Excalibur, King Arthur, and stuff, right?

Javier's cut my hair for the last eight years, and in all that time we've never been closer. He's invested himself in me, in my situation, to a degree that I think he would fly from if he understood how I felt about him. There's his hand on my shoulder, his eyes dark and tender as he leans over me and we plot together, two men seeking to subvert cruel genetics. It feels like a lie, sometimes, the anxiety around him that I mask as fear of going bald.

We've progressed in stages as my hairline began to recede, as the first pink glints of my scalp began to shine through. Javier's fluffed his fingers through my hair, blow-dried it, done his best to give it volume. He's trimmed down the back and sides to half an inch from the skin, to reduce the contrast to my thinning crown. He's used sprays, creams, anything to make the remaining follicles darker, give them more volume. And when even his best efforts began to fail, he's shaved my head down to the contours of my scalp, making it seem intentional.

I wonder sometimes what he sees when he looks at me. A challenge? A tragedy? The natural limitations of his chosen profession? Or a desperate balding fool, returning to his barber's chair again and again and again in an attempt to pretend that the world isn't falling out from under him. He looks up and sees me, raises an eyebrow at my naked scalp, and grins at me in the mirror, signalling at me to wait. I am curiously calm. A stage of our relationship has ended. A new one will begin.

"I wasn't expecting you back," he teases afterwards, brushing the stray hairs from his chair. He gestures me forwards. "I tried, Eddie, I tried the best I could." He hangs his head melodramatically. "I figured I failed you." "Never," I tell him, easing into the familiar seat, rubbing a hand across my stubble. "Just a shave. That's all." "You used to shave yourself," he remarks, flicking open his straight razor and running across his leather strap. The sound of it scraping across the leather is soothing. Brisk, steady sweeps of the shiny silver blade. It's mesmerizing.

The silence builds, becomes heavy, becomes unbearable. I ease open my eyes and see us both in the mirror, my own pink, half-shaven face staring dazedly out at him; him standing over me with his eyebrows furrowed in concentration or anger, his fingers stern and unyielding. I have lied to him by omission these past eight years. I can lie to him no longer. "I love you," I tell him, and he tilts my head backwards and presses his razor to my throat.

Una mujer afirmó haber sido estafada por 40 mil dólares por una empresa de inversión en línea y sostuvo que, solo en Rosario, hay cerca de 400 personas afectadas.

"Te voy a presentar al maestro, al número uno, el tipo que trajo la empresa Trading Waves a Argentina"; así convencieron a Yésica de invertir cerca de 40 mil dólares en una criptomoneda llamada Tronus, una moneda digital creada por la misma empresa que, según la víctima, pone diversas excusas para no pagar las ganancias.

Yésica contó que solo cobraron las ganancias del primer mes, dinero que no llegó a sus manos ya que lo reinvirtieron. "De un momento a otro empezaron a surgir problemas; se culpaban entre ellos por la falta de dinero y decían que habían hackeado las cuentas", indicó en diálogo con El Tres.

"En Trading Waves nos hicieron cambiar nuestros dólares por una moneda que generaron ellos, Tronus, que es propia de su empresa", explicó, y añadió: "Tenemos millones de Tronus, pero el dinero no aparece".

La mujer aseguró que a nivel mundial son cerca de 90 mil las personas que invirtieron en esta empresa, de las cuales unas 400 son de Rosario. "Dicen que dentro de treinta días van a habilitar un exchange para cambiar los Tronus por Bitcoins, que podremos vender para recibir nuestro dinero", comentó, pero aseguró que los plazos se han prorrogado varias veces sin obtener respuestas positivas.

Trading Waves es una empresa de brokers en línea, un comercio en línea que permite invertir en criptomonedas y promete ganancias diarias del 3%.

El sitio Brokers Recomendados, que se dedica a analizar brokers en línea, señala que Trading Waves "es una empresa no regulada, no menciona dónde tiene su base" y "no menciona qué empresa administra la página web".

Algunas víctimas de Rosario ya se han puesto de acuerdo para presentar una denuncia conjunta en la Justicia Federal y también en la embajada de la República Dominicana, donde supuestamente se encuentra la sede central de Trading Waves.

Deep learning has been the foundation of numerous accomplishments in artificial intelligence in recent years, leading to significant advancements in computer vision, reinforcement learning, and natural language processing. Thanks to advancements in techniques like residual connections and batch normalization, training very deep models with thousands of layers on powerful GPU or TPU clusters has become easier. For instance, training a ResNet model on a popular image recognition benchmark with millions of images takes less than ten minutes, while training a powerful BERT model for language understanding takes no more than an hour and a half. Despite the remarkable success of large-scale deep models, the substantial computational complexity and extensive storage requirements pose a significant challenge in deploying them in real-time applications, particularly on devices with limited resources like video surveillance and autonomous driving cars.

To address the challenge of deploying deep models in resource-constrained environments, recent research has primarily focused on developing efficient building blocks for deep models. This includes innovations such as depthwise separable convolution, as seen in models like MobileNets and ShuffleNets.

David sat down at the bar in the ballroom, even though he knew drinking wouldn't help him. Around him, workers buzzed like bees, preparing for the most joyous and wonderful union about to take place. It was supposed to be a day of utmost perfection, but David's head was pounding harder now than when he had woken up six hours ago, two hours late for the groomsman photos his best friend had insisted would not proceed without him.

"Fucking Gatorade," he muttered under his breath. 

"Only got the regular kind, Jack," said an approaching bartender. David hated bartender talk.

Without looking up, he responded, "Whiskey, double, clean." The bartender nodded and swiftly prepared the drink, delivering it quicker than David had anticipated. Normally, choosing to drink was like a fork in the road for David, but today, he saw only one path with many drinks along the way. He would either numb the pain or let it spill out of him in a drunken slur; it was up in the air.

"That'll be 18 buckaroos, buckaroo," the bartender said. David looked at him but said nothing. It was supposed to be an open bar, a gift from the bride's father's grave, courtesy of the trust fund he left her. The thought brought back a sting from the night before.

'What kind of idiot sends a 200-dollar wreath to a headstone?' he thought to himself, pathetically. 'The same kind who spends the night watching the Keira Knightley-Rick scenes from "Love Actually" on a drunken loop,' he answered himself.

David needed a change of subject, but the weed he had smoked before arriving for the photos—hoping to cover up his hangover—was backfiring. Instead of dulling his headache and relaxing him, it had left him swimming in an ocean of tortured thoughts. 'What a poetic motherfucker,' he thought. 'Shakespeare would shit himself.'

The bartender returned just as the whiskey was beginning to take effect. Noticing David's empty glass, he prepared to refill it. "I thought the bar was open... asshole," David said, his anger swirling within him. The bartender, unfazed, replied, "Open for the reception. Do you see a reception going on in here... asshole?" with a slight edge in his voice. 

'He better watch his ass or I'll use that edge to slit his throat,' David thought maliciously.

The wedding felt so small to me. We had been together for eight years, and it was my decision that we do this. I answered the question as honestly as I could. I didn't know I even had it in me to lie. I'd spent all night looking in the mirror, repeating to myself to make sure, "I want this to happen, I need this to happen, my life has brought me here, and I'm happy to go through with it". I don't know why, in the moment, it scarred me. It's like my body knew what my mind didn't. When I said, "I do," I knew I had made a mistake. I told her this and fell silent. I had never lied before this. It was far more painful than I would have thought. I held back the pain. I didn't want her to see it. I couldn't. I felt it start to form, deep down my back. It slowly raised higher and higher, stopping right before my neck.

She used to be my best friend, my other half, my everything. She guided me through life, leading me until she tried to make me take it, until she got me a sullen gift that the doctors called PTSD. She was the part of me that guided the "Transport," making the discussions. We were best friends, intertwined, until the day she became filled with horror, trying to kill me. Now, I am broken without her, shattered by the memories of our once harmonious bond. I pray she'll stop talking, be quiet, be numb. She, who used to care for me, to my mind, is now a stranger, a tormentor, a betrayer, a broken mirror, a shadow.

A clinically feasible and accurate artificial intelligence (AI)-based disease diagnosis model using modern neuroimaging techniques is highly desired for precision medicine. The literature has seen significant advancements in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) for personalized diagnosis, which not only reduces human effort but also enhances our understanding of disease mechanisms. The integration of PET/MR equipment offers a unique opportunity to uncover molecular and anatomical changes in a single scan, making PET/MR research a hot topic in clinical studies. However, current brain studies either utilize anatomical MRI with PET or treat the two modalities as separate sources in AI models, leaving the untapped potential of PET/MR.

This paper presents pioneering research on simultaneous functional PET/MR (sf-PET/MR) for comprehensive characterization of brain metabolic, hemodynamic, and perfusion networks in a single scan for early Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis. It marks a paradigm shift in neuroimaging by concurrently modeling brain connectome and revolutionizing previous AI methodologies by deeply learning from the multifaceted brain connectome at micro and macro levels. While integrating multimodal information with deep learning can leverage deep representations, challenges like hardware accessibility in real clinical settings and increased AI workflow complexity due to modality variations hinder the application of sf-PET/MR in clinical scenarios.

The study aims to develop a clinically feasible AI model for integrating multimodal sf-PET/MR and uni-model diagnosis in common clinical settings. The model needs to balance multimodal accuracy and uni-model flexibility while handling high-dimensional, non-Euclidean, and complementary brain connectome data.

Instead of traditional modality fusion requiring full-modality data during inference, a multimodal MiXture-of-experts Alignment and Reconstruction Model (MX-ARM) is proposed. This model features a modality-detachable architecture that reduces the need for full modality data during inference. The Mixture-of-Experts utilizes a fingerprint-based router to dynamically allocate modality-specific weights for a combination of multi-layer perceptrons, ensuring modality-independent model performance. Additionally, a modal alignment module aligns PET representations with other modalities, while a multimodal reconstruction module improves representation quality. The model is tested on a carefully curated sf-PET/MR dataset for early AD diagnosis.

The contributions of this work include: 1) a pioneering design for multimodal brain connectome modeling in a disease population using simultaneous functional PET/MR; 2) an AI framework trained on multimodal sf-PET/MR but implemented on single modality data with balanced accuracy and clinical flexibility; 3) a fingerprint-based mixture-of-experts adapter for adaptive multimodal learning and uni-modal inferencing; and 4) modules for modality Alignment and Reconstruction to enhance representation quality and diagnostic accuracy.

Le climat politique instable, la baisse inexorable du pouvoir d'achat et l'économie morose de la Tunisie n'encouragent pas ces jeunes élites à rester. En 2011, après la révolution, nombreux étaient ceux qui pensaient que la situation allait s'assainir et que de nouvelles perspectives allaient s'offrir à eux. Mais la désillusion a fait son effet, poussant nos cerveaux, nos élites et même nos décideurs de demain à quitter le pays. Même s'ils sont conscients du problème, les pouvoirs publics semblent immobiles, incapables de faire face à ce fléau. À ce rythme-là, la Tunisie, où tout est à reconstruire, pourrait se vider de ses bâtisseurs.

Dans ce contexte, le président du Conseil de l'ordre des ingénieurs tunisiens, Kamel Sohnoun, a déclaré ce mercredi 27 avril 2021 que « les ingénieurs ont entamé leur protestation depuis 2016. » Il a expliqué que « les ingénieurs sont les seuls à ne pas avoir bénéficié de primes depuis des années, ce qui a poussé plusieurs ingénieurs à émigrer. » Il a précisé que 3 500 ingénieurs quittent la Tunisie chaque année.

L'Ordre des ingénieurs tunisiens (OIT) a récemment appelé, dans un communiqué, tous les ingénieurs des entreprises et des établissements publics à entamer une grève non présentielle ouverte. Les ingénieurs tunisiens, qui ont entamé leur grève après une série de protestations (brassards rouges, sit-in, grève de trois jours et de cinq jours), revendiquent l'application d'un accord avec le gouvernement qui prévoyait la généralisation des primes spécifiques pour en faire bénéficier les ingénieurs de la fonction publique.

L'OIT a également appelé les ingénieurs de la fonction publique à porter des brassards rouges pour soutenir leurs collègues dans les entreprises et les établissements publics, soulignant que la grève ouverte répond aux conditions légales et que l'OIT s'est engagé à défendre ses adhérents par tous les moyens légitimes. Kamel Sahnoun a mis en garde, lors d'une séance d'audition, lundi 26 avril à l'ARP, contre les impacts de la grève des ingénieurs, « si elle continue », sur la formation professionnelle, les entreprises de l'État et sur les systèmes informatiques, actuellement non sécurisés.

The concept of driverless cars is becoming less interesting to some because these vehicles still require human intervention in certain situations. For example, they alert the driver to take control when navigating driveways or dealing with complex traffic scenarios. Moreover, these cars can only navigate themselves on clear roads, which limits their autonomy.

Driverless cars could be particularly beneficial for individuals who lack the physical ability to operate traditional vehicles, such as those without arms or legs. For these people, a car that can assist with tasks like parking might be appealing. However, if a so-called smart car cannot reliably manage traffic and requires frequent manual intervention, it hardly seems more advantageous than using cruise control on a regular vehicle.

I have concerns about the safety of these cars. While I understand the vision behind them, it doesn’t make sense to have a vehicle that can't fully handle all driving tasks independently. If it's smart enough to switch lanes autonomously, shouldn't it also manage more challenging scenarios like navigating through traffic accidents or pulling into driveways? Additionally, even if such technology becomes available for purchase, its likely high cost may restrict ownership primarily to affluent individuals.

I appreciate the idea of self-driving cars and acknowledge their potential impact; however, I'm hesitant about adopting them soon due to uncertainties surrounding their operation and reliance on electronic systems. Perhaps I'm mistaken and they will become one of the greatest automotive innovations ever—potentially generating millions in revenue—but that's just my perspective based on current limitations.

Creak, creak, creak.

The hinges desperately needed oiling. He winced slightly at the noise as he pushed the old swing.

The wind blew softly, tousling the grass and sending a shiver down his spine. He sighed, realizing he had forgotten his coat again.

"Hey, sport, do you remember the first day I brought you here?" he said, continuing to push as a slow smile crossed his face.

"You spent hours running up and down the hills. They hadn't installed the playground back then, but you didn't care. I remember spinning you around, playing hide and seek in the bushes, and that time we even brought water guns."

He sniffed a little, still pushing the swing. The cold was getting to him.

"Of course, once they installed the playground, we spent even more time here. You played with other children then, growing up with those your own age."

His hands shook. Once robust, they now hung weakly. The skin that was once ruddy and rough with callouses was now mottled with age. Yet he continued to push.

"You grew up so fast, but I couldn't stay. Do you remember what I said to you in middle school? I promised I'd be around. I told you that no matter what happened to our family, I would be there in your heart," he looked down at his feet, "Yet I broke that promise, didn't I?"

Eyes that once twinkled with youthful sparkle watered with tears that refused to fall.

"I'm sorry. I'm so sorry for disappearing from your life."

"Dad, what are you doing out here without your coat? It's getting chilly."

"Eh? Really?"

She smiled lovingly and took his hand. "Come on, let's go home."

They walked slowly away, leaving the empty swing to sway in the evening breeze.

My name is Bob Greene, and I am a scientist at NASA. I am discussing the "Face on Mars" with a man who believes it is evidence of an alien artifact. Despite my explanations, he insists that aliens are real and that this feature resembles a human face. I repeatedly explain that the formation is a natural landform known as a butte or mesa. It appears facial because shadows create the illusion of eyes, a nose, and a mouth. 

The man questions how NASA can be sure that the formation is a mesa, implying it's a sign of alien life. I clarify that a mesa is a large rock formation with a flat top, which is exactly how the "face" appears up close. Nonetheless, he remains skeptical. I assure him that the truth will be revealed, and indeed, it is. 

On April 8, 2001, the NASA team, myself included, obtained a clear image of the "face" with the Mars Global Surveyor. The Surveyor, having a perfect, cloudless day, captured a photo that was significantly clearer than the original 1976 Viking photo. 

Many who believed the "face" was an alien artifact eagerly awaited the release of the new image. NASA, eventually, revealed the photo, which, as the evidence confirmed, depicted a mesa. While the image disappointed some, a few, the man I debated, included, suspected a NASA conspiracy to conceal the truth about aliens.

In the article "Making Mona Lisa Smile," the discussion revolves around using technology to interpret students' emotional expressions in classrooms. In my opinion, this is a fantastic idea because it would enable teachers to respond effectively, helping shift students' moods towards happiness. For instance, if a student appears sad, the teacher could address the issue and offer support to make them feel better. Additionally, this technology could identify why students might be bored or confused by analyzing their reactions to specific topics.

The "Facial Action Coding System" has potential applications in preventing bullying too. By detecting emotions such as fear or anger, it could identify situations involving bullies and their victims. The system could intervene by alerting teachers with a loud noise that draws attention to the situation. Upon arrival, teachers could use this technology to assess students' feelings and begin addressing the issue from there.

I find this new technology fascinating because of its potential to solve numerous problems worldwide and prevent many others. It can contribute positively by promoting happiness—after all, "happy person, happy life" is how I see it. However, it's important to acknowledge that not everyone may benefit from this approach; some individuals prefer maintaining a serious demeanor and reserve smiles for genuine moments of joy.

We have an opportunity now with technologies like the "Facial Action Coding System" to tackle negativity effectively. I believe this innovation holds great promise because while humans alone can't solve everything, we can make significant progress with assistance from machines. Facial expressions reveal so much about our emotional world; through unconscious imitation of others' expressions, we connect emotionally.

The angels formed a circle around me, maintaining a cautious distance. With a mere snap of my fingers, I could obliterate every one of them, and they knew it. Once again, I doubled over, struggling to catch a breath that seemed eternally out of reach.

A gentle hand touched my back. "Hey," a melodic voice whispered, "you'll be fine. There's no need to worry."

The archangel Michael stood behind me, offering a practiced smile that betrayed his own uncertainty. Me? A god? I had neither earned nor deserved this power.

I laughed sarcastically. "Yeah, sure, everything's fine. I die, at the age of eighteen, mind you, and arrive here, greeted by a ring of winged humans calling me 'God.'"

Michael shrugged, his bright eyes reflecting a jaded familiarity, as if he had done this a million times. "The Lord works in—"

"If you say 'mysterious ways,' I swear, I will smite you where you stand," I warned, allowing my anger to surface. All my life, I had concealed my anger, playing the part of the nice, calm girl, when, in reality, I was a mess.

台湾捐赠口罩，并由华航陆续运抵欧洲各国。然而，英文名「China Airlines」可能让人误认为是中国籍航空，再次引发改名争议。资深媒体人黄暐瀚指出，在陈水扁前总统时期和2016年蔡英文上台后均曾提及华航改名，如今仍在争议中。他呼吁尝试正名，探索新可能性。

黄暐瀚强调，华航原名即为华航，不应被迫伪装成「China Airlines」。在现今情况下，许多台湾人不愿看到「China」，也担心国际上误解，因此支持将「中华航空」更名为「台湾航空」。他认为，值得尝试，不妨一试。

他指出，口罩上清楚印有「Made in Taiwan」，接收国不太可能混淆。并不是每个人都会前往停机坪领取口罩，所以飞机标有「China」并不会造成大误会。如果真的不喜欢，政府也可以选择其他航空公司，无需一定请华航运送。

他认为，既然讨论华航改名已有多年，不如抓住机会试一试。不愿再见到长期纠缠不清的「华航正名运动」再次发生。最终，黄暐瀚强调，应该勇敢尝试新可能性，即使结果不尽如人意，也不至于无法承受。

À l'occasion des 20 ans des prix Galian, qui célèbrent l'excellence journalistique au Burkina Faso, Sidwaya a souhaité en savoir plus sur la composition des jurys. La Directrice générale des médias (DGM), Alima Fartha/Ouédraogo, a détaillé les principes guidant la formation de ces jurys.

Institués depuis 1997, les prix Galian récompensent chaque année les meilleures œuvres journalistiques du paysage médiatique burkinabè, tant au sein des organes de presse étatiques que privés. Pour marquer les 20 ans des Galian, nous avons rencontré Alima Fartha/Ouédraogo, Directrice générale des médias, afin d'éclaircir le processus de sélection des jurys au fil des ans. Selon Mme Ouédraogo, les prix Galian visent à magnifier l'excellence journalistique au niveau national.

Cette exigence se reflète dans les critères de sélection des jurys. «Tous les acteurs impliqués dans l'organisation de ce concours s'accordent sur l'importance d'avoir un jury professionnel, doté de l'expérience et des compétences nécessaires pour évaluer une œuvre journalistique. L'expérience et le professionnalisme sont les critères principaux pour choisir les membres des jurys. De plus, la plupart d'entre eux ont été ou sont toujours enseignants en journalisme», a expliqué la DGM.

Trois jurys se chargent généralement de l'évaluation des œuvres selon les catégories. Le plus récent est celui de la presse en ligne, participatif depuis 2013. «Ce jury compte dix membres, dont des professionnels des TIC, des administrateurs de sites web et des informaticiens. Nous avons inclus des journalistes spécialistes en informatique et des administrateurs de sites web. Nous avons voulu inclure dans ce jury des personnes qui ne sont pas forcément journalistes, mais qui peuvent évaluer certains aspects de la presse en ligne», a précisé Alima Fartha/Ouédraogo.

«Le jury est renouvelé à 40% chaque année.»

Le second jury concerne les langues nationales telles que le mooré, le dioula, le fulfuldé et le gulmancema. Les productions dans ces langues ont commencé à participer aux Galian en 2009. Ce jury, également composé de dix membres, inclut au moins deux auditeurs de chaque langue, qui sont des journalistes et des spécialistes en langues nationales. «Pour ce jury, nous sollicitons l'expertise de notre institution spécialisée dans les langues, notamment la direction générale de l'éducation non formelle, qui offre un regard sur le plan sémantique et autres aspects», a-t-elle ajouté.

Le troisième jury concerne la langue française et regroupe la presse écrite, la radiodiffusion sonore et télévisuelle. Ce jury comprend également dix membres et intègre des spécialistes en radio, télévision et presse écrite. Selon la DGM, c'est la catégorie qui reçoit le plus de candidatures. 

«Le jury est constitué de manière à ce que chaque œuvre soit évaluée dans sa globalité par tous les membres. Par exemple, l'œil du spécialiste en presse écrite doit apporter un complément à l'évaluation. Ce jury inclut des représentants de la presse privée, publique, et des membres de l'administration publique et privée», a-t-elle précisé. Une autre particularité des jurys est leur renouvellement à 40% à chaque édition des prix Galian.

90% des œuvres proviennent des médias publics.

Qu'en est-il des critiques adressées au jury? Pour la DGM, il n'y a pas lieu de douter de la crédibilité du jury des Galian. «Le jury doit être impartial pour préserver sa crédibilité. Tous les médias, publics et privés, ainsi que d'autres spécialistes, sont représentés dans chaque jury. Il est donc impossible de manipuler les résultats pour favoriser quelqu'un de non méritant», a-t-elle clarifié.

Selon elle, les personnes chargées d'évaluer les œuvres travaillent objectivement, selon des critères bien définis, et ne se soucient pas de l'identité des auteurs des productions. Qu'est-ce qui explique que de nombreux lauréats proviennent des médias publics? Alima Fartha/Ouédraogo a précisé que 90% des œuvres soumises à la compétition émanent des médias publics.

I have lived a thousand times, or perhaps more accurately, I have died a thousand times and awoken each time in a new place, a new life, distinguished only by the memories of the hundreds or thousands of deaths that preceded it. I've lost count, and each time, I wear a new face.

Initially, I thought I might be mad, or perhaps I was dreaming my deaths so vividly that they seemed real. I attempted, on several occasions, to legitimize these deaths, at least to myself, but each time, I was met with the inescapable truth. With each death, my appearance changed, making it impossible to prove my experiences to others, who, unsurprisingly, accused me of madness or, at the very least, a perverse, stalker-like obsession.

Estados Unidos.- No solo la humanidad está en riesgo por los virus, pues como si de una película se tratara, la NASA alertó sobre un asteroide gigantesco que se acerca a la Tierra y que es “potencialmente peligroso”.

Se trata del asteroide Atón 163348 (2002 NN4), del tamaño de 'siete estadios de fútbol', según advirtió la NASA. Este asteroide se prevé que se aproximará al planeta, de acuerdo al Centro para los Estudios de Objetos Próximos a la Tierra (CNEOS), un organismo que forma parte de la NASA.

El informe señala que el objeto se acercará, como mínimo, a unos 5 millones de kilómetros (0,034 unidades astronómicas) y a una velocidad de 11,146 kilómetros por hora. Su tamaño es de unos 735 metros de diámetro. 

La información sobre el asteroide se encuentra en el sitio web del CNEOS de la NASA, que monitorea los acercamientos cercanos a la Tierra. Según los datos, se espera que varios otros objetos vuelen a través del espacio cerca de la Tierra esta semana.

“Todo lo que tenemos que hacer es cambiar su velocidad un poco más rápido o un poco más lento para que cuando cruce la órbita de la Tierra, cruce delante o detrás de nosotros", dijo el Dr. Lori Glaze, director de ciencia planetaria de la NASA.

¿Realmente representa un peligro? A pesar de la clasificación de la NASA de ‘potencialmente peligroso’, las probabilidades de que impacte con la Tierra son casi nulas. Los científicos llegaron a esta conclusión basándose en que el asteroide se aproxima a unos 5 millones de kilómetros de la Tierra, una distancia que es considerada muy cercana en relación a otras medidas astronómicas.

The old knight stood before the garden, where a crescent shaped pond would force those taking a stroll to deviate around either side, tempting them down any of the other paths between the hedges, down less-observed divisions of the compass. The hedges were overgrown, and the paths were barely visible now. Still, it was clear how magnificent the maze had been, once upon a time. The old knight's face seemed remorseful, his eyes distant, as if remembering those times.

The way to the old knight's position was a singular path, paralleled on both sides by rose bushes. The roses grew in all different colours, on the same bush, from indigo to yellow and all the spectrum in between. Upon closer inspection, one would find that the petals were made of glass.

In the pond two koi fish danced around each other. One of them was gold, and the other black. The water would flicker with their colors as the sun glinted off their scales, and every time it did so, a little rumble would send the water on the surface trembling, and sparks would fly out from the middle of the two fish.

From down the path to the knight's left, a rabbit emerged from underneath the hedgerow. Cautiously, sniffing the air, it determined that the maze was deserted and came out further. It was very fluffy and grey. The old knight stayed still, and the rabbit did not notice him. The rabbit foraged silently, its head buried in the grass.

A hawk cast a shadow across the shoulders of the old knight, before diving to snatch the rabbit. The rabbit, all of a sudden surprised by the bird's dive, exploded into the white seeds of a dandelion, which were then scattered into the wind by the hawk's talons. The old knight stayed motionless, hands upon the pommel of his greatsword, his chin resting upon them. The hawk rose from its swoop, confused and distracted, and so did not see the spiderweb stretched between the hedges. Its beak pierced the very middle, and the threads closed around her like a tattered cloak. She thrashed weakly as dozens of spiders revealed themselves amongst the leaves, shaking their spears and cheering.

Music could be heard, simple tones that echoed over the maze, drifting closer and receding. The knight waited, and the music revealed itself as a dragonfly flew around one corner. It flew so fast, and turned at right angles, and each time it did so, a tone rang out. A long time ago, a musical troop had tried to navigate the maze by mapping the tones to certain corners, as they had discovered a pattern. Nevertheless, they failed.

It was said that in the middle of the maze was a fountain, or a tree. No one could decide which, as it was arguably both. The water spread upwards from the base, twisting and bubbling, until it rained down again in drips like a heavy rain, or the branches of a willow tree. No one knew what drinking from the fountain would do, not even the knight.

The maze had other tricks, almost as many as it had stories. There were butterflies that set your clothes on fire if they landed on you. There were some passages that never ended. There were no exits besides that at which the old knight stood. The old knight would not enter the maze. Instead, he stood and watched, his stone face aged from the sun, wind, and moss.

Astrophysics, particularly solar physics, is an observational science where experimental conditions cannot be altered, only observed. Therefore, the primary method of learning is by comparing observations with advanced theoretical models. These models are refined until they explain the observations, shaping our understanding of the universe based on available data.

Until the late 20th century, the limited data could be easily stored in conventional media like notebooks or small computing centers. Researchers heavily relied on informed generative models, incorporating theoretical advancements and inductive biases to generalize conclusions. Generative models describe the joint probability p(x, y), where x represents observations and y denotes model parameters.

Solar physics is now transitioning into the big data era, characterized by vast amounts of data that surpass current computing capabilities. The challenge lies in storing and accessing this data efficiently, as exemplified by the Solar Dynamics Observatory dataset requiring 6.5 TB of storage. The increase in data volume poses a technological hurdle that remains partially unresolved.

Access to large datasets in solar physics has fueled the rise of machine learning (ML) as a means to extract valuable insights efficiently. ML methods are categorized into supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, each with distinct roots and applications within the field. The advent of big data spurred the ML revolution, necessitating the development of algorithms and hardware to handle large datasets effectively.

Supervised and unsupervised learning in ML are deeply rooted in statistical learning, focused on model fitting and understanding data structures. Reinforcement learning, on the other hand, draws from control theory and has potential applications in observational planning and adaptive optics within solar physics. Functional optimization is a common thread across all three classes of ML, contributing to advancements in the field.

In summary, the integration of machine learning in solar physics facilitates the direct extraction of insights from vast datasets, revolutionizing data analysis and accelerating scientific discoveries. The intersection of advanced theoretical modeling and machine learning is propelling the field towards a deeper comprehension of the universe's complexities.

Movie enthusiasts know that Hollywood releases its most prestigious films every December, just before the Oscar nomination deadline. Similarly, Broadway sees its most notable openings in the spring, right before the Tony nominations. This year's season is exceptionally crowded, with 18 shows—half of them musicals—debuting in March and April.

Last season was dominated by "Hamilton," which everyone anticipated would win the Tony for Best Musical. However, Barry Weissler, the producer of "Waitress," remained unfazed. 

"They were a massive hit, and some of our investors even begged us to delay for a season," Weissler says. "'Go to Chicago,' one of them suggested, 'and then come back.'"

Yet Weissler already had a theater and a cast in place, and despite not winning a single Tony Award, "Waitress" proved to be a profitable success. While Weissler took a gamble, other shows opted to sit out last season and are now opening before this spring's Tony deadline.

Scott Mallalieu, owner of GreatWhiteWay.com, a company that sells Broadway tickets to groups, believes that timing can dictate a show's success on Broadway. 

"The general rule of thumb is you don't want to open a show in the fall, because even with good reviews, it can be overshadowed by all the fresh new productions in the spring," he explains.

However, Mallalieu thinks this year might be an exception, as three hit musicals already opened in the fall: "Dear Evan Hansen," "Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812," and "A Bronx Tale."

According to Jeremy Gerard, a theater critic for Deadline with four decades of experience covering Broadway, this leaves limited room for new shows to make an impact. He notes that many of these new productions are opening one day after another, vying for a portion of a relatively small audience.

"The producers know there's going to be a bloodbath," Gerard says. "The total size of the Broadway audience isn't highly flexible, and in fact, the numbers are decreasing. The grosses are going up due to insane ticket prices, led by 'Hamilton' with its $849 top ticket. So, the grosses are skewed, but the actual audience numbers are declining."

Nevertheless, in an industry where one in four Broadway shows fails, hope is ever-present, and producers employ various strategies to make their shows stand out. Sometimes, they hire a star, like Bette Midler in "Hello Dolly!" or adapt a popular movie, like "Groundhog Day" or "Amélie."

Yet some musicals, like last fall's "Dear Evan Hansen," manage to succeed without such strategies. This could also be true for this spring's "Come From Away," an original Canadian musical set in Newfoundland after September 11, 2001, when American airports were closed, and locals hosted 7,000 stranded passengers. Sue Frost, the lead producer of "Come From Away," acknowledges the risk.

"It was a title that no one understood; it was an ensemble piece with no stars, and people might label it 'the 9/11 musical'—so it was like three strikes!" Frost remarks.

We are living in a world where vast amounts of data hold the power to revolutionize industries and shape the future of manufacturing. Datasets play a pivotal role in virtually every field within today's digital world, enabling data-driven decision-making. In the manufacturing industry, datasets assume a critical position, offering invaluable insights to enhance product quality, optimize production processes, streamline supply chains, and achieve heightened operational efficiencies.

While certain generic datasets, such as YCB Videos, MVTech AD, and Dex-Net 2.0, have been employed for training models in semantic segmentation, classification, and localization, their limitations become apparent in terms of restricted object variety and the absence of real-world manufacturing context. Consequently, our research proposes the creation of an extensive, high-fidelity dataset encompassing a range of 3D objects commonly employed within the manufacturing industry.

The process of annotating 6D poses in datasets for robotic grasping and manipulation represents a labor-intensive endeavor, surpassing the challenges encountered in 2D image labeling. To mitigate this challenge, a viable solution lies in the utilization of synthetic data, which offers meticulously annotated samples at a low cost for training pose estimation models. However, the substantial disparities between synthetic (source) and real (target) models result in suboptimal performance. To bridge this gap, a promising approach emerges, combining domain randomization and photo-realistic synthetic data, aiming to address the domain shift between the source and target domains.

As illustrated in Fig. 1, we discretize the captured 3D object, acquired using a high-resolution camera, into descriptive components, comprising texture, material, shape, and inertial dynamics. This process is facilitated by a customized neural network known as Disc-Net, which accepts RGBD data and CAD models of the object of interest as inputs, enabling the extraction of desired object features. The proposed Disc-Net architecture incorporates two distinct neural network components: style extraction, encompassing texture and material, while the other focuses on shape and inertial parameters.

In our study, we adopt the real-sim-real transfer method as a means of domain adaptation to overcome sensor noise and realism issues. The resulting synthetic annotated dataset is then utilized for training various pose estimation networks, including PoseCNN, PVNet, and DOPE, and assessing their performance within real-world settings, thereby providing a benchmark for evaluating the realism and effectiveness of the generated dataset for sim2real transfer.

I believe driving should be in the hands of humans along with the assistance of a machine. Semi-autonomous cars can help us get to a hospital if we are sick or injured and are unable to drive. If a parent needs to take care of a child in the backseat, she can reach back and take care of the child without having to worry about the road as well. These systems can also teach people how to drive behind the wheel; and if there is a problem, the car can take control and keep others safe as well as the driver. Kids that are working to get their license could have more experience driving alone since the system in the car is there to help in case of a problem.

Having autonomous care can enable us to do different things while driving. With the extra control over the car, we can make the roads safer while we multi-task on the road. But that won't completely destroy the purpose of needing a license to drive because people will still need to know how to drive since the car is not always in full control. In conclusion, fully automated cars may not be the best thing due to their inability to judge and react to situations. Semi-autonomous vehicles can assist us in the vehicle, but can still be controlled with our quick reactions in case of a problem. Instead of giving all control to the machine, the driver and the car should work together to preserve the safety of themselves and others around them.

Interactive 3D segmentation using radiance fields has garnered significant attention from researchers, thanks to its potential applications in various domains such as scene manipulation, automatic labeling, and virtual reality. Previous methods primarily involved translating 2D visual features into 3D space by training feature fields to mimic multi-view 2D features extracted by self-supervised visual models. The resulting 3D feature similarities are then used to determine whether two points belong to the same object. While these approaches are fast due to their simple segmentation pipeline, the segmentation granularity may be coarse as they lack a mechanism for parsing the embedded information in the features, like a segmentation decoder.

In contrast, another approach proposes lifting the 2D segmentation foundation model to 3D by directly projecting multi-view fine-grained 2D segmentation results onto 3D mask grids. While this method can provide precise segmentation results, its significant time overhead limits interactivity due to multiple executions of the foundation model and volume rendering, making it impractical for complex scenes with multiple objects needing segmentation.

The above discussion highlights the current challenge faced by existing paradigms in balancing efficiency and accuracy, identifying two key factors hindering the performance of existing methods. First, the use of implicit radiance fields in previous approaches impedes efficient segmentation, requiring traversal of 3D space to identify a 3D object. Second, while employing a 2D segmentation decoder yields high segmentation quality, it results in lower efficiency.

To address these challenges, we propose a new approach building on the recent advancements in radiance fields, particularly leveraging 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) for high-quality and real-time rendering. By representing the 3D scene with a set of 3D colored Gaussians, 3DGS acts as a point cloud, offering explicit 3D prior and enabling efficient rendering, making it ideal for segmentation tasks.

Building on 3DGS, we introduce Segment Any 3D GAussians (SAGA) by distilling the fine-grained segmentation ability of a 2D segmentation foundation model into 3D Gaussians. This novel strategy allows for fine-grained 3D segmentation without the need for multiple forwarding of the 2D segmentation model during inference. The distillation process involves training 3D features for Gaussians based on automatically extracted masks with the Segment Anything Model (SAM). In inference, a set of queries is generated with input prompts to efficiently retrieve the expected Gaussians through feature matching.

SAGA achieves fine-grained 3D segmentation in milliseconds and supports various prompt types such as points, scribbles, and masks. Evaluation on existing benchmarks demonstrates that SAGA's segmentation quality is comparable to the previous state-of-the-art.

As the first interactive segmentation approach using 3D Gaussians, SAGA is versatile, accommodating various prompt types. Our evaluation on existing benchmarks shows that SAGA performs on par with the state-of-the-art, with training of Gaussian features typically concluding within 5-10 minutes. Subsequently, segmentation of most target objects can be completed in milliseconds, achieving nearly 1000× acceleration.

Finding a parking spot in busy city streets can be a frustrating experience due to limited parking spaces. To address this issue, we present a smart parking system that uses Arduino, an open-source microcontroller platform. Our system aims to optimize parking by monitoring the availability of parking spaces in real-time and providing valuable information to drivers.

The system consists of sensors installed in each parking slot, which detect the presence of vehicles. These sensors are connected to an Arduino microcontroller, which processes the sensor data and determines whether a parking space is occupied or vacant. The status of each parking space is then displayed on a screen, allowing drivers to quickly identify available spots.

To further manage parking efficiently, the system includes a barrier controlled by a motor. The barrier opens and closes based on the availability of parking spaces. When all the spots are taken, the barrier restricts entry to prevent unnecessary traffic congestion within the parking area.

For real-time monitoring and management, the Arduino system is equipped with wireless communication modules. This allows the system to transmit parking occupancy data to a central server or a mobile application. Drivers can access this information remotely, making it easier for them to find available parking spaces.

The benefits of this smart parking system are significant. Drivers experience reduced search time, making their parking experience more convenient. Authorities, on the other hand, can efficiently manage parking resources, enforce regulations effectively, and gather valuable data for future planning.

Tomorrow was supposed to be the day I became a man and got my own set of wheels.

I awoke abruptly to my alarm at 6:01 a.m.—my worst enemy. But something was wrong. The house was dark, and there were no celebratory scents of birthday bacon wafting through the air. What on earth was going on?

I slipped on my pants and made my way downstairs. Dad was sitting nervously in his chair, fidgeting with whatever was nearby. Mom was there too, barely glancing at me.

"Sit down, son," my father said, clearing his throat. "Your mother and I have something we've been hiding from you. All parents do it. We needed to ensure you had a normal life before anything happened."

Puzzled, I met my father's gaze. I glanced at Mom, who emitted a small squeak as she quickly looked away. "Well? What is it? Am I adopted? Because I promise I—"

"Hush, boy. I was there the day you were born. I was the first human to touch you. It was my plan. You see, I'm a healer. When I touch someone, I feel their pain. I can hear it, and I absorb it. I've had this ability since I was your age."

"Me too," Mom squeaked. "I can comprehend force on a visual level. I see gravity, friction, air resistance—you name it. It's like a heat map. With it comes comprehension: equations, variables, all floating around in one beautiful image of science."

This explained the puzzled stares Mom often had, as if her mind was an instant blank canvas. Dad's kisses always did make me feel better. How on earth had they managed to keep this a secret?

"As required by law, you will be picked up at your birth time, about four hours from now, and taken to the Facility. There, you will learn about your power as it manifests, and they will teach you how to control it," Dad said.

"What if no power presents itself?"

Have you ever wanted to explore or learn more about other planets? In "The Challenge of Exploring Venus," the author suggests that studying Venus is a worthy pursuit despite the dangers it presents. Venus, a nearby planet, holds valuable intel that we need to understand. Is the data and research we could gather from this mysterious planet worth the risk? The author argues that it is indeed worth the risks involved.

Venus presents extreme conditions with its temperatures soaring above 800 degrees Fahrenheit and an atmosphere comprised of 97% carbon dioxide along with highly acidic and corrosive sulfuric acid. These factors pose significant challenges even for unmanned ships, which have only managed to last a few hours upon landing due to these hostile conditions.

One may wonder why we persist in our attempts to study Venus when our ships can't even survive there for a day. The answer lies in what we stand to gain: valuable insights into both planetary science and space travel. Scientists theorize that long ago, Venus was much like Earth—possibly harboring bodies of water like oceans and lakes, as well as trees and other life forms. Evidence such as rocky sediments featuring valleys, mountains, and craters supports this intriguing hypothesis about its past habitability.

Despite these formidable challenges, advancements in technology provide hope for future explorations. Researchers believe they can utilize more resilient materials alongside robust computer systems reminiscent of those from the 1800s and early 1900s—systems operating on gears rather than delicate electronics—to build sturdier spacecraft capable of withstanding Venus's harsh environment. Tests conducted in controlled chambers mimicking these conditions have shown promising results with materials enduring up to three weeks.

In light of these developments, should we shy away from pursuing answers on Venus?

**Title: The Debate on Driverless Cars**

The concept of driverless cars has sparked significant debate, with tech visionaries like Google cofounder Sergey Brin advocating for their use in public transportation and taxi systems. Brin envisions driverless cars as a revolutionary approach to modern transportation, promising to use half the fuel of today's taxis while offering more flexibility than a bus. However, the safety and practicality of these vehicles remain contentious.

**Safety Concerns and Challenges**

Critics argue that driverless cars pose safety hazards and, therefore, shouldn't be allowed on the road. One significant concern is the potential for malfunctions. If a driverless car experiences a technical issue while in motion, it could endanger the passengers and other road users. The current discourse lacks clarity on how these cars would handle situations like accidents or mechanical damage. This absence of a human driver, capable of making quick, intelligent, and perceptual judgments, underscores the argument that driverless cars, as of now, cannot replicate the "smartness and physical view and skills as a human do."

**Potential Benefits and Safety Features**

On the other hand, driverless cars could offer unprecedented convenience, allowing humans to relax, eat, or check a text message while on the road. These cars, equipped with advanced sensors, could potentially detect and mitigate dangers, including out-of-control skids and rollovers, by accelerating and, if necessary, stopping the car.

Achieving stable and robust locomotion on legged systems is a challenging control task due to underactuation, power limitations, and ground impacts. In this work, we aim to improve existing approaches by synthesizing robust reference trajectories. Two main approaches that have proven successful include generating stable reference trajectories and modifying these behaviors online using regulators, as well as determining the desired behavior of the robot in real time using online planning via model predictive control or reinforcement learning.

Our approach for generating robust walking gaits builds upon the Hybrid Zero Dynamics (HZD) method. The HZD framework encodes walking via nontrivial periodic orbits and directly accounts for discrete impact events. One advantage of this approach is that the stability of the walking can be analyzed using the method of Poincaré sections for systems with impulse effects. However, synthesizing and controlling these periodic orbits can be challenging due to computational expense and noisy timing of impact events in real-world systems.

There exists previous work towards generating robust limit cycles; however, these methods can be computationally expensive and do not scale easily to high-dimensional systems. The goal of this work is to develop a method of generating robust limit cycles that is scalable to high-dimensional systems, such as the 18 degree-of-freedom Atalante lower-body exoskeleton. Our approach improves the robustness of nominal reference trajectories by evaluating the extended saltation matrix directly in the gait generation framework, demonstrated in simulation and on hardware for the 7-DOF AMBER-3M planar biped and the 18-DOF Atalante lower-body exoskeleton.

This paper proposes a robust HZD framework that leverages saltation matrices to synthesize robust nominal walking trajectories. Saltation matrices are first-order approximations of a system's sensitivity to discrete events and have been recently demonstrated for state estimation in hybrid systems and hybrid event shaping. The proposed framework includes the induced norm of the extended saltation matrix in the HZD optimization cost function, leading to stable periodic walking gaits with robust behavior in the real world, even for high-dimensional systems.

大陸結婚率創下2008年以來的10年新低。 大陸官方最近公布一項數據顯示，近年結婚率創下2008年以來的新低。作為結婚「主力」的年輕人，特別是90後，是什麼原因，讓他們不結婚了？

近日公布的「2018年民政事業發展統計公報」讓不少人長吁短歎，2018年，依法辦理結婚登記1013.9萬對，比上年下降4.6%，結婚率為7.3，比上年降低0.4個千分點。這一數據創下2008年以來的新低。

根據民政部近11年的相關統計數據，結婚率自2008年的8.27，逐年攀升至2013年的9.9，之後逐年下降，降至2018年的7.3。民政部報告顯示，2018年結婚登記人口年齡分佈情況中，20至24歲有435.6萬人，25至29歲有736.2萬人，遠遠高出其他年齡段，而他們都是90後。

日前，年齡最小的「90後」都已逐步步入適婚年齡，成為結婚的「主力軍」。不過，作為正值婚姻和生育黃金年齡的90後，婚姻情況參差不齊：有的人已經是兩個孩子的父母，有的結婚又再離婚，有的則堅定抱著「不婚」的主意。

許君雅（化名）是一位在上海做銷售的姑娘，標準的「90後」，談起婚姻，她的態度是堅定的「不婚不育主義」。

她說：「不管是社會還是個人的影響，讓某個個體選擇了不婚，這都是他自己的選擇，應該理解和尊重。結婚和不結婚只是選擇了不同的生活方式，沒有對錯。」

談起婚姻的想法，許君雅認為，現在物質生活條件已經很好了，更多人都開始追求精神層次。人們對於婚姻的看法也在改變，以前很多人為了結婚而結婚，現在很多人慢慢不再把結婚看做是必須要完成人生使命的任務，或者說不會為了結婚而隨便找個人將就。

另一方面，現代城市的生活成本很高，結婚生子很可能會帶來很多難以承受的負擔，無論是經濟還是對家庭的責任，不結婚或許也是一種逃避。

她認為，當前社會很多現象，包括出軌、家庭矛盾升級等各種事件頻出，也造成了人們對於婚姻的恐懼和不信任。

目前，許君雅把重心更多放到了工作上，但她並不認為，單身與工作投入有直接的關係。

Ren Jianxin, Chairman of China National Chemical Corp, arrived at the headquarters of the Swiss agrochemicals maker Syngenta in Basel, Switzerland, on February 3, 2016. (REUTERS/Arnd Wiegmann)

HONG KONG—China Inc. will continue acquiring foreign companies with strategic value, despite efforts to control significant capital outflows. ChemChina's acquisition of Syngenta, listed as SYNN.VX, exemplifies this trend.

State-owned ChemChina agreed on Wednesday to a $43 billion bid for the Swiss seeds and pesticides group. This marks the largest overseas deal by a Chinese firm and is equivalent, by itself, to one-third of all foreign acquisitions by Chinese companies last year. 

The landmark acquisition occurs amid record-high M&A activity and as China grapples with reversing currency outflows that undermine its yuan currency and deplete foreign exchange reserves. However, bankers and industry experts anticipate more deals, as Beijing aims for a strategic long-term shift from low-value manufacturing to high-growth production.

Syngenta represents a prime example, as the acquisition will grant China immediate global leadership in the high-tech GMO segment of the agricultural sector. "In the medium to long term, we will see more M&A activity as China aims to become more globally relevant," said Oliver Barron, senior China analyst at China-focused investment bank NSBO. He noted that yuan policy and concerns over outflows might slow M&A activity in the next few months compared to last year.

"Some Chinese companies have faced restrictions in purchasing foreign exchange (FX). Against such a backdrop, the Syngenta acquisition is a strategic priority with support from the top," Barron added.

**'GOING OUT'**

China's 'Going Out' strategy has been in place for several years as Beijing seeks to build global champions. According to Thomson Reuters data, China's foreign acquisitions last year totaled $116 billion, with ChemChina's purchase of Pirelli [PIRELR.UL] topping the list, set against $700 billion of currency outflows during the same period.

I am walking alone on my way home from work. It's dark, or at least, it will be soon. I can smell the rain coming. I try to walk a little faster to beat the storm, but to no avail. Drip. Drip. Drip. And then I'm drenched in rain. I don't mind so much; I'll be home in five minutes. It's almost refreshing, anyway.

But then it happens. The sky turns black, save for a mangled white slash—a blink of lightning. Its gnarled, ugly shape is followed by an angry roar of thunder, threatening me, targeting me. I'm terrified. A scream escapes me; I didn't mean to let it. I whimper, and suddenly, I am no longer a working woman on her way home from work but a child again, longing for the safety of my bedroom.

I close my eyes and walk faster, faster, as fast as I can, praying that the next flash will come after I'm hidden under the safety of my blankets at home. At home, at home, I plead silently, please stop until I get home…

But I am lashed at again by an unforgiving sky—a clap; the sky is giddy with my fear. Another scream escapes me. I just want to make it home.

With the numerous advances that car companies are making, there is no doubt that driverless cars are on their way to America's roadways. The author of this article presents some compelling arguments supporting driverless cars, but they also make points that lead me to oppose them. I have not seen enough evidence to prove their safety.

Currently, we find comfort in knowing there is a human in charge when we see a large SUV speeding down the road, hopefully paying attention to the driving task at hand. I doubt a computer could consistently make all the necessary logical decisions for safe travel. Let's consider interstate driving as an example: quick decision-making is essential when reacting to unexpected maneuvers or deciding when to overtake another vehicle. These are decisions computers might struggle with.

Looking at it from a legal perspective, the author discusses some legal issues in paragraph nine and poses a crucial question: "If the technology fails and someone is injured, who is at fault – The driver or the manufacturer?" Logically speaking, I believe fault lies with the manufacturer since it's their system controlling the vehicle and not the driver directly. Therefore, if their system fails, they should be held responsible for any resulting failures.

In conclusion, there isn't enough conclusive evidence demonstrating these cars' safety for public use. Without such proof of safety, it would be unwise to introduce them onto our roads. Moreover, manufacturers may not be prepared for shouldering responsibility if their systems malfunction. Perhaps as new advancements emerge and additional evidence surfaces my concerns may diminish; however; currently I firmly oppose introducing driverless cars into our communities.

Have you ever experienced that feeling of eager anticipation, where you simply cannot wait for something to happen? That's exactly how I feel about getting my driver's license. Having a license opens up a world of opportunities beyond just sitting at home. Personally, I don't think I would enjoy driverless cars, simply because I love driving too much, but I can see why older people might appreciate them.

Trust would be a significant factor in getting into a driverless car and allowing it to transport you at high speeds. At this point in my life, I find driving to be exhilarating, and I can't quite grasp why some people don't share this enthusiasm. The idea of being in control of a vehicle, capable of taking you almost anywhere in the world, given the time and resources, is thrilling. If driverless cars became a reality, we might not have to worry as much about speeding, or about older drivers moving too slowly.

I, however, would be too anxious in a driverless car, despite the impressive advancements in technology. I can imagine a plethora of things going wrong, such as the car veering off the road, a power outage, or the vehicle accelerating when it should be slowing down.

Le président Donald Trump affirme une fois de plus que les États-Unis ont un déficit commercial face au Canada, même si les agences de son propre gouvernement témoignent plutôt d'un excédent. La nuance est importante. Si les tarifs et les autres mesures protectionnistes qu'il envisage provoquent une guerre commerciale, les entreprises américaines de services qui compétitionnent sur la scène internationale pourraient faire l'objet de représailles, au même titre que les usines et les fermes qui veulent écouler leurs biens à l'étranger.

TRUMP: «Nous avons un déficit commercial avec le Canada, comme avec pratiquement tous les pays (parfois énormes). Le P.M. Justin Trudeau du Canada, un très bon gars, n'aime pas dire que le Canada a un excédent avec les États-Unis (il négocie), mais ils en ont un... ils en ont presque tous un... et c'est comme ça que je sais!» (Twitter)

SARAH HUCKABEE SANDERS, porte-parole de la Maison-Blanche: «En 2017 nous avions un déficit commercial de 17,5 milliards $ US. En janvier 2018 nous avions un déficit de 3,63 milliards $ US. Tous deux reflètent les échanges de marchandises. C'est exactement ce à quoi faisait référence le président.» (Twitter)

Les faits révèlent que la décision de M. Trump de n'utiliser que certains chiffres signifie qu'il présente un portrait déformé de la situation. L'excédent commercial des États-Unis avec le Canada s'est chiffré l'an dernier à 2,8 milliards $ US, selon le Census Bureau, la même agence gouvernementale que celle qui rapporte le déficit dans les échanges de biens évoqué par Mme Sanders. Ce déficit a toutefois été effacé par le surplus généré par les multitudes de services qui traversent la frontière, dans des secteurs comme le voyage, la finance, les transports et la propriété intellectuelle.

Lors d'un événement mercredi, M. Trump a candidement avoué avoir affirmé à M. Trudeau que les États-Unis avaient un déficit commercial avec le Canada, même s'il n'en savait absolument rien.
