La junte birmane resserre son étau judiciaire autour d’Aung San Suu Kyi, renversée en février, en l'inculpant pour « fraude électorale » lors des élections législatives de 2020, remportées haut la main par son parti. La prix Nobel de la paix, assignée à résidence depuis plus de neuf mois, va être poursuivie pour « fraude électorale », a rapporté mardi le journal Global New Light of Myanmar, contrôlé par le régime, sans donner plus de détails. Quinze autres responsables, dont l’ex-président Win Myint, également arrêté lors du coup d’État du 1er février, vont être poursuivis pour la même infraction.

La junte justifie son action en affirmant avoir découvert plus de 11 millions d’irrégularités lors des élections de novembre 2020, remportées massivement par la Ligue nationale pour la démocratie (LND) d’Aung San Suu Kyi. Cependant, personne n'avait été inculpé pour ces irrégularités jusqu'à présent. Les observateurs internationaux avaient alors qualifié ce scrutin de « globalement libre et équitable ».

Le chef de la junte, Min Aung Hlaing, a menacé de dissoudre la LND, principale force d’opposition du pays, et a annoncé l'organisation de nouvelles élections d'ici août 2023. Selon Richard Horsey de l’International Crisis Group, « La junte utilise des allégations fallacieuses de fraude électorale pour justifier son coup d’État ». Il est convaincu que le soutien massif des électeurs envers Aung San Suu Kyi et son parti rendra les verdicts de culpabilité peu convaincants.

Cette nouvelle inculpation de l’ex-dirigeante intervient après la libération du journaliste américain Danny Fenster, gracié après plus de six mois de détention à la veille d'un procès où il risquait la perpétuité pour terrorisme. Il a été expulsé vers les États-Unis. Aung San Suu Kyi, 76 ans, est jugée depuis juin pour plusieurs infractions, dont l'importation illégale de talkies-walkies, la sédition, la corruption et l'incitation aux troubles publics, en plus d'avoir enfreint les règles de restrictions liées au Covid-19. Un premier verdict est attendu le 14 décembre dans cette affaire.

Les médias sont exclus de son procès qui se déroule à huis clos devant un tribunal spécial à Naypyidaw, la capitale. La junte a également interdit à son équipe juridique de s'exprimer devant la presse et les organisations internationales. Le putsch de février a mis fin à une transition démocratique d’une décennie, les militaires réprimant violemment leurs opposants avec plus de 1 250 civils tués et près de 7 300 en détention, selon une ONG locale, l’Association d’assistance aux prisonniers politiques (AAPP), qui a signalé des cas de tortures, de viols et d’exécutions extra-judiciaires.

La presse est muselée, l'accès à l'internet est limité et les licences des médias sont annulées pour renforcer le contrôle de l'information par la junte.

Before representation learning started gravitating around deep representations in the last decade, a line of research that sparked interest in the early 2000s was based on the so-called manifold hypothesis. According to it, real-world data given in their raw format (e.g., pixels of images) lie on a low-dimensional manifold embedded in the input space. At that time, most manifold learning algorithms were based on locally linear approximations to points on the sought manifold (e.g., LLE, Isomap) or on spectral methods (e.g., MDS, graph Laplacian eigenmaps).

Back to recent years, two trends are apparent: the use of graph-structured data and their direct processing by machine learning algorithms, and the resurgence of the manifold hypothesis, but with a different flavor - being explicit about the assumed manifold and, perhaps, the inductive bias that it entails: hyperbolic spaces, spherical spaces, and Cartesian products of them. While for the first two the choice can be a priori justified - e.g., complex networks are intimately related to hyperbolic geometry - the last one, originally through the work of Gu et al., is motivated through the presumed flexibility coming from its varying curvature. Our work takes that hypothesis further by exploring the representation properties of several irreducible spaces of non-constant sectional curvature. We use, in particular, Riemannian manifolds where points are represented as specific types of matrices and which are at the sweet spot between semantic richness and tractability.

With no additional qualifiers, graph embedding is a vaguely specified intermediary step used as part of systems solving a wide range of graph analytics problems. As a particular instance of that general task, here we embed nodes of graphs with structural information only (i.e., undirected and without node or edge labels), as the ones shown in Figure 1, in novel curved spaces, by leveraging the closed-form expressions of the corresponding Riemannian distance between embedding points; the resulting geodesic distances enter a differentiable objective function which "compares" them to the ground-truth metric given through the node-to-node graph distances. We focus on the representation capabilities of the considered matrix manifolds relative to the previously studied spaces by monitoring graph reconstruction metrics. We note that preserving graph structure is essential to downstream tasks such as link prediction and node classification.

Our main contributions include the introduction of two families of matrix manifolds for graph embedding purposes: the non-positively curved spaces of symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices, and the compact, non-negatively curved Grassmann manifolds; reviving Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (SNE) in the context of Riemannian optimization as a way to unify, on the one hand, the loss functions based on the reconstruction likelihood of local graph neighborhoods and, on the other hand, the global, all-pairs stress functions used for global metric recovery; a generalization of the usual ranking-based metric to quantify reconstruction fidelity beyond immediate neighbors; a comprehensive experimental comparison of the introduced manifolds against the baselines in terms of their graph reconstruction capabilities, focusing on the impact of curvature.

Related Work. Our work is inspired by the emerging field of geometric deep learning (GDL) through its use of geometry. That being said, our motivation and approach are different. In GDL, deep networks transform data in a geometry-aware way, usually as part of larger discriminative or generative models.

La Guardia Civil ha detenido a dos mujeres acusadas de robar la suma de 1.400 euros a un hombre de 81 años en la ciudad gaditana de Tarifa.
En un comunicado, el Instituto Armado explicó que las arrestadas, ambas de nacionalidad española y una de ellas con antecedentes policiales por delitos contra el patrimonio, aprovecharon la distracción del anciano para quitarle el dinero que acababa de retirar de un banco.
El hombre, de 81 años, había retirado el dinero de una sucursal bancaria recientemente.
Las detenidas, que no eran conocidas en la zona, llamaron la atención de un comerciante, quien las vio abandonar el lugar en un vehículo y pudo proporcionar información para su identificación.
La información proporcionada por el gerente del establecimiento, junto con la revisión de las cámaras de seguridad de varios comercios y del propio banco, condujeron al equipo investigador de la Guardia Civil a la identificación y posterior localización de las mujeres en la ciudad de Tarifa.
Se realizaron las diligencias correspondientes sobre los hechos. Por lo tanto, las mujeres arrestadas como presuntas autoras de un delito de hurto fueron puestas a disposición de la autoridad judicial competente.

Pentagon leaders warn that more marine vessels might experience coronavirus outbreaks, following an incident on a Pacific carrier where over 400 sailors were infected. General John Hyten, Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, announced today that a crew member from the USS Theodore Roosevelt is currently in intensive care on Guam. The ship has been docked there for over a week. Presently, 416 crew members are infected, and 1,164 test results are still pending.

"It's not wise to think that the situation with the Teddy Roosevelt is unique," Hyten stated at a Pentagon news conference. "We have numerous ships at sea... assuming it won't happen again is poor planning."

Admiral Mike Gilday highlighted the primary issue: the difficulty in conducting rapid and widespread testing, including for those aboard the USS Nimitz, the next U.S.-based carrier slated to deploy.

"The challenge we face is developing the capability to test in both volume and speed," Gilday informed a small group of reporters. "I can't provide a precise estimate on when we'll achieve the testing capacity we desire."

Sailors on the USS Nimitz, currently in port, will undergo a two-week quarantine before deployment. Although a civilian worker was transported to the Nimitz over a week ago after exhibiting symptoms, the test results were inconclusive. Hyten mentioned a small number of sick sailors, but the Navy clarified today that no current sailors on the Nimitz have tested positive for COVID-19 or displayed symptoms.

Retired Admiral James Stavridis, a former NATO commander, foresees continued challenges for the Navy and other military branches. "It's evident there are more challenges ahead," Stavridis expressed via email. "The Navy and all services face difficult decisions on whether to pull units to ensure their well-being or accept a certain level of risk due to the virus. I anticipate a case-by-case approach based on mission requirements."

Gilday noted that the Navy has learned from the Roosevelt outbreak, particularly the transition from prevention to managing the virus as sailors begin to show symptoms. As of today, 3,190 crew members have tested negative, with pending results for the remainder. About 2,700 sailors have been moved off the ship and accommodated at the base and hotels on the island. Those testing positive are monitored medically twice a day.

More broadly, Hyten stated that the Roosevelt incident illustrates how the military must adapt. "This will be a new operational reality we must address," he said, referencing the challenges of recruiting, training, deploying, and potentially engaging in combat during the pandemic. "We're adjusting to this new world in real time."

The outbreak on the Roosevelt began in late March, plunging the Navy into a leadership crisis. Thomas Modly resigned as Navy Secretary after dismissing Captain Brett E. Crozier, the Roosevelt's commander, for widely disseminating a letter urging the Navy to take swifter action to protect his crew. Modly faced backlash for visiting the Roosevelt and delivering remarks harshly critical of Crozier.

Gilday announced that the investigation into the Roosevelt incident, initiated last week, is complete, and he is reviewing the report. He has not ruled out any actions, including potentially reinstating Crozier, depending on the findings. The central issue is why Crozier felt the need to send the memo and whether it indicated a breakdown in communication and leadership. "All options are on the table," Gilday said regarding Crozier's future. He added that he hasn't spoken with Crozier and feels no external pressure concerning the investigation, emphasizing fairness in his actions.

In a separate appearance, General Mark Milley, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, remarked that despite the outbreak, the Roosevelt could be reactivated and return to duty if global events necessitate it. Speaking alongside Hyten, Deputy Secretary of Defense David Norquist emphasized that military leaders recognize the coronavirus as a long-term challenge. "We need to adapt, as the virus won't disappear in the coming months," Norquist stated. "We must learn to operate effectively in a COVID environment."

The new coronavirus generally causes mild or moderate symptoms, such as fever and cough, lasting two to three weeks. However, it can lead to severe illness, including pneumonia and death, particularly in older adults and those with pre-existing health conditions.

Since the 1980s, the world has made significant advancements in technology, improving devices like phones and TVs, among others. Imagine a future where cars are no longer manually driven. Instead, driverless cars could dominate, offering a safer, more enjoyable, and beneficial mode of transportation.

Some people may wonder what they would do while the car is driving itself. The answer is simple: they could play games and spend quality time with their children. A common concern is the safety of driverless cars, but they are, in fact, safer because they are not entirely autonomous. They require human intervention, such as pulling out of driveways and navigating work zones, ensuring additional safety measures are in place.

There are numerous reasons why driverless cars should gain popularity. First, they could potentially be safer than human-driven cars. For instance, many accidents are caused by human error, such as driving under the influence or texting. Driverless cars could significantly reduce the number of such incidents, leading to fewer injuries and fatalities.

Another reason driverless cars should be embraced is the enhanced enjoyment they offer. While the car drives, people could engage in fun activities, like playing games, and interacting with their children, fostering better family connections. Nowadays, children are often absorbed in their phones, paying little attention to their surroundings, and driverless cars could help bridge the gap, allowing parents and children to spend more time together.

Marilyn sat in the corner of the room, nestled in a red paisley armchair, painting her fingernails a deep burgundy that flirted with black. Each stroke of the brush was purposeful and intense, the glossy handle gleaming in the dim light that reflected off her teeth. Watching from the bed, Morgan couldn't quite fathom why she was smiling. Glancing around, he counted three empty bottles of gin and a couple more half-full ones.

"What have I gotten myself into?" he pondered.

"Shall we go?" Marilyn's voice interrupted his dark thoughts from the corner. "I'm ready to go."

"Let's go, then," he replied.

They traveled in a sleek black car to the ball. Morgan presented the forged invitation, feeling his tie constrict like a serpent around his neck until the bouncer nodded and welcomed him as "Mr. Strumford, enjoy the evening."

As soon as they mingled with the crowd, Marilyn detached herself from his arm and vanished. "I'm going to powder my nose," she had said. Ha. Marilyn seldom wore makeup, and when she did, it was only lipstick and eyeshadow. Nonetheless, she outshone every woman in the room. If they were diamonds, she was the moon—rarer and more precious than all of them combined.

Morgan drifted towards a group of partygoers, holding champagne flutes in their flawless hands and engaging in light banter. They made way for him to join, and he realized keenly that he was out of his element here.

He was a kind of businessman, involved in minor crimes and information trading. Enough to provide a taste of luxury but never to truly indulge. These were the men who lounged, indulging in caviar and cocaine in homes he couldn't even dream of entering. Yet Morgan was there to deceive them.

"Who are you?" inquired the leader, tall and blond with a perfect part and dazzling smile. Gianiss, a mobster and the proprietor of two casinos.

Recalling Marilyn's advice, Morgan hesitated. "Lie all you want, but never reveal enough for them to truly know who you are. It's better to be seen as a pretender than a thief."

"I'm new in town, arrived by train just a month ago. Looking to build an empire."

"What kind of empire?" Gianiss probed.

"Something I'm not prepared to discuss in good company," Morgan replied.

"Well, look at this big shot. What do you say, gentlemen? Shall we introduce ourselves to Mr...?" The weight of the question hung in the air. If Morgan used his usual aliases, there was a risk of exposure. What had Marilyn suggested?

"Stanford, no relations."

They welcomed him. Finding a table, they delved into business discussions while discreetly eyeing the elegant women passing by, pretending not to notice a group of emerging mobsters and businessmen.

"Are any of those women yours?" Morgan asked Gianiss.

"I assume you have your own arrangements, Stanford."

"For men of simpler tastes, certainly. But you employ women for clientele like us, don't you?"

Gianiss chuckled. "No one comes to sin city seeking a virtuous life, but I had hoped you might be an exception."

"There's no harm in indulging in what you've paid for."

Gianiss signaled, and three women approached the table.

Morgan kissed the hand of a woman with auburn hair and green eyes. "What's on your agenda tonight, Miss?"

She smiled, a bit too widely, and whispered in his ear. Blushing, Morgan excused himself from the table. "I think it's time for me to leave, gentlemen. Pleasure meeting you."

She led him upstairs, away from the ongoing party below. Morgan's absence went unnoticed.

Opening a door on the third floor, she pushed him inside. Under the room's solitary lamp sat Marilyn, still grinning like a jackal. "Sit, talk, give me a sign."

"I've got it.

Los Mossos d'Esquadra detuvieron el martes en Lleida a un hombre y a un menor de edad por presuntamente vender marihuana, según informó el cuerpo policial en un comunicado el miércoles. Durante el mes de julio, los Mossos pusieron en marcha un dispositivo para investigar un posible caso de tráfico de drogas, y observaron que las ventas las realizaban un hombre y un joven que parecía ser menor de edad.

Los investigadores lograron identificar a las dos personas involucradas: un hombre de 28 años y un joven de 17, que resultó ser hermano de la pareja sentimental del adulto. El martes, procedieron a la detención de ambos y llevaron a cabo un registro en el domicilio, donde encontraron 1,5 kilos de marihuana, 2.215 euros y varios utensilios para la venta de drogas.

En el piso, que presentaba deficientes condiciones higiénicas, también residían dos bebés pertenecientes a la pareja, por lo que los Mossos alertaron a la Dirección General de Atención a la Infancia y la Adolescencia (Dgaia) sobre la situación.

I strongly believe that the Face on Mars is just a natural landform. There are many reasons for my belief; similar formations are common around Cydonia, and it could just be another Martian mesa.

When the Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) arrived at the Red Planet in September 1997, it began capturing images as soon as it could get a clear shot. When the photo was released on the internet, it showed nothing but a natural landform, not an alien monument. Some people argue that it was particularly cloudy on Mars when the MGS took the picture, which may have obscured any alien features with haze. However, the mission controllers later captured another image of the Face on a cloudless summer day in Cydonia, using the camera's maximum resolution. This image confirmed the Face was the Martian equivalent of a butte or mesa, similar to the formations common in the American West.

Lying in my hammock, fashioned from old jumpers, I gaze upon the mountains of lost socks. I have traversed this godforsaken island from one end to the other, seemingly spending an eternity in search. I've discovered all sorts of things, from shoelaces to CDs and everything in between. Yet, nothing has proved useful for my escape. Le débat fait rage sur la scène sombre et caverneuse d'un entrepôt de la Warner Bros, à propos d'un... champignon. Un membre de l'équipe du film veut éclairer cet accessoire de 15 centimètres depuis la droite. Un autre préfère le côté gauche. Richard Crudo, un vétéran de Hollywood, cinéaste ayant travaillé pour de nombreux films, dont American Pie (1999) ou Donnie Darko (2001), d'abord en retrait, intervient. « Si vous pouvez bien l'éclairer, vous allez gagner un prix de l'Académie », professe-t-il, sourire en coin.

Il supervise une trentaine de jeunes stagiaires de l'Academy Gold, un programme d'été sélectif mis en place par l'Académie des Oscars où les aspirants cinéastes participent à des sessions de travail en coopération avec des géants de l'industrie comme Disney, Sony ou Paramount. L'initiative a été mise en place dans le sillage de la campagne Oscars So White qui dénonçait le manque de diversité dans l'industrie cinématographique. L'Academy Gold s'adresse aux minorités ethniques, aux femmes et aux personnes souffrant d'un handicap.

« C'est dur pour tout le monde de percer et c'est surtout difficile pour les personnes issues des minorités et les gens qui ont été sous-représentés dans l'industrie depuis des années », poursuit ce membre de l'American Society of Cinematographers. Hollywood a franchi le pas après avoir pris conscience que son univers composé d'hommes blancs riches était « simplement une situation intenable », développe Richard Crudo. « Il était temps, il était grand temps », assène-t-il.

Les stagiaires ont, ce jour-là, été divisés en cinq groupes, chaque groupe devant transformer le même scénario, volontairement sibyllin, en scène de film d'un genre de leur choix. Cette équipe veut du surréel et une esthétique à la David Lynch. D'où ce mannequin hilare, au regard sombre, avec un chapeau de cowboy, et cet étrange champignon. L'optimisme de ces jeunes - dont certains ont commencé à travailler dans le cinéma après l'éclosion de la campagne #OscarsSoWhite et des mouvements anti-harcèlement #metoo et #TimesUp - concernant les progrès sur le front de la diversité est palpable.

« Le jour où je serai aux Oscars et qu'il y aura autant de nommés femmes que d'hommes alors je serai satisfaite », relativise toutefois Alyssah Powell, 22 ans.

In today's technology-driven society, equipping students with the knowledge and skills for active civic engagement and addressing societal issues using computing tools has become essential. Computer science proficiency stands out as a key competency applicable across various disciplines, careers, and civic contexts. With the "Computer Science For All" initiative, computer science courses are increasingly being implemented in K-12 education. Simultaneously, efforts at different levels are aimed at enhancing environmental science education to address climate challenges. California, for instance, is committed to fostering environmental literacy throughout K-12 education, following the lead of the California Department of Education, while the United Nations Decade of Education for Sustainable Development focuses on instilling behaviors necessary for sustainability.

Integrating computer science and environmental science into the curriculum enriches students' skills in both areas. This integration not only enhances learning experiences but also cultivates computing and computational thinking abilities. By using coding as a tool, students can create projects to address societal issues and teach scientific concepts. Through coding, students not only learn how to code but also utilize it to achieve their creative goals, nurturing computational thinking skills in the process.

Data literacy is another crucial skill across academic disciplines and everyday life, playing a vital role in various domains. Data literacy empowers students to make informed decisions, enhances problem-solving abilities, and prepares them for active civic engagement. Initiating data literacy education early on is crucial in equipping students with these essential skills.

An integrated computer science curriculum, utilizing culturally sustaining pedagogy, can benefit underrepresented students by creating a multisensory learning environment. By incorporating various modalities and sensory inputs, technology enhances content comprehension for students with disabilities and English language learners. Connecting curriculum content to students' lives and experiences makes learning meaningful and fosters computing skills through innovative technology.

A curriculum framework integrating computer science with community-based environmental literacy, language and literacy scaffolding, and culturally sustaining elements has been developed to support diverse students. Piloted with Latinx 5th-grade students with disabilities and English language learners, this curriculum framework represents the early stages of a design-based implementation research project. The research seeks to explore the design of an integrated curriculum framework to promote environmental and data literacy for students with diverse needs and assess the affordances and challenges in teaching multilingual Latinx students with disabilities.

The increasing prevalence of the Internet of Things (IoT) has made the task of securing IoT networks more complex. Wireless devices in these networks, such as sensors, are often limited by their power and computational capabilities, making traditional cryptography-based authentication systems impractical. To tackle this challenge, the concept of passive Physical Layer Authentication (PLA) has emerged, as it doesn't burden the transmitter with additional overhead [1]. PLA relies on channel state information and signal fingerprints, which are affected by hardware imperfections, to identify transmitters.

An effective authentication system must be able to distinguish authorized transmitters from unauthorized ones (outliers). Given that the unauthorized set is potentially infinite, this issue is framed as an open-set classification, unlike the closed-set classification, where all classes are known. Recent studies have shown the efficacy of open-set classification models based on deep learning (DL) in the context of PLA, as they achieve high accuracy and exhibit robustness to channel variations [2, 3].

Up to now, authentication systems have been evaluated with a fixed, static authorized set, assuming no changes during training, testing, and deployment. However, in real-world scenarios, the authorized set often evolves, necessitating the addition, removal, or replacement of transmitters. For instance, a malfunctioning sensor in an IoT network might require substitution, highlighting the need for the authentication system to swiftly adapt to the updated authorized set, preventing prolonged downtime. The cold winds blew harshly in the night as he pushed the hair from his angular forehead with his rough hands. His dark eyes surveyed the land that his people had once called home. The winds of change had swept through the valleys, and the fires that illuminated the night were no longer those of his people. Around each flickering orange glow, unfamiliar sounds filled the air, speaking words he could not understand. The echoes of their laughter mingled with the clinking of chipped stones as the newcomers crafted tools more advanced than ever seen before. Some of his people had been defeated in battle by the more sophisticated tribe, while others had found refuge around the new fires, creating homes for children whose features no longer bore the distinctiveness of his own.

In the night, wolves howled and the distant scream of a wildcat pierced the air from a far-off ridge. The cold seeped through his furs as winter drew near. His companions had succumbed to hunger and cold, while the rest had deserted him for the warmth of foreign fires. Alone, he stood, gazing at the end of an era.

As Ryan slopped another ladle of lumpy broccoli soup into the waiting bowl, he couldn't help but think, *Ugh*. The smell of the soup wafted over him, a mix of week-old piss and year-old sweat that turned his stomach. 

Across from him stood a man in a filthy old T-shirt, linen pants held up with a rope, and threadbare leather sandals. His matted black hair was tangled, with encrusted patches of snot in his long, straggly beard. Despite his unkempt appearance, Ryan could see that the man had a decent look about him. It was a reminder that looks didn't define a person; some still fell through the cracks. 

Glancing down the line, Ryan noted that most of them easily scored a seventy, enough to claim government benefits and secure a lease for their own place. As he served another bowl, he caught sight of the sign above the door, announcing the Bay Area 51st Annual Homeless Soup Drive in bold, enthusiastic letters. How much longer would he have to endure this routine? Becca, who used to volunteer at the animal shelter, had significantly improved her score from forty-seven to seventy-eight within four months. She had since moved on to better opportunities. 

In contrast, Ryan had been stuck at twenty-eight for nearly two years. He couldn't seem to make any progress. The homeless man in front of him held out his bowl, looking at Ryan with pale blue eyes and a hint of disgust. It sparked an urge in Ryan to take the ladle and do something drastic. He was accustomed to receiving such looks; his physical features often led people to misjudge his character. Yet, he had changed. Sure, he had made mistakes in the past, but everyone did. And if he had enjoyed some of those mistakes, was it really his fault? After all, he couldn't change how he was wired. 

Two years of volunteering at soup kitchens, cleaning graffiti, and assisting at the old folks' home had not raised his score by even a single point. He needed forty-two more points to reach the golden number of seventy, mandated by the Universal Moral Fiber Act (or as it was colloquially known, the Ugly Motherfucker Act). Only then would he become eligible for a Betterment Grant and have a chance to leave government housing. Many employers also required a minimum score of seventy for hiring. 

Every month, Ryan dutifully submitted his photo and forms, only to receive the same response that his Appearance Index remained at twenty-eight.

Les Mercedes se sont encore montrées intouchables vendredi lors des deux premières séances d'essais libres du Grand Prix des 70 ans de la F1 en réalisant des temps beaucoup plus rapides que leurs rivales les plus proches. Valtteri Bottas le matin, Lewis Hamilton l'après-midi, les pilotes des "Flèches noires" ont devancé Max Verstappen (Red Bull) à l'issue de la 1re séance d'essais libres et Daniel Ricciardo (Renault) lors de la seconde. Mais Verstappen était à 727/1000e de Bottas le matin et Ricciardo à 815/1000e d'Hamilton l'après-midi, démontrant le gouffre qui sépare les voitures allemandes de leurs adversaires.

Ces séances d'essais du vendredi servent essentiellement à mettre les monoplaces au point avant les qualifications samedi et la course dimanche, elles ne reflètent pas nécessairement le rapport des forces. Mais les Mercedes, qui ont gagné les quatre premières courses de la saison (3 à Hamilton, 1 à Bottas), ne semblent pas avoir de souci à se faire. Sauf du côté des pneus; tant Hamilton que Bottas ont crevé à l'avant-gauche lors du dernier Grand Prix de Grande-Bretagne la semaine dernière sur ce même circuit de Silverstone. Si le Britannique est quand même parvenu à franchir la ligne d'arrivée en vainqueur, son pneu détruit, le Finlandais, alors derrière lui, n'a terminé que 11e, laissant son coéquipier s'envoler au championnat.

Il fera encore chaud pour le Grand Prix dimanche et Silverstone, avec ses enchaînements de longues courbes rapides, est connu pour martyriser les pneus. L'écurie allemande a donc à cœur de tester la résistance des gommes pendant les essais. D'autant plus que celles retenues, de longue date, pour la course, par le manufacturier Pirelli qui équipe l'ensemble du plateau, seront plus tendres que dimanche dernier.

Mais l'attention ne se portait pas vendredi que sur la piste. La décision de la Fédération internationale de l'automobile (FIA) de donner raison à Renault face à sa rivale Racing Point a animé le paddock. L'écurie française accusait Racing Point d'avoir copié certaines pièces équipant sa monoplace de cette année directement sur la Mercedes victorieuse du championnat 2019, notamment les écopes de freins. La FIA a jugé que c'était le cas même si cela ne rend pas illégales ces écopes, qui jouent un rôle essentiel pour le refroidissement des freins et l'aérodynamique.

Racing Point va donc perdre 15 points au championnat constructeurs et devra payer 400.000 euros d'amende. Mais Lance Stroll et Sergio Pérez gardent toutefois leurs points acquis depuis le début de la saison, au classement pilotes. L'écurie du milliardaire canadien Lawrence Stroll perd du même coup la 5e place au classement provisoire du championnat au profit de Renault.

La 3e place de l'Australien Ricciardo, lors de la 2e séance d'essais libres, est donc venue couronner une bonne journée pour Renault. Il avait terminé 4e du GP de Grande-Bretagne la semaine dernière et Renault semble avoir enfin trouvé la vitesse qui lui faisait défaut.

A Quique Peinado, la televisión le ha proporcionado grandísimos momentos y lo ha puesto bajo el foco, pero no es el medio que más le gusta. Aunque hace humor, se define claramente como periodista y no como cómico. Su estilo humorístico está diseñado para extraer la gracia de situaciones que otros no ven. Desde su papel como colaborador en programas, se lanza hacia cualquier polémica que surja, defendiendo su fe en la libertad de expresión.

Su verdadera pasión, confiesa a Crónica, sería "dirigir documentales". Sin embargo, la necesidad de vivir lo ha llevado a encontrar su lugar en la televisión, donde, a través de Zapeando en La Sexta, logra sacar sonrisas a diario, incluso de los temas más complicados. Cabe mencionar su peculiar estilo en la vestimenta, con sus llamativas camisas que nunca pasan desapercibidas.

Peinado enfatiza: «La verdad es que yo no soy un cómico». A pesar de que muchos cómicos están en auge en la televisión, él considera que este campo está lleno de riesgos, especialmente cuando se cruza la delgada línea de lo que se puede decir. Para él, el humor es esencial para sobrellevar las peores situaciones. Reírse de todo es su lema, y aunque no es un cómico tradicional, utiliza el humor como una herramienta periodística.

Los inicios de Peinado están profundamente ligados al periodismo deportivo. Durante más de veinte años, ha colaborado con la revista Gigantes del Basket y se ha aventurado en diversos medios, como Eurosport, Esquire y otros. Sin embargo, su enfoque cómico surgió de forma natural en su trayectoria. Él mismo menciona que, antes de Zapeando, trabajaba como guionista en un programa de radio y nunca tuvo formación como humorista.

Su humor, a menudo satírico y sarcástico, le ha llevado a generar reacciones encontradas en las redes sociales, donde no se corta en criticar a figuras como Cifuentes o Vox. Peinado recuerda un enfrentamiento en Twitter con el community manager de la ex presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid tras un artículo que publicó en EL MUNDO, donde se defendía a la alcaldesa Manuela Carmena. En esta batalla de comentarios, Quique tuvo la última palabra, reafirmando su estilo directo y su capacidad de respuesta ante cualquier controversia.

Si bien es cierto que su humor puede herir sensibilidades, él es consciente de que hacer comedia en la televisión conlleva riesgos. La libertad de expresión que defiende es un principio básico, aunque reconoce que hay comentarios que pueden desatar críticas. Por ello, vive en constante tensión con las reacciones que su trabajo genera, siendo el blanco de ataques, algunos de los cuales han afectado a su familia.

A pesar de su estilo mordaz, Peinado también se aleja de la crítica sarcástica a través de proyectos que humanizan la televisión, como su programa Radio Gaga, donde presenta historias de vida a cambio de canciones. En este formato, la conexión con las personas es fundamental, algo que valora profundamente.

Reflexionando sobre su paso por la televisión, destaca un recuerdo: su estancia en un programa rodeado de profesionales experimentados. Reconoce que logró hacerse un hueco cuando otros se quedaron atrás, aludiendo a su “intrusismo absoluto” en este mundo.

Have you ever considered if life on a different planet would be the same as it is on Earth? Spoiler alert: it's not. Venus, the closest planet to Earth, presents significant challenges for human exploration due to its unique characteristics such as its orbit around the sun and its corrosive sulfuric acid clouds. Despite these dangers, the author of "The Challenge of Exploring Venus" argues that Venus is worth exploring because of its proximity to Earth and shared traits with our own planet. The author envisions conquering this challenge as a valuable learning experience.

To begin with, the author points out that Venus is often referred to as Earth's "twin" due to similarities in size and density. This similarity could provide an opportunity for humans to study and reach this intriguing planet. Furthermore, since Venus is considered one of the most Earth-like planets in our solar system, efforts should be made to push boundaries and explore its mysteries.

The author further emphasizes their argument by highlighting how spacecraft have not landed on Venus for over three decades. As stated in the article, there is immense value in revisiting Venus; however, the challenge lies in executing a mission that is both safe and scientifically fruitful. Overcoming this challenge could lead to groundbreaking discoveries and advancements in space exploration.

Lastly, the potential knowledge gained from venturing into Venus' unknown territories is underscored by NASA's proposed solution: floating above the hostile surface conditions. Imaginative strategies like using technology inspired by World War II-era mechanical computers demonstrate the innovative spirit driving efforts towards studying this enigmatic planet.

In conclusion, with strong statistical support and unwavering ambition, exploring Venus remains an alluring possibility for future explorations. It may only be a matter of time before humanity sets foot on this fascinating world, reaping rich rewards from such endeavors.

La Bourse de Paris a clôturé en légère hausse mardi (+0,37 %), la perspective d'un redémarrage imminent de l'activité l'emportant sur les craintes inflationnistes, dans un contexte de détente du marché obligataire. L'indice CAC 40 a progressé de 21,98 points pour atteindre 5 924,97 points, après une forte augmentation de 2,08 % la veille.

"La tendance reste positive sur les marchés actions", soutenus par les perspectives de reprise économique, bien qu'ils apparaissent "volatils d'un jour à l'autre" en ce moment, estime Françoise Cespedes, gérante actions chez Aviva Investors France. Alors que les résultats annuels des entreprises sont désormais derrière nous, les investisseurs se concentrent sur les statistiques économiques et "le marché réagit à des nouvelles à très court terme", explique-t-elle à l'AFP.

L'OCDE a révisé à la hausse sa prévision de croissance mondiale pour 2021, la portant à 5,6 %, grâce aux effets conjugués du méga-plan de relance américain et de la vaccination, selon ses perspectives intermédiaires publiées mardi. Pour 2021, la croissance de l'économie française sera "au moins égale à 5 %", a estimé mardi le gouverneur de la Banque de France, François Villeroy de Galhau, sur France Info.

Dans ce contexte de reprise économique, combiné à un risque d'inflation accru, les rendements des bons du Trésor américain et des autres obligations souveraines ont récemment bondi avant de commencer à se détendre. Après avoir nettement progressé lundi, les valeurs bancaires ont réagi négativement au repli des rendements obligataires : Société Générale a perdu 2,37 % à 21,81 euros, BNP Paribas 1,24 % à 52,59 euros et Crédit Agricole 1,51 % à 12,38 euros.

Worldline (+3,31 % à 74,96 euros), Capgemini (+3,15 % à 143,90 euros) et Atos (+1,73 % à 64,64 euros) ont mené la danse, dans le sillage de l'indice américain Nasdaq qui regroupe les grandes valeurs technologiques de Wall Street.

In "Challenges of Exploring Venus," the author argues for the importance of gaining more knowledge about Venus, our sister planet, and suggests that it is possible to explore it safely and effectively. He provides compelling examples and reasons why such an exploration would be beneficial.

Expanding our understanding of Venus is advantageous in numerous ways and can be conducted safely. With an average surface temperature of 800 degrees Fahrenheit, Venus is virtually uninhabitable for humans. The author notes, "such an environment would crush even a submarine accustomed to diving to the deepest parts of our oceans." Given Venus's harsh conditions, surface exploration poses significant challenges, requiring alternative exploration methods. NASA, for instance, has proposed exploring Venus from a distance of about 30 miles, where the pressure is comparable to sea level on Earth, and the temperature is around 170 degrees Fahrenheit. The author states, "Not easy conditions, but survivable for humans." Although the mission would entail significant risks and be a formidable challenge, it is achievable with the right expertise and technology. The knowledge gained from exploring Venus, a planet that has long intrigued the world, would be invaluable, and it's time to rise to the challenge for the benefit of humanity.

Una historia de telenovela: La cantante mexicana Lucero y Manuel Mijares se convirtieron durante los años 90 en una de las parejas más mediáticas y famosas, caracterizados por el gran amor que los unía. Esta mágica historia inició a mediados de los años 80, en 1985, cuando ambos se conocieron en la película “Escápate conmigo”.

El amor floreció entre ellos y, poco después de conocerse y colaborar en diversas producciones televisivas, decidieron dar un paso más allá y se casaron en 1997. El lugar escogido para la boda fue la capilla de San Ignacio de Loyola del Colegio de la Paz, también conocido como “de las Vizcaínas”, ubicada en la Ciudad de México.

Su matrimonio traspasó fronteras, pues fue transmitido no solo en México, sino también en los Estados Unidos, algo que pocas parejas, incluso en el medio artístico, logran conseguir. Este evento forma parte de los 10 programas más vistos en la televisión. Además, la transmisión de la boda trajo consigo importantes ganancias económicas, recaudando un total de 32 millones de pesos por la venta de publicidad durante el espacio.

Más información: La millonaria propuesta que le hizo a Lucero su novio para que no realice la gira con Mijares.

Luego de un año, la pareja inauguró un restaurante en la colonia Anzures y en 2002 nació su primer hijo, Manuel Antonio. Tres años más tarde, llegó su hija, Lucerito.

Rumores de la ruptura:
Casi al llegar a los 10 años de matrimonio, exactamente en 2006, comenzaron a circular ciertos rumores sobre la pareja, entre ellos, que Lucero era la única que generaba ingresos para la familia. Sin embargo, la pareja evitó que estas versiones afectaran su hogar y felicidad.

Durante 2009, se evidenciaron algunas diferencias entre los dos artistas, lo cual fortaleció los rumores de un posible rompimiento en cualquier momento. 

En un evento realizado por Manuel Mijares en el Auditorio Nacional, el cantante reafirmó que Lucero era la mujer más importante de su vida y la presentó ante el público. Acto seguido, cantaron “Cuatro veces amor”, de donde surgió la frase “Hasta que se nos hizo, Manuelito”.

High-capacity neural networks trained on large, diverse datasets have led to remarkable models capable of solving numerous tasks, rapidly adapting to new ones, and producing general-purpose representations in NLP and vision (Brown et al., 2020; He et al., 2021). The promise of offline reinforcement learning (RL) lies in leveraging these advances to produce policies with broad generalization, emergent capabilities, and performance that exceeds the capabilities demonstrated in the training dataset.

Thus far, the only offline RL approaches that demonstrate broadly generalizing policies and transferable representations are heavily based on supervised learning (Reed et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2022). However, these approaches are likely to perform poorly when the dataset does not contain expert trajectories (Kumar et al., 2021b).

Offline Q-learning has shown to perform well across dataset compositions in a variety of simulated (Gulcehre et al., 2020; Fu et al., 2020) and real-world domains (Chebotar et al., 2021; Soares et al., 2021). However, these are largely centered around small-scale, single-task problems where broad generalization and learning general-purpose representations are not expected. Scaling these methods to high-capacity models on large, diverse datasets remains a critical challenge. Prior works have hinted at the difficulties: on small-scale, single-task deep RL benchmarks, scaling model capacity can lead to instabilities or degrade performance (Van Hasselt et al., 2018; Sinha et al., 2020; Ota et al., 2021), explaining why decade-old tiny 3-layer CNN architectures (Mnih et al., 2013) are still prevalent. Moreover, works that have scaled architectures to millions of parameters (Espeholt et al., 2018; Teh et al., 2017; Vinyals et al., 2019; Schrittwieser et al., 2021) typically focus on online learning and employ many sophisticated techniques to stabilize learning, such as supervised auxiliary losses, distillation, and pre-training. Thus, it is unclear whether offline Q-learning can be scaled to high-capacity models trained on a large, diverse dataset.

In this paper, we demonstrate that with careful design decisions, offline Q-learning can scale to high-capacity models trained on large, diverse datasets from many tasks. This leads to policies that not only generalize broadly but also learn representations that effectively transfer to new downstream tasks and exceed performance in the training dataset. Crucially, we make three modifications motivated by prior work in deep learning and offline RL. First, we find that a modified ResNet architecture (He et al., 2016) substantially outperforms typical deep RL architectures and follows a power-law relationship between model capacity and performance, unlike common alternatives. Second, a discretized representation of the return distribution with a distributional cross-entropy loss (Bellemare et al., 2017) substantially improves performance compared to standard Q-learning that utilizes mean squared error. Finally, feature normalization on the intermediate feature representations stabilizes training and prevents feature co-adaptation (Kumar et al., 2021a).

To systematically evaluate the impact of these changes on scaling and generalization, we train a single policy to play 40 Atari games (Bellemare et al., 2013; Agarwal et al., 2020), similarly to Lee et al. (2022), and evaluate performance when the training dataset contains expert trajectories and when the data is sub-optimal. This problem is especially challenging because of the diversity of games with their own unique dynamics, reward, visuals, and agent embodiments.

Nine firefighters and three vehicles from the Lebanon Fire District have been actively combating the Beachie Creek wildfire over the past week. The firefighters were dispatched on Tuesday, September 8, joining other crews in 12-hour shifts to combat the blaze that has ravaged communities in the Santiam Canyon. The Lebanon firefighters are directly involved in fire attack operations and are providing structural protection and evacuation support.

Lebanon Fire Chief Joseph Rodondi mentioned that the department is collaborating with neighboring fire departments in Scio and Sweet Home. Lebanon crews are backing up these departments, which are more heavily engaged in fighting the fires threatening their communities. "We are in constant contact with our partner agencies in Scio and Sweet Home," Rodondi stated.

To meet these demands, Rodondi noted that the Lebanon department has relied heavily on its full-time and volunteer firefighters. "We have increased our staffing levels this week," Rodondi remarked.

In addition to firefighting efforts, the department is committed to ensuring the public receives the most accurate and up-to-date information available. Rodondi emphasized that the Linn County Sheriff's Office is the most reliable source for updates on the fires and current evacuation levels and zones. "I encourage people to visit the Linn County Sheriff's Office website," Rodondi advised. "The most important thing is to have accurate, consistent information."

The perceptions of sentient beings often distort their understanding of concepts like good and evil, which are popular even outside of humanity. Without the behaviors deemed "good" or "evil" by these beings, such concepts are nonexistent. At their core, any destruction, regardless of intent, is still just destruction where creation once existed. Both destruction and creation find their paths to success, indicating there is no true distinction between them. One simply leads into another, demonstrating their interconnectedness. 

Many of the words used by humans to describe me, such as "God," are often inappropriate. Most of them can't articulate what exactly they mean when they invoke this term, as they lack understanding of my actual role. I can't specify the details of my work, as doing so would require assigning names, which implies the use of language, something I inherently lack. Generalizations, therefore, are necessary, though my essence is far simpler than they perceive. 

There are, however, words that are more fitting, like "creation," "destruction," and "influence."

Bodies lay scattered everywhere, each figure telling a story of violence and betrayal. His personal staff, a group of young men, lay lifeless, surrounded by pools of their own blood, victims of fatal bullet wounds. Among them, one man stood out, seemingly having endured a different, more gruesome fate, with burn marks covering his arms and neck. Amidst this grim scene, I found him, clutching a blood-covered book, a bullet hole piercing directly between his eyes. It was frustrating, to say the least, that he took the satisfaction of justice away from us, opting instead to end his own life, a cowardly escape from the consequences of his actions.

Curious, I flipped through the pages of the book, wondering what a scumbag like him could possibly cherish, even in his final moments, before choosing a coward's exit.

It was a dark and stormy night. The house was dead as a doornail, but I couldn't imagine the stories it would tell if the walls could talk. I gazed around at the piles of books in my room, surrounded like a kid in a candy shop, all old poems and stories written by obscure authors that others of my generation didn't know. I picked the first book off a pile, the low hanging fruit, *The Fault in Our Stars* by John Green, it's a totally obscure book that you probably don't know about. I looked at the pictures on the wall, my best friend who was dead and my parents who had died too. My tape deck (I used a tape deck because it was so unique and I'm so weird and unique compared to other kids of my generation) played David Bowie, an obscure 80s musician you've probably never heard of.

Durante una conferencia de prensa en el despacho de alcaldía, para dar a conocer las distintas actividades a realizarse por el 86 aniversario de creación política del distrito, el alcalde de La Brea-Negritos, Pedro Hoyos León, señaló que las playas negriteñas, sobre todo Punta Balcones y el Puerto Menor de San Pablo, son las más limpias del litoral que conforma la provincia de Talara. Esto no se debe solo a la vigilancia permanente en ellas, sino también a las advertencias a bañistas, turistas y pescadores sobre las drásticas sanciones por contaminación.

El alcalde de La Brea-Negritos, Pedro Hoyos León, manifestó que no basta con colocar personal de vigilancia y serenazgo municipal en las playas de la provincia para evitar que sean contaminadas por bañistas, turistas y pescadores con el arrojo de basura. Es esencial hacer cumplir las normas de protección que establecen sanciones drásticas a las personas que atentan contra el ecosistema marítimo en la región Piura.

Recordó que años atrás lo que contaminaba las playas del distrito era la matanza indiscriminada de lobos marinos. Con el apoyo de Capitanía del Puerto de Talara y otros organismos responsables del cuidado del medio ambiente y el ecosistema marino, se tuvieron que tomar acciones drásticas para poner fin a esta práctica. Las embarcaciones rastreras, que también depredaban el banco de especies hidrobiológicas y arrojaban residuos sólidos al mar, contribuyeron a la contaminación del mar en gran parte.

Además, señaló que otra forma de contaminación del mar negriteño era el desembocadura de las aguas residuales de la ciudad. Pese a pasar por las dos lagunas de oxidación existentes en el distrito, estas aguas llegaban con coliformes al mar. Por ello, se optó por construir y ampliar una tercera laguna, a fin de que las aguas residuales sean mejor tratadas y las que discurran al mar lo hagan sin coliformes.

"Se ha publicado un reportaje en un medio nacional que indica que las playas de Talara están contaminadas y perjudicando el ecosistema marino. Es responsabilidad del alcalde convocar a las autoridades marítimas y organismos de protección del medio ambiente y ecosistema marino para tomar acciones drásticas contra los responsables, porque no basta solo con colocar personal de vigilancia, sino hacer cumplir las leyes", expresó el alcalde.

Agregó además que, "aquí en La Brea-Negritos, hubo un tiempo en que las playas se contaminaban con la matanza de lobos marinos, la depredación de los bancos marinos por embarcaciones rastreras y el arrojo de residuos sólidos.

Barça : Le Coup de Gueule de Ter Stegen

Vainqueur laborieux 2-1 contre la modeste équipe du Slavia Prague (3e journée de la Ligue des Champions), le Barça a irrité son gardien.

Bien que le Barça ait remporté la rencontre sur le terrain du Slavia Prague (2-1), Marc-André ter Stegen n'a pas apprécié la performance de ses coéquipiers et l'a fait savoir. En effet, il a été sollicité tout au long de la soirée, malgré l'ouverture du score dès la 3e minute par le Barça face à un adversaire, sur le papier, beaucoup plus modeste.

Barça : Messi entre un peu plus dans la légende de la Ligue des Champions

"Nous n'avons pas joué au niveau auquel nous aspirions. Heureusement, nous avons pris les trois points, ce qui est le plus important. Mais je pense qu'il est nécessaire de discuter de certaines choses", a déclaré le gardien allemand à l'issue du match, dans des propos rapportés par Marca.

"C’est quelque chose que nous devons aborder entre nous. Je ne vais pas en parler ici, mais il est vraiment nécessaire de régler certains aspects. Cela arrive tout le temps, il y a toujours des choses à améliorer. Dans ce cas précis, nous avons de nombreux sujets à aborder", a souligné le gardien du club catalan, auteur par ailleurs d'une prestation de grande qualité mercredi soir.

Autoritaire, le portier du Barça souhaite surtout en discuter avec ses coéquipiers en interne, comme il le précise dans des propos relayés par Footmercato : "J’insiste sur le fait que c’est une chose que nous devons régler entre nous. C’est en interne. J’aimerais d’abord en parler avec ceux qui étaient sur le terrain."

NEW YORK — Executives at a New York hedge fund have agreed to pay as much as $7 billion to settle a long-running dispute with the U.S. tax authorities, according to reports Thursday. The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times reported that insiders at Renaissance Technologies agreed to the deal, which could be one of the largest in U.S. history.

Renaissance had been locked in a yearslong dispute with the Internal Revenue Service after a Senate investigation determined that the firm used complex financial instruments to avoid paying nearly $7 billion in taxes. The deal covers transactions between 2005 and 2015 and involves moves by the hedge fund to convert short-term trading gains into long-term profits, according to the reports.

Among those included in the settlement are Renaissance founder and prominent Democratic Party donor James Simon, and Robert Mercer, who was a major donor to former President Donald Trump's campaign, according to the reports. Messages were left with Renaissance and the IRS seeking comment.

There is always a new trend that emerges, and many people feel compelled to jump on the bandwagon just because everyone else is doing so. The latest innovation in the works is driverless cars, but despite the advancements, they still require human assistance in certain situations. Currently, there are cars that can be driven with some level of assistance, and they function perfectly well. While the concept of creating cars for the physically disabled who are unable to drive is commendable, for those who are capable of driving and are not physically disabled, relying on such cars could be seen as mere laziness.

I believe that the development of driverless cars is not particularly beneficial for those who are not physically disabled. There is a growing trend of laziness, with the belief that since self-driving cars are being introduced, people can simply be passive passengers, relaxing or even sleeping, while the car autonomously takes them to their destination. Personally, I am not in favor of this idea. When these cars are eventually created, they should be primarily marketed to individuals with physical disabilities, as they are the ones who would benefit the most from this technology.

If these cars are mass-produced, there is the potential for serious safety issues, as malfunctions could occur, leading to accidents, injuries, or even fatalities.

Dr. Paul Eckman created an invention called the Facial Action Coding System (FACS), which can detect human emotions by scanning facial expressions. This innovative technology has the potential to enhance students' focus levels by adapting to their emotional state. The ability to read students' facial expressions in the classroom can be beneficial in improving focus, engaging students with more interesting exercises, and assisting teachers in understanding students' emotions.

FACS can significantly improve students' focus by providing assignments that students find engaging or can relate to. Research has shown that students perform better when they are interested in the topic or assignment. Additionally, the technology can detect when students are becoming confused or bored, prompting adjustments to the lesson, similar to the intervention of a skilled human instructor.

Moreover, the implementation of FACS in schools can lead to the creation of more engaging exercises for students. By tailoring assignments to students' interests, the technology can enhance student performance and motivation. When students are intrigued by the topic, they are more likely to excel in their work.

Furthermore, the use of FACS can also assist teachers in supporting students who may be experiencing emotional distress. If the system detects signs of sadness or anger in a student, it can alert the teacher, providing details to help the teacher comfort the student or help them calm down. This proactive approach can contribute to a supportive and caring classroom environment.

In conclusion, the integration of the Facial Action Coding System in schools can have a positive impact on the learning environment. By improving students' focus, creating engaging exercises, and assisting teachers in addressing students' emotional needs, FACS can enhance the overall educational experience for students.

فاز اللاعب الإسباني رافائيل نادال ببطولة أمريكا المفتوحة للتنس لعام 2019، بعد فوزه على الروسي دانيل ميدفيديف بنتيجة ثلاثة أشواط مقابل شوطين في المباراة النهائية بينهما.
وبهذا الفوز، ارتفع إجمالي ألقاب نادال في بطولات الجراند سلام إلى 19 لقبًا، مما جعله يقترب من السويسري روجر فيدرر الذي يحتل المركز الأول برصيد 20 لقبًا، بينما يمتلك الصربي نوفاك دجوكوفيتش 16 لقبًا.
نادال يعتبر الأفضل على الملاعب الترابية بتحقيقه 12 لقبًا في رولان جاروس، وقد توج بأربعة ألقاب في أمريكا المفتوحة، وفاز بلقبين في ويمبلدون وبطولة واحدة في أستراليا.
من ناحية أخرى، يحمل روجر فيدرر الرقم القياسي بفوزه بـ 20 لقبًا في البطولات الأربع الكبرى، بما في ذلك ستة ألقاب في أستراليا المفتوحة، ولقبًا واحدًا في رولان جاروس، وثمانية ألقاب في ويمبلدون.
أما دجوكوفيتش، فهو في المرتبة الثالثة برصيد 16 لقبًا، منها سبعة ألقاب في أستراليا المفتوحة، وثلاثة في أمريكا المفتوحة، ولقبًا واحدًا في رولان جاروس، وأربعة ألقاب في ويمبلدون.
خلال بطولة أمريكا المفتوحة، تعرض دجوكوفيتش لإصابة، مما دفعه إلى إعلان نهاية موسمه الحالي وعدم مشاركته في البطولات القادمة هذا العام.

Laura Deboucher, âgée de vingt-huit ans, était hypermotivée à l'idée de donner son sang. Pourtant, jusqu'à présent, son poids inférieur à 50 kg l'en empêchait, le verdict de la balance étant sans appel. Mais cette fois-ci, elle a enfin pu tendre le bras. Un large sourire illuminait son visage après sa descente de l'estrade où un médecin venait de la consulter. « Ce n'est pourtant pas faute de manger suffisamment ! », affirmait-elle.

Sa maman, Jocelyne, avait partagé leur motivation familiale à participer à cette noble cause. « Mon mari est en attente d'un don des deux poumons, la transplantation devant se faire à Lyon », avait-elle confié. Dans cet élan solidaire, le compagnon de Laura, Jérémy Sarti, à peine plus jeune, était venu également pour donner son sang pour la première fois. Il ne manquait plus qu'Aurélie Miranda De Macedo, la sœur de Laura, pour compléter ce tableau familial exemplaire, tous les quatre figurant sur la photo.

Tout s'est déroulé selon les règles dictées par le protocole sanitaire mis en place par les personnels de l'Établissement français du sang (EFS) basé à Moulins.

LE PARISIEN MAGAZINE. Déjà à la tête de « On n’est pas couché » et des « Grosses Têtes », l’animateur de 54 ans reprend « Les Enfants de la télé » à partir du 3 septembre sur France 2. Sa carrière, la concurrence, l’arrivée de Christine Angot dans son équipe... Il nous raconte tout.

Laurent Ruquier passe beaucoup de temps devant les caméras, mais il déteste manifestement les appareils photo, une aversion presque instinctive. Il est vrai qu’il est difficile de saisir en une seule image ce personnage dynamique. Laurent Ruquier n'existe qu'en mouvement. En photo, il perd de son éclat. À 54 ans, dont trente-cinq passés derrière les micros, il est devenu l'un des visages les plus célèbres du paysage audiovisuel français. Ses jeux de mots en rafale et son rire tonitruant font la joie de YouTube et des archives de l’INA. Cette année, en plus des « Grosses Têtes » sur RTL et de « On n’est pas couché » (« ONPC ») sur France 2, il reprend les rênes des « Enfants de la télé », qui passent de TF1 à la deuxième chaîne. Lors de notre rencontre, mi-juillet, après une séance photo pénible, il répond à toutes nos questions avec précision et sincérité, toujours avec beaucoup d'énergie.

Une rentrée sur tous les fronts

Vous allez animer « Les Enfants de la télé » dès le 3 septembre. Quels sont les changements à attendre par rapport à la version d’Arthur sur TF1 ?
Laurent Ruquier : Retour aux fondamentaux ! L’émission sera centrée sur la télévision. Sur TF1, elle était devenue « les acteurs font leur promo ». Nous choisirons d’autres types d'invités – personnalités de la télé, chanteurs, politiques... – et nous tisserons des liens entre l’histoire du petit écran et l’actualité de la semaine.

Est-on venu vous chercher pour cette émission ?
Non, je me suis porté candidat. D’habitude, j’aime qu’on vienne me chercher, mais là, c’est moi qui ai fait le premier pas car j’adore le concept. Je suis vraiment un enfant de la télé : chez nous, le poste est arrivé en 1963, l’année de ma naissance ! Je n’ai pas besoin de travailler énormément pour connaître l’histoire du petit écran. Quand j’ai appris par la presse – ce n’est pas France 2 qui m’en a informé – que « Les Enfants de la télé » arrivaient, j’ai sauté sur l’occasion. D’autres animateurs étaient envisagés, comme Michel Drucker ou Thomas Thouroude. J’ai dit aux patrons de la chaîne : « S’il y a bien une émission pour laquelle je me sens légitime, c’est celle-là. » En plus, j’avais du temps, car France 2, qui m’avait promis d’autres programmes à la rentrée, n’a pas tenu ses promesses.

Quelles étaient ces promesses ?
La chaîne reconduisait seulement « On n’est pas couché ». Rien pour « Mardi Cinéma » ni pour les « Grosses Têtes » télé... J’ai râlé. Cela m’arrive rarement. Comme je ne suis pas producteur, je ne réclame pas des cases horaires de diffusion. Or, quand on ne demande rien, on n’a rien (rires) ! J’ai dit aux dirigeants de France 2 : « D’autres me font des propositions, et vous, rien ! Vous avez de la chance que je sois encore sous contrat pour un an avec “On n’est pas couché”, sinon je serais déjà parti. »

Pourriez-vous quitter France Télévisions ?
Si je n’étais pas sous contrat, oui.

Le président américain Donald Trump à la Maison Blanche, le 13 octobre 2017 à Washington / AFP.

Donald Trump a annoncé vendredi que les États-Unis ne se retireraient pas de l'accord international sur le nucléaire iranien. Cependant, il a précisé qu'il ne "certifierait" pas que Téhéran respecte ses engagements. Voici les principaux points de son discours :

- Congrès
La "non-certification" des engagements iraniens place, de facto, le Congrès américain en première ligne. Le président américain a ainsi exhorté les parlementaires américains, ainsi que les autres pays signataires de l'accord — Russie, Chine, France, Allemagne, Royaume-Uni — à faire preuve de plus de fermeté vis-à-vis de Téhéran. "J'ordonne à mon administration de collaborer étroitement avec le Congrès et nos alliés pour combler les nombreuses et graves lacunes de l'accord, afin d'empêcher le régime iranien de menacer le monde avec des armes atomiques", a-t-il déclaré.

- Participation annulée à tout moment
En cas d'échec pour trouver une solution, Donald Trump a menacé de mettre fin à l'accord à tout moment. "Dans l'éventualité où nous ne serions pas capables de trouver une solution en travaillant avec le Congrès et nos alliés, alors l'accord prendrait fin. Il est sous examen permanent et notre participation peut être annulée par moi, en tant que président, à tout moment."

- 'L'un des pires' accords
Il a estimé que l'accord visant à empêcher l'Iran de se doter de la bombe atomique est "l'un des pires" qui soit. Avec cet accord, "nous avons obtenu de faibles inspections en échange de rien de plus que de repousser, purement à court terme et temporairement, l'avancée de l'Iran vers l'arme nucléaire. Quel est le sens d'un accord qui ne fait que retarder la capacité nucléaire pour une courte période? Ceci est inacceptable pour le président des États-Unis". Donald Trump a souligné que son administration souhaitait en particulier supprimer les échéances en vertu desquelles les restrictions sur le programme nucléaire pourraient être progressivement levées après 2025.

- 'Dictature iranienne'
L'hôte de la Maison Blanche a dénoncé le comportement de la "dictature iranienne", qu'il considère comme l'un des principaux "soutiens au terrorisme" dans le monde.

Leonard Slatkin, le chef d'orchestre américain, partage ses souvenirs personnels et musicaux avec Benjamin François dans une interview traduite par Xavier Combe. Slatkin se plonge très jeune dans le monde du jazz, qu'il pratique en amateur, et croise la route de nombreux musiciens. Il raconte : "J'ai appris à connaître le jazz très très tôt, parce que je traînais dans les studios d'enregistrement. Il y avait beaucoup de musiciens indépendants qui jouaient pour Frank Sinatra, Nat King Cole, Doris Day... C'étaient de formidables musiciens de jazz, qui jouaient aussi du classique !"

Slatkin se souvient de ses visites fréquentes au Manne-Hole, un club de jazz dirigé par le célèbre batteur Shelly Manne. Ce lieu était un point de rencontre pour tous les grands musiciens de jazz de l'époque. "Lorsque les autres boîtes fermaient vers 1 heure du matin, tous les musiciens s'y retrouvaient, et jusqu'à 6 heures du matin, ils jouaient les uns pour les autres..." ajoute-t-il. Parmi ses souvenirs, il évoque une prestation mémorable de Dave Brubeck avec Miles Davies, qui, bien que n'ayant pas parfaitement fonctionné, était extrêmement intéressante à écouter. Slatkin s'est également lié d'amitié avec André Prévin, un artiste aux talents multiples qui ne cessait de l'étonner.

Le programme musical mentionné inclut une variété d'œuvres marquantes :

- Al Hoffman, Carl Lampl & Jerry Livingston, "Close to you" interprétée par Frank Sinatra et le Quatuor de Hollywood (enregistré en 1956 chez Capitol).

Autonomous driving (AD) is a long-researched area with numerous novel motion planning algorithms proposed. Despite these advancements, AD continues to present significant challenges. Traditional motion planning algorithms typically rely on rule- or optimization-based methods. However, these manually designed rules or models often contain inaccurate assumptions, limiting their scalability to complex real-world scenarios such as overtaking, roundabouts, interactions, and merging. This limitation has driven the exploration of learning-based approaches, promising the automatic learning of complex driving policies through data. Deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is at the forefront of these approaches, combining the perception abilities of deep neural networks (DNN) with the decision-making capabilities of reinforcement learning (RL), and has been widely investigated for AD tasks.

DRL has been successfully applied to various sequential decision-making problems. In the context of AD, a DRL-augmented system processes inputs such as the behaviors of the autonomous vehicle (AV), surrounding human-driven vehicles (HDVs), and road network information, outputting vehicle control commands like steering, torque, and braking. The effectiveness of DRL is contingent on vast amounts of training data and computational resources. However, large-scale human driving data collection can be prohibitively expensive. This challenge means DRL models are still vulnerable to unexpected behavior in out-of-sample scenarios and susceptible to malicious backdoors (also known as "neural Trojans" or "Trojan attacks").

In this paper, we focus on the backdoor threat to DRL-augmented AD systems through manipulation during the training stage. Various existing neural Trojans can infiltrate AV capabilities related to vision perception, such as image classification, object recognition, and tracking. A backdoored DNN behaves normally with benign samples but produces malicious outcomes when an attacker-specified trigger is present in the input. DRL's challenge with backdoors lies in the need to disrupt sequential decisions rather than isolated ones while maintaining performance in the absence of triggers. Consequently, there is limited research in this area. Notable works include those by Kiourti et al., who used image patterns as backdoor triggers, and Ashcraft et al., who examined DRL backdoors using action trajectories as triggers. One study focused specifically on DRL-based AD using vehicle speed and position combinations as triggers. These backdoor triggers are insightful for DRL-based AD, motivating the investigation of stealthier and more practical backdoors that real-world attackers can easily activate.

The DRL agent learns optimal policies through environmental interactions. While most DRL methods assume complete observability of the environment, the occlusions and noisy sensors in AVs result in only partial visibility of the system state. A partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) can better capture the dynamics of the AD environment, but finding an optimal policy for POMDP is notoriously difficult. A common approach is to integrate a recurrent neural network (RNN) or a generative model to uncover hidden states and generate optimal policies. This partial observability can advantageously aid hackers, suggesting that embedding a backdoor trigger in unobservable states can increase stealth.

In this paper, we aim to hide backdoor triggers into spatiotemporal traffic features, crucial for ensuring AD performance. We design a spatiotemporal DNN model for DRL using the gate recurrent unit (GRU) and attention mechanisms to capture features from observations. Our evaluations reveal that these features notably enhance the efficiency and safety of DRL algorithms across different AD tasks. We also examine the security of these features by crafting a backdoor trigger based on the temporal and spatial relevance of a sequence of states, introducing a spatiotemporal-pattern stealthy Trojan attack on DRL-augmented AD systems. This attack enables an attacker to control spatial and temporal dependencies between the AV and an attacker’s vehicle through specific driving behaviors, activating the backdoor. Once triggered, the AV is controlled by backdoor neurons using malicious rewards to dictate actions while keeping the value of these rewards similar to original genuine rewards for stealth.

Votre programmation musicale est inspirée par "Le Gopak. Danse des cosaques zaporogues" d'Ilya Répine. Ce tableau est actuellement exposé au Petit Palais à Paris dans le cadre de l'exposition dédiée à l'artiste (1844-1930).

Ilya Répine occupe une place essentielle dans l'histoire de la peinture russe des XIXe et XXe siècles, étant une figure majeure du monde artistique de son époque. Il s'intéresse à divers domaines culturels tels que la littérature, la musique et les sciences. Proche de personnalités telles que l'écrivain Tolstoï, le compositeur Moussorgski et le collectionneur Trétiakov, Répine est un témoin attentif des bouleversements de la Russie, reflétant les profondes mutations de son pays à travers ses œuvres.

L'exposition "Ilya Répine (1844-1930). Peindre l’âme russe" est présentée au Petit Palais de Paris jusqu'au 23 janvier 2022.

Pour en savoir plus, vous pouvez écouter l'émission "Musicopolis" sur Moussorgski et son opéra "Boris Godounov" pendant 24 minutes. De plus, ne manquez pas le documentaire "Maestro" sur ARTE qui sera diffusé le dimanche 24 octobre à 18h55 et qui sera consacré au violoncelle selon Gautier Capuçon.

Gautier Capuçon, originaire de Chambéry, a complété sa formation au Conservatoire de Paris avant de se produire aux côtés de grands artistes tels que Martha Argerich et Daniel Barenboim sur les scènes internationales. Il entretient une relation fusionnelle avec son violoncelle, un instrument vieux de trois siècles fabriqué par le luthier vénitien Matteo Goffriller en 1701.

رام الله - دنيا الوطن: جرفت آليات الاحتلال الإسرائيلي، اليوم الخميس، أراضٍ زراعية، واقتلعت أشتال كرمة وزيتون في بلدة الخضر جنوب بيت لحم. وأفاد مصدر منسق لجنة مقاومة الجدار والاستيطان في الخضر، أحمد صلاح، بأن آليات الاحتلال، جرفت أراضٍ زراعية بمساحة 5 دونمات، تعود للمواطن إبراهيم محمد موسى، واقتلعت عدداً من أشتال الكرمة والزيتون، في منطقة "خلة ظهر العين"، الواقعة بين مستوطنتي (دانيال) و(اليعازر) الجاثمتين على أراضي المواطنين في البلدة.وأشار صلاح إلى أن هذا التجريف ليس الأول من نوعه في المنطقة ذاتها، حيث شهدت في الفترة الأخيرة، هجمة من قبل المستوطنين، وتحت حماية قوات الاحتلال، وذلك لأطماع استيطانية. وأوضح المصدر أن قوات الاحتلال، أزالت عدداً من الوحدات الاستيطانية التي أقامها المستوطنون في المنطقة المذكورة، عندما انتزع المواطن موسى قراراً بإزالتها.
