Bianca Buitendag is one of those surfers who exudes zen-like calm and looks at one with the ocean, but qualifying for the Tokyo Olympics has left the South African completely “overwhelmed.” The graceful 25-year-old secured a provisional spot for next year’s Olympics at the World Surfing Games in Miyazaki over the weekend, an emotional release after enduring a rollercoaster of emotions in recent years.

Buitendag’s journey to the Olympics is remarkable, having faced significant challenges since 2015 when her surfer dad, Colin, passed away. Despite this, she achieved a career-best fourth in the world rankings with runner-up finishes in Rio, Fiji, and California. However, she has struggled to replicate that form in the years since.

Now, Buitendag is daring to dream after claiming a continental berth for Tokyo 2020 alongside Japan’s Shino Matsuda, Israeli Anat Lelior, and Ella Williams of New Zealand. “It’s going to take a while to really understand the magnitude of the opportunity,” Buitendag told AFP in an interview. “It’s a bit overwhelming really, the whole idea of being in the Olympics,” she added. “It’s so bizarre. We grew up watching it on TV. My family doesn’t understand any result I have — but the Olympics is a universal word that everyone understands, so they understood that.”

When surfing makes its first Olympic appearance at Tokyo 2020, Buitendag will not be short of support. “It’s a once-in-a-lifetime chance,” she said. “My family have already decided they’re going to fly over, so I’ve got to cater for about 20 people — my mum is a big sports fan; she probably won’t even watch the surfing, she’ll just head to the track.”

Reflecting on the prospect of marching behind her country’s flag at the opening ceremony, Buitendag admitted, “I just have no idea what to expect. I’m doing my best to kind of formulate an idea in my head, but I know it’s not going to come close to when it actually happens, my dear.” She added, “If you knew how special my country is to me, from what circumstances we’ve come and what realities we represent, you’ll start to understand how proud I’ll be walking out there. I think I’ll be in pieces.”

Growing up near False Bay, outside of Cape Town, a notorious hunting ground for great white sharks, Buitendag recalls being more frightened of big waves as a junior surfer. “I guess you just naturally evolve past the fear,” she smiled. “But we don’t mind the sharks — (attacks) happen occasionally, but it’s worth the risk.”

As she looks forward to the Olympics, Buitendag does admit to some trepidation about the conditions that await surfers in Japan. South Africa is known for its classic surf breaks, but the smaller waves in Japan could throw the Olympic competition wide open. “There are no magazine shots,” smiled the former rookie of the year, referring to the giant rollers seen in Tahiti or Hawaii. “It’s a different type of surfing, more technical. When the waves are small and tricky, it’s a more open field.

فنون - كتب أمير التهامي يوم الثلاثاء 13 يوليو 2021 الساعة 04:09 صباحًا - أفاد محمد رمسيس عروب، رئيس مجلس الإدارة والرئيس التنفيذي لشركة الوفاء للتأمين، بأن "قيمة صناعة التأمين في إفريقيا تُقدّر حاليًا بنحو 68 مليار دولار، ومن المتوقع أن تنمو أكثر من ذلك، خاصة في منطقة شمال إفريقيا، التي تُعد ثاني أكبر سوق بعد جنوب إفريقيا. وتأتي مصر في مقدمة الأسواق التي نركز عليها حاليًا لتقديم خدمة متميزة لعملائنا في الأسواق المستهدفة."

وفي أغسطس 2020، منحت هيئة الرقابة المالية ترخيصًا للشركة للعمل في مجال التأمين والفروع الطبية المختلفة وبرامجها طويلة الأجل، حسب بيان أصدرته الشركة يوم الاثنين.

صرحت عبير صالح، الرئيس التنفيذي لشركة الوفاء لتأمينات الحياة في مصر، أن الشركة تأسست برأس مال يصل إلى 150 مليون جنيه مصري، وأنها تعتزم تقديم خدمات متميزة وتجربة عملاء متطورة، مما سيساهم في نمو الصناعة بشكل جذري من خلال القوة المالية للشركة ومزاياها التنافسية. وأضافت أن الشركة حصلت على موافقة الهيئة العامة للرقابة المالية لإتاحة 6 منتجات جديدة في السوق المصري.

تتواجد شركة الوفاء للتأمين حاليًا في 6 دول إفريقية من خلال 10 شركات، وهذا التواجد يتيح للشركة تغطية 39٪ من إجمالي سوق التأمين الإفريقي باستثناء جنوب إفريقيا، وتسعى الشركة لتحقيق معدل تغطية يصل إلى 65٪ بحلول عام 2025، من خلال تأسيس مزيد من الشركات في 10 دول إفريقية أخرى.

Advancements in technology are shaping the future of the 21st century. Every day, improvements are made across various domains, including phones, cars, and home systems. Among these, the development of driverless cars stands out as a significant leap toward a more advanced technological future.

The production of driverless cars is already underway, driven by companies like Google, which see it as a means to push the boundaries of current technology. Halting the development of these vehicles would impede technological progress. Notably, there have been no reports of accidents that would suggest driverless cars pose a danger to drivers, passengers, or pedestrians, although they are not yet fully autonomous, and testing continues to enhance their safety features.

Driverless cars, however, are not without their risks, particularly concerning the potential dangers of alerting drivers. To mitigate these, the cars are equipped with built-in alert systems, such as seat vibrations and flashing lights, to inform the driver when human intervention is needed. While these safety measures are not perfect, the technology will continue to improve with ongoing usage and development.

One of the most significant benefits of the development of driverless cars is the potential for substantial economic gain.

Robotic platforms rely heavily on dynamics models for tasks such as object manipulation, motion planning, and control. A robust dynamics model is crucial for executing trajectories accurately while maintaining compliance. Traditionally, inverse dynamics models were computed using rigid body dynamics equations. However, modern systems face challenges with these approaches due to the reliance on noisy sensor data, leading to inaccuracies when models are computed analytically. Additionally, unmodeled effects such as manufacturing uncertainties, wear and tear, and friction further contribute to potential inaccuracies and undesirable behavior.

To address these issues, non-parametric models offer a data-driven approach that allows for learning non-linear functions encompassing all forces within robot dynamics. Here, the problem is framed as a mapping function from input states to output torque. Various regression methods have been successfully utilized for learning inverse dynamics models, including Gaussian processes (GPs) and neural networks (NNs).

Gaussian processes provide accurate predictions with uncertainty estimation through their covariance functions. However, they suffer from computational challenges; their complexity scales exponentially (O(n³)) with the number of training data points, and they have quadratic space complexity. To overcome these limitations, methods like local Gaussian process regression (GPR), sparse GP regression, and drifting GPs have been developed. Despite these advancements, such methods still scale quadratically with the samples (O(n²)), limiting them to a few thousand samples.

Neural networks are proficient at approximating non-linear functions and come with a time complexity of O(n), making them inherently efficient. However, standard deep models lack the ability to represent prediction uncertainty.

The success of deep generative models is rapidly permeating both industry and academia. In contemporary game development, these models are increasingly aiding in the creation of various assets, including graphics, sounds, character motions, dialogues, landscapes, and level designs. For example, the Game Developers Conference 2021 featured a special session titled "Machine Learning Summit," showcasing various deep generative models used in game production. These included models for generating character motions that align with conversation content (Ding 2021) and for creating 3D facial expression models of characters from human face images (Li 2021).

Despite the progress, deep generative models for rhythm-based actions have largely been explored only as proof of concept or for personal hobby projects, and not yet widely adopted in leading commercial products. This raises several questions, such as what hinders the adoption of chart generation models in the gaming industry and how these barriers can be overcome.

A key issue identified in this article is musical structure recognition. Our model considers features like beats and temporal scales (see Section 2.1 for more on musical structures). While existing models lack components dedicated to these aspects, our model incorporates them, processing beats and multiple temporal scales through what we call the beat guide and multi-scale conv-stack, respectively.

The beat guide is a noteworthy technique due to its ability to be computed straightforwardly for any input audio. Surprisingly, it has been overlooked in previous works. The multi-scale conv-stack is designed to capture musical features across different time scales, such as repetitions and notes of varying lengths.

We conducted a comprehensive evaluation of this improved model, utilizing both supercomputing resources and user feedback from our application within a gaming company. The benchmarks demonstrate that our model surpasses the state-of-the-art Dance Dance Convolution model (Donahue, Lipton, and McAuley 2017). Business feedback (see Section 6) indicates that our model effectively replaces the manual effort of creating initial drafts, a task typically dependent on managerial decisions for refinement. Our model, named GenéLive!, cuts business costs by half and remains in active use. To conduct this study, we collaborated with the game artists at KLab Inc., a Japan-based video game developer, which employs some of the authors. The company operates three rhythm action game titles online, including the particularly successful "Love Live! School Idol Festival All Stars," or simply "Love Live! All Stars" (Fig. 1). This game has been released in six languages and has attracted over 10 million users worldwide. The relevance of our work extends to a broad audience, given the competitive landscape of games with similar impact.

Our primary focus is the generation of charts, which instruct players to tap or flick buttons at specific moments—a defining challenge of rhythm action games. These buttons, known as notes, fly across the screen in a spatial pattern akin to a musical score, while the background audio, or song, plays.

A chart generation model consists of two submodels: the onset model, which determines the timing of a note, and the sym model, which decides the user action type (e.g., tap or flick). Since timing is the bottleneck in KLab's workflow (detailed in Section 2.3), this article emphasizes our onset model. The contributions of this work include:

- Artists at KLab confirm that the musical structure is common to nearly all songs in their rhythm action games and is a critical aspect of chart creation. Specifically, artists often place identical note patterns on repeated phrases. For more on the musical structure of "Sweet Eyes" and the note placement by artists, refer to Appendix H.

To capture temporal patterns with our generative model, it is essential to consider multiple time scales, a feature absent in the network design of the DDC. For details on how our model captures these features, see the explanations of the beat guide (Section 4.3) and multi-scale conv-stack (Section 4.4).

COLUMBIA (WBTW) – The South Carolina High School League unanimously approved the starting dates for the winter sports seasons this morning. High school boys and girls basketball are set to commence practice on November 2nd, with teams allowed to engage in two scrimmages before the regular season kicks off on November 30th. Just like football, the playoffs will be condensed to four rounds, heightening the importance of regional play every night. Attendance is anticipated to be restricted, with social distancing guidelines still in effect and masks required for everyone inside.

High school wrestling will be permitted to start practice on November 9th, while the first matches are scheduled to begin on December 14th.

The SCHSL is currently in the process of securing venues for the football and cheerleading finals in December. Williams-Brice Stadium and Benedict College in Columbia have traditionally hosted the finals, but will not do so this season due to COVID-19.

Las instalaciones de la Finca de Briz acogieron ayer una nueva reunión de la Mesa de Trabajo Contra la Violencia de Género, en la que participaron la concejala de Igualdad, Marián Sanmartín, y representantes del CIM de Marín, de Servicios Sociales y de la policía.

Según los datos expuestos en la mesa, actualmente el ayuntamiento cuenta con 29 casos activos de violencia de género, concentrados principalmente en el rango de edad de 30 a 45 años. Aunque ninguno de estos casos está catalogado como de alto riesgo, tres de ellos se consideran de riesgo medio. Los participantes en la reunión analizaron estos datos, que "siguen evidenciando esta lacra en nuestra sociedad contra la que tenemos que seguir luchando con medidas, recursos y concienciación ciudadana", aseguró la concejala.

Sanmartín quiso destacar cómo se mantuvo todo ese trabajo durante la pandemia, agradeciendo la labor de todos los organismos representados en la Mesa: "Siempre realizan un trabajo muy importante, pero especialmente durante esta época tan compleja, en la que no se paró, sino todo lo contrario".

De hecho, el Punto de Intercambio Familiar siguió funcionando durante todo el confinamiento en los casos en los que se demandó el servicio, atendiendo actualmente a 9 núcleos familiares.

Además, la edil hizo hincapié en el contacto estrecho que se mantiene entre todos los organismos implicados: el CIM de Marín, el departamento de Servicios Sociales, la Policía Nacional, la Policía Local y la Unidad de Violencia de Género de la Subdelegación del Gobierno en Pontevedra.

Thomas reflected on the series of improbable events that had unfolded in his life: from the fire sparked by a malfunctioning pilot light in his home, to the bizarre encounter with man-eating fireflies in the woods, and the raids by refrigerator thieves and poachers armed with banana-sized rocket launchers. It seemed miraculous that he had survived, as if he were a protagonist in a story with a unique purpose—though what that purpose was, he had no idea, nor had he ever been informed.

Standing atop the rooftop of his office tower, the wind whipped his worn, tattered jacket back, making him feel like a hero in a triumphant pose. He felt invincible. Running his fingers through his hair, he leapt, gliding like a sugar glider, and landed gracefully on a nearby building. The thought crossed his mind, "This is incredible, oh my god, I am such a hotshot."

With a flourish, he pressed the crosswalk button, a futile gesture, to get a coffee from the attractive barista, the one who usually wore a green apron, a turtleneck, and, he imagined, nothing else.

牛津经济研究院预测，即便北京政府推出更多刺激措施，中国经济增速可能在今年第四季度放缓至5.7%，并在明年基本维持这一水平。

据香港信报财经网报道，牛津经济研究院首席亚洲经济学家路易斯·奎伊斯（Louis Kuijs）在一份报告中指出，自去年底以来实施的政策宽松虽有助于缓解经济放缓，但效果有限。由于中国经济减速、中美摩擦及全球贸易疲软，进一步放松政策显得尤为重要，以有效稳定经济增长。

报告提到，相较于以往侧重于基础设施和住房支出的政策，本次财政刺激方案包括约2万亿元人民币的减税措施，但对国内外增长的乘数效应减弱。随着经济放缓及贸易战升级，信贷需求依然疲弱，但政策制定者仍不愿过度推动信贷增长。

报告还指出，尽管预计中国经济增速将趋于稳定，但这一稳定出现的时间将晚于之前的预期，并且增速可能更低。主要的下行风险在于决策者没有充分强化政策宽松的力度。

The practical success of deep learning is evident across various applications such as image recognition [27], speech recognition [23], and others [21, 44]. Despite numerous recent advancements, the empirical triumph of deep learning still surpasses the development of a solid theoretical understanding of the optimization process. Specifically, the question of how and when deep learning algorithms generalize effectively remains unanswered. This challenge is rooted in the nonlinear and intricate structure of these networks, which are highly non-convex functions with millions of parameters.

Furthermore, the current practice of designing these networks for specific applications primarily relies on trial and error.

In this paper, we establish Cramér-Rao (CR) type lower bounds [42, 10] on the generalization error of these networks when the training data is noisy. These bounds can offer valuable insights into the design and assessment of learning algorithms. Our analysis is inspired by the application of CR bounds in engineering as a performance benchmark, as seen in [47, 15] and related works, and as a guiding principle for enhancing experimental design. To compute the CR bounds, we merge tools from statistical estimation theory and random matrix theory. Our analysis is versatile and can be extended to various learning tasks and architectures.

Our key discoveries are as follows. We present lower bounds for general estimators and assess them using random matrix theory for linear models and feed-forward neural networks. We demonstrate the tightness of the bounds for a two-layer neural network with a linear activation function. Additionally, as a comparison, we offer a lower bound on the generalization error for unbiased estimators in nonlinear models, based on the classical CR bound. This bound is the ratio of the expected rank of the Fisher information matrix to the number of samples, multiplied by the noise variance. We illustrate the significance of the expected rank of the Fisher information matrix in the high-dimensional space of the standard nonlinear network architectures, affirming the necessity of the bias in the learning algorithms of the successful nonlinear networks in the high-dimensional context.

The randomness inherent in human-driving behavior creates instability within the traffic system, contributing significantly to shockwaves and stop-and-go patterns. These phenomena have become primary safety concerns and the main causes of traffic jams. Moreover, human drivers strive to maximize travel efficiency by improving average speed and minimizing headway. Consequently, a critical question for developing an intelligent car-following system is how to encourage vehicles to travel as fast as possible while maintaining safe and efficient headway to the leading vehicle and reducing shockwaves.

Car-following is a fundamental driving task that has spurred the development of numerous models aimed at mimicking human driving behavior. In traffic flow theory, classic Car-Following Models (CFMs) are rooted in physical knowledge and human behaviors. For instance, the Gipps model considers both free-flow mode (without a leading vehicle) and car-following mode (with a leading vehicle), using the minimum velocity of the two modes to decide on acceleration or deceleration. The following vehicle's speed is also constrained by safety considerations. Another well-known model, the Intelligent Driver Model (IDM), determines the output acceleration based on desired velocity, headway, relative velocity, and distance to the leading vehicle.

In recent years, data-driven methods have been proposed to train CFMs. He et al. utilized K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) to deduce the most likely behavior of vehicles in the car-following mode. Other studies have applied supervised learning; for example, Chong et al. used Neural Networks (NN) to model driver behavior in terms of longitudinal and lateral actions, while Zhou et al. employed Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) to capture and predict traffic oscillations. Although supervised learning methods have shown promising results, they require hand-collected microscopic car-following data, which are rare and expensive to acquire. The data collected typically originate from human drivers, and learning methodologies such as Imitation Learning might lead trained models to adopt irrational behaviors, such as overly aggressive or conservative patterns.

Autonomous driving technology has been extensively studied and is becoming a reality with the advancement of sensors and Artificial Intelligence (AI). Autonomous vehicles have the potential to outperform human driving in terms of safety and comfort. One significant advantage of Connected and Autonomous Vehicles (CAVs) is their ability to substantially reduce randomness in driving behavior, allowing the entire system to be better managed by control algorithms with minimal reaction time.

Recent research has seen the rapid maturation of Reinforcement Learning (RL) applications. RL has effectively addressed problems in areas such as Go and Atari games. Within this framework, RL agents interact with the environment, observing states and receiving corresponding rewards. They aim to discover optimal policies that maximize accumulated rewards. A well-defined reward function typically ensures that an agent's policy converges to the desired objective. For example, Zhu et al. defined CFMs to maintain safe distances to the front vehicle while achieving desired speeds, and their model demonstrated strong generalization compared to data-driven CFM.

In our study, we focus on extending the Bidirectional Car-Following Model (BCM) into a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) framework to address the multi-objective problem of optimizing efficiency, safety, comfort, and traffic stability. Our experimental results reveal that our proposed bidirectional DRL CFM surpasses previous human driving models in terms of inter-vehicle headways, average speed, jerk, safety, and string stability.

Every night, when the clock strikes midnight, time halts for everyone except me. It's just me and my watch. I remember missing a couple of classes before realizing that my watch was consistently running an hour ahead each day. Yet, I couldn't overlook the frozen raindrops in mid-air and the profound stillness of a motionless world, punctuated only by the gentle ticking of my watch.

Do you recall that game where you pick a superpower? Most choose flying, reading minds, or turning invisible (the pervy option). For me, it was always about being able to freeze time. I perpetually felt short on time and dreamt of the ability to pause it to complete tasks, ace exams, nap, or craft the perfect comeback during conversations. Despite countless wishes and experiments, I couldn't quite master this time-stopping power. All I had was an additional hour each day, which was quite satisfactory.

If you've been a student, you know that money is often in short supply. Admittedly, the prospect of time freezing while I was tipsy in a crowded club proved too tempting for my meager wallet. Initially, I borrowed a few drinks to pass the time while I waited. Gradually, I escalated to discreetly pilfering wallets and skimming off small amounts of cash from unsuspecting patrons.

After a guilt-ridden episode of relieving random students of their spare change at a local bar, I decided to target those who wouldn't miss the money. If I was going to pilfer, I might as well do it right and profit more from the heist. All that remained was selecting the perfect mark.

A swift online search revealed that a midnight art exhibit was taking place at the local theater on Friday. I deduced it would attract affluent attendees with bulging wallets full of cash they probably wouldn't notice missing. So, my plan was to lurk in a nearby bar until midnight, discreetly relieve the well-off patrons of some cash, and retreat to the bar before 1 a.m.

The scheme unfolded seamlessly. By 1 a.m., I was back at the bar, resetting my watch to midnight, and pocketing a wad of cash. I shared a sly smile with the bartender, who seemed intrigued, considering my earlier penny-pinching payments. I tipped generously, earning her favor.

In the subsequent weeks, I established a routine: studying and catching up on sleep midweek, reveling in drinks at the bar opposite the theater on Fridays, and discreetly snatching cash from the theatergoers during the twenty-fifth hour. Gradually, I amassed a substantial sum under my bed to offset my student loans, and even the bartender seemed to warm up to me. To avoid raising suspicion, I refrained from depositing large amounts of cash in my bank account, but I relished the luxuries my illicit earnings afforded me.

However, this carefree existence couldn't last forever. One ordinary Friday night, something unexpected unfolded during the twenty-fifth hour at the theater.

As I traversed the aisles, greeting the familiar faces of patrons, I noticed the distinguished Waistcoat and Big Hat duo seated at the front, indicating they must have booked tickets in advance. I proceeded to deftly extract cash from Waistcoat's jacket pocket, expressing my gratitude audibly in the eerie silence of the auditorium.

Midway through the act, a faint noise to my left startled me, prompting a quick glance at my watch - it was only five past midnight, ample time left. Perplexed, I strained to detect any sound beyond the rhythmic ticking of my watch.

Despite my unease, I resumed my routine, but an inexplicable sense of being observed nagged at me. Whether from the motionless gaze of the frozen audience or the stillness of that timeless hour, a creeping anxiety took hold.

After relieving a couple more patrons of their cash, I decided to call it a night prematurely, feeling a chill as I hastily returned the wallets and headed towards the exit. A subtle noise, 'Tick, Tick,' made me whirl around, but the theater remained deserted. Glancing at my watch – 12:35 – reassured me that no one could be stirring yet. Bundling up against the cold, I hastened out of the theater, my senses on edge.

Crossing the road to the pub, I cast furtive glances towards the theater, sensing an unsettling presence. As I entered the bar, I removed my coat and settled down, meticulously restoring every item to its original place before time resumed. Lifting my glass, I downed a generous measure of whisky, determined to level out the excess before the twenty-fifth hour concluded. Glancing at my watch – 12:42 – I prepared to bide my time with a book, only to freeze at the sight before me.

As I stared at my motionless watch, its hands locked in time, a haunting 'Tick, tick, tick,' reverberated behind me.

I'd love to pen more, but time is slipping away (ironic, I know) as I must head out now.

A sheriff on Thursday urged a man sought in the killing of a deputy to turn himself in and warned the community to stay vigilant during a manhunt. This tragic event is believed to be the first slaying of a law enforcement officer in Maine in nearly 30 years.

The fatal shooting of Somerset County Cpl. Eugene Cole on Wednesday in Norridgewock triggered an intensive search for 29-year-old John Williams in and around the heavily wooded rural community located about 60 miles (96 kilometers) west of Bangor.

Somerset County Sheriff Dale Lancaster, speaking at a news conference, directly addressed Williams, urging him to turn himself in, as authorities have had no contact with him since the incident. Williams, from Madison, Maine, was scheduled to appear in court on Wednesday to face gun charges when he committed the heinous act of killing Cole, stealing his cruiser, and robbing a convenience store.

Authorities advised residents to secure their doors and cars, with officers assigned to protect local schools. They believe Williams is still in the vicinity.

Lancaster stated that 175 to 200 officers from various agencies, including the FBI, have been tirelessly working on the case, with additional support from law enforcement in Massachusetts and New Hampshire.

State Police Lt. Col. John Cote appealed to the public for assistance and emphasized the safe return of Williams, as he is the key to providing answers to their questions.

Helicopters, armored vehicles, and police cruisers were deployed around Norridgewock, with schools placed on lockdown as federal, state, and local law enforcement converged on the area in search of Williams, who has previous arrest records in Maine, Tennessee, and Massachusetts.

This stark reality stands in contrast to Williams' high school days at Skowhegan High School, where a yearbook photo showed him as a former class officer.

(Boursier.com) — Air Liquide et Faurecia ont signé un accord de développement conjoint visant à concevoir et produire des systèmes de réservoirs embarqués d'hydrogène liquide pour l'industrie automobile. Ce partenariat technologique permettra d'accélérer le déploiement de la mobilité zéro-émission des poids lourds.

Les réservoirs d'hydrogène liquide pour les véhicules à pile à combustible, particulièrement adaptés aux longues distances, jouent un rôle clé dans l'accélération de la transition vers la neutralité carbone. Cette technologie double la capacité de stockage d'hydrogène embarqué par rapport à la quantité stockée sous forme gazeuse, offrant ainsi aux camions deux fois plus d'autonomie. De plus, les véhicules bénéficient d'un temps de rechargement rapide et d'une charge utile inchangée.

Ce partenariat capitalise sur les compétences respectives des deux entreprises dans leurs domaines d'expertise. Air Liquide apporte son savoir-faire reconnu sur toute la chaîne de valeur de l'hydrogène liquide, incluant la cryogénie extrême, les technologies de stockage, les interfaces de rechargement et une connaissance approfondie des infrastructures. Faurecia contribue avec son expertise dans les architectures et l'intégration de systèmes, ses compétences en tests et simulations, son expérience dans l'industrie automobile mondiale, et ses relations avec les constructeurs de véhicules.

Benoît Potier, PDG d'Air Liquide, a déclaré : "Il existe une réelle dynamique autour de l'hydrogène qui suscite un intérêt mondial. Dans ce contexte, des acteurs issus de secteurs très différents s'associent pour développer le potentiel de l'hydrogène. Notre partenariat avec un leader mondial comme Faurecia s'inscrit dans cette démarche. Il vise à accélérer le développement de la mobilité hydrogène en se concentrant sur le marché des poids lourds, pour lequel l'hydrogène est particulièrement adapté".

Patrick Koller, PDG de Faurecia, a ajouté : "Ce partenariat est le premier jalon d'une grande aventure avec Air Liquide, entreprise de premier plan dans le secteur de l'hydrogène".

Ce jeudi 3 octobre, C8 a diffusé "Monsieur Aznavour", une émission spéciale présentée par Cyril Hanouna en hommage au chanteur disparu en octobre 2018. Parmi les nombreux invités venus se souvenir de Charles Aznavour se trouvait Jean-Rachid Kallouche, le mari de Katia Aznavour. Interrogé par le présentateur sur l’homme qu’était l’interprète de "J’me voyais déjà", son beau-fils a répondu : "Il avait toujours des projets énormes, il n’arrêtait jamais. Il pouvait écrire un livre tout en composant trois ou quatre chansons en parallèle. Il me disait : « Dans la vie, il faut avoir des projets, sinon cela ne sert à rien »."

Cyril Hanouna l’a ensuite questionné : "Charles vous a-t-il accepté tout de suite ?" "C’est un fils d’immigré et moi, je suis d’origine algérienne, donc cela nous a rapprochés", a expliqué son gendre, Jean-Rachid Kallouche. L'animateur, qui connaît très bien son invité puisqu’ils sont amis de longue date, s’est alors permis d’aller plus loin dans ses questions : "Je ne te l’ai jamais demandé, mais moi, j’aurais été extrêmement stressé le jour où j’aurais rencontré mon beau-père, surtout sachant que c’est Charles Aznavour." Avec humour, il a ajouté qu’il aurait même répété toutes ses chansons avant de rencontrer une telle légende.

أكد محمد بن مسعود من الدمام أن نقل العدوى في المرحلة السابعة يكون مرتفعًا بسبب فاشيات مجتمعية. كشف الباحث في الفيروسات، الدكتور بندر العصيمي، تفاصيل ارتفاع معدلات الإصابة بفيروس كورونا في المملكة والأسباب وراء ذلك.

في التفاصيل، أوضح الباحث خلال برنامج "mbc في أسبوع": نحن في المرحلة السابعة، وبزيادة طفيفة عن معدل انتشار كورونا في المملكة بمعدل R0=1، وهو قدرة شخص واحد على نقل العدوى لعدة أشخاص بفيروس كورونا. فإذا نقل شخص العدوى لشخص واحد فقط، يصبح R0=1، وهكذا كما حدث الأسبوع الماضي حيث كنا قريبين من تسجيل عدوى واحدة لشخص واحد بنسبة 1.04 تمامًا كما كانت في المرحلة السادسة التي انتهت في 6 إبريل.

والآن، للأسف، ارتفع المعدل إلى 1.3 نتيجة لارتفاع فاشيات مجتمعية، خاصة في مكة المكرمة والمدينة المنورة، حيث أدى ذلك إلى إغلاق 6 أحياء. وأضاف: بعد صدور الأمر السامي الكريم بعلاج جميع المواطنين والمقيمين، بما في ذلك مخالفي أنظمة الإقامة، في المستشفيات الحكومية والخاصة، وبدون مسألة قانونية أو ملاحقة مالية، نشكر خادم الحرمين الشريفين وولي عهده - حفظهما الله - على هذه المبادرة الكريمة والإنسانية التي خدمت المواطنين والمقيمين لاحتواء الوباء والسيطرة عليه.

وأشار إلى أننا لا زلنا في مرحلة الانتشار، ولكن بنسبة طفيفة، وليس تزايدًا كبيرًا، وهي مرحلة طبيعية في الاحتواء.

Arthur Bourlet succumbed to injuries sustained in an incident in Isham, near Kettering, as reported by a recent investigation. The report concluded that police officers were not responsible for the cyclist's death, which occurred during a high-speed chase involving a burglar. Earlier this year, Gary Lynch was sentenced after police pursued him in a stolen 4x4 across Northamptonshire on April 11.

The police managed to corner Lynch in Isham, but he reversed the vehicle, striking 75-year-old Arthur Bourlet, who passed away three weeks later. According to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), the police could not have "foreseen the presence of the cyclist" in the village.

During the pursuit, Lynch, 55, collided with police vehicles, severely damaging one beyond repair. When forced into Isham, he reversed at high speed, hitting Mr. Bourlet. Lynch, who had no fixed address, was eventually apprehended after a police BMW halted his vehicle by striking the driver's side.

Mr. Bourlet, a resident of Burton Latimer, was airlifted to University Hospital Coventry, where he was pronounced dead on May 3. The IOPC stated that there was "no evidence that the officers could reasonably have been expected to foresee the presence of the cyclist." They also acknowledged that "officers had been conscientious in providing the cyclist with medical care."

The Internet of Everything is a crucial application scenario for future 6G communication systems, which generally demand extensive spectrum resources. Over-the-air computation (AirComp) is considered a promising solution to the issue of limited spectrum availability. AirComp technology allows the concurrent transmission of multiple nodes. Instead of treating signals from other nodes as noise, it leverages the signal superposition property of cochannels to compute a class of nomographic functions, such as the weighted sum and arithmetic mean, of distributed sensing data, thereby enhancing the efficiency of wireless communication systems.

The concept of AirComp originated from studies on computation functions in multiple-access channels. Subsequently, extensive research has investigated the AirComp system from various perspectives, including signal alignment, power control, and beamforming design, all assuming perfect channel state information (CSI). In practice, however, channel estimation can be imperfect due to factors such as noise. Consequently, some studies have designed AirComp transmission schemes that incorporate a channel estimation procedure. For instance, researchers have proposed a two-stage architecture: in the first stage, the fusion center obtains the sum channel gain from the reference signal from sensors, and in the second stage, the estimated CSI is used for data transmission. Another approach involves sensors using pilot signals broadcast by the fusion center to obtain local CSI, followed by a low-overhead CSI feedback algorithm. Additionally, the impact of imperfect CSI on computation accuracy has been analyzed, leading to a transceiver design based on the statistical error of channel estimation.

In the aforementioned works, channel estimation and data transmission occur in separate phases, which can incur signaling overhead. Moreover, existing studies have typically based their transmission mechanisms on orthogonal frequency division multiplexing waveforms or examined the AirComp system in static scenarios, neglecting the impact of multipath effects and Doppler shifts. In high-mobility scenarios (e.g., involving vehicular or drone-based fusion centers), the channel becomes time-frequency doubly-selective, rendering traditional schemes ineffective.

For reliable communication over time-frequency doubly-selective channels, orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS), a recently proposed two-dimensional (2D) multi-carrier modulation technique, is a promising candidate. OTFS modulates information symbols in the Delay-Doppler (DD) domain and maps each symbol to the entire time-frequency (TF) domain through 2D transformation, harnessing full TF diversity. Furthermore, it converts the complex time-varying channel in the TF domain into a sparse and stable channel in the DD domain, facilitating improved channel estimation and equalization. To the authors' knowledge, the application of OTFS signaling to the AirComp system has not yet been explored in the literature.

Inspired by the above discussions, this paper proposes an AirComp system based on the OTFS waveform, which includes multiple sensors with dual radar and communication functions and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) as an access point (AP). Specifically, leveraging the advantages of dual-function sensors, we introduce a novel transmission scheme along with a frame structure. In this scheme, CSI estimation no longer requires a separate phase; instead, sensors use the echo from the AP to assist in CSI estimation. This implementation significantly reduces signaling overhead and enhances system efficiency.

The estimated CSI from the current frame is utilized to design a precoding matrix for the next frame, mitigating the effects of the time-frequency doubly-selective channel. By accounting for errors in the estimated CSI and those caused by outdated CSI, we propose a robust precoding design based on the statistical characteristics of these errors. Our numerical results demonstrate that the developed robust precoder outperforms the non-robust version, particularly in high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) scenarios, underscoring the importance of incorporating imperfect CSI.

**Returned Afghans on the Run**

According to data from The Refugee Aid (Flykningehjelpen), seven out of ten refugees who have returned to Afghanistan have been forced to flee their homes once more. The organization conducted a survey in Afghanistan involving 1,161 returned refugees, revealing that 72% of them have had to escape from their homes at least twice. Additionally, 27% of respondents reported having to flee three times.

"The findings in our report should compel European countries and Afghanistan's neighbors to halt deportations and reevaluate their policies," says Secretary General Jan Egeland. He believes this is not the time to return Afghans.

Egeland maintains that war-torn Afghanistan is currently unsuitable for returnees, noting that conditions have recently deteriorated throughout the country. In the past two years, more than one million Afghans have been displaced from their homes, a figure that has tripled in less than five years.

Statistics from the Police Immigration Unit indicate that a total of 238 people were forcibly returned from Norway to Afghanistan in 2017, with voluntary returns adding to this number.

تزايد القلق الإسرائيلي من مرحلة ما بعد سقوط نظام بشار الأسد يتجلى في التجسس على الثورة السورية ومراقبة ما يجري من تحركات على الأرض السورية. وكشفت صحيفة "صنداي تايمز" البريطانية عن استخدام إسرائيل لصخور وهمية على ضفاف ميناء طرطوس السوري لزرع معدات تجسس، اكتشفتها مؤخراً قوات النظام السوري. تمكنت هذه المعدات من مراقبة الأسطول البحري الروسي في المنطقة، حيث يُعتقد أنها نقلت تسجيلات بالفيديو لإسرائيل عبر الأقمار الصناعية.

وتفاصيل هذه العمليات تشير إلى أن صيادي أسماك سوريين اكتشفوا الصخور المزوّدة بالمعدات، وأبلغوا عنها قوات النظام. ووفقاً للصحيفة، تم العثور على الصخور المزيفة بالقرب من جزيرة غير مأهولة قرب ميناء طرطوس. يبدو أن قوات كوماندوز إسرائيلية زارت الجزيرة للحصول على عينات من تربتها وصخورها الحقيقية، مستخدمةً قوارب منفوخة بالهواء مع محركات صامتة للوصول إليها ليلاً.

ورغم الجهود البريطانية والأمريكية في مراقبة المنطقة، تمكنت القوات الإسرائيلية من الإفلات من مركز مراقبة بريطاني في قبرص ومن دوريات الأسطول الأمريكي السادس في البحر الأبيض المتوسط. ويُعتقد أن التجسس كان يهدف لمراقبة الأسطول الروسي الذي يعدّ دعماً كبيراً للنظام السوري في مواجهة الثورة الشعبية.

تأتي هذه المعلومات وسط تصاعد القلق الإسرائيلي من مرحلة ما بعد الأسد، مع اقتراحات لإقامة منطقة أمنية عازلة في مرتفعات الجولان خوفاً من ضربات محتملة من مقاتلين سوريين عبر الجولان.

Police Chief Petunia was stumped. He cradled his soy milk half-caf delicately in his manicured fingers, furrowed his brow, and then tore the lid off a sugar dispenser filled with low-calorie artificial sweetener labeled "organic." He poured the majority of the contents into his drink, which immediately crystallized into a viscous sludge. "When I first joined the force these kids meant business. They were up in arms, sticking rose petals in carbines or sitting at the counter of Woolworth's…sinisterly…just waiting for a nightstick to the midsection or a fire hose blast to the sternum. Bring me the new recruit."

A meek young man, just a few days removed from his 18th birthday, ambled towards him. "H… hello Chief. I don't know why Officer Stacy thought my hands were down my uniform but I can assure you…"

"Enough. We have a job for you, Cadet Deefus. I've been Chief of Police here in Stagsack for 28 years, and never have I seen a protest like this. These kids are so…placid. So calm. They must be stopped." Cadet Deefus stood there, small-armed and soft-bellied, his slack jaw hanging in direct parallel to his delicate unibrow. "S… stopped, sir?"

Police Chief Petunia strolled over to a locker with a menacing-looking exterior lock. He gently tugged at it, and it snapped open. He reached inside and pulled out various articles of clothing. "Here is your riot gear, cadet. You're going out to the front lines. We can't assure your safety… but we can assure you that a reasonably priced plaque will be hung in your honor. Haven't you always wanted to be a hero, son?"

Cadet Deefus stuck out his gaunt arms, collecting the riot gear from Police Chief Petunia: a pair of lensless horn-rimmed glasses, a green cardigan, a tight pair of khakis, and most importantly, wingtips. "Put these on. Report to the front lines. When I give you the signal, you charge."

"Ch… charge the protestors, sir? But they're just sitting there…"

"If I wanted you to charge them I would have said so! No. I will be out there with Officer Stacy and the better half of our K-9 unit. I want you to charge towards us!"

"S... sir?"

"You heard me cadet! Now get moving."

A rotund lump formed in Cadet Deefus's meager throat. He shrugged his shoulders, removed his uniform, and placed the riot gear over his meager frame. The door lightly shook on its hinges as he attempted to slam it on his way out.

Outside of the police building, the crowd had grown complacent. The rally cries of "Mock our sins no more!" ceased to ring out through the idyllic Vermont rolling hillsides. Nobody knew what exactly had precipitated the beginning of this pro-Wingtip protest, and nobody seemed to wonder why. A thin figure gawked at the crowd from inside the door, before being pushed out by a sturdy hand with well-polished fingernails.

"Uh… uh…. Up with Wingtips!" A quiet rally cry returned the sentiment. "No more moccasins!" A second rally cry, quieter than the first, reaffirmed the notion.

Cadet Deefus cast a furtive glance towards the headquarters, as a squadron of heavily armed officers and hungry German Shepherds advanced towards the reclining protestors. Police Chief Petunia raised his riot shield in the air three times; the unmistakable international symbol for "charge at me." Cadet Deefus removed a wingtip and tossed it towards the officers, the loafer covering half the distance between his limp wrist and the intimidating legion of officers. The sinewy legs of Cadet Deefus ran towards the battalion. "Fire up the tear gas, boys."

No fewer than three canisters of Civil Rights grade tear gas sprang out from the officers, landing upon the unsuspecting protestors like artillery fire. One round hit a small dog, who bit the crotch of the closest individual. The pro-Wingtip crowd began coughing, sneezing, choking, vomiting, oozing, and crying. A thick fog formed over the crowd, and visibility fell to zero.

"You know what to do!"

Cadet Deefus had no idea what to do. His eyes burned, his throat was dry, a burning rash was forming on his skin, and his dry heaves were causing him severe discomfort. The police pounced upon him, their batons ready. "Here's one right here! 200 points!"

Fortunately for Cadet Deefus, he did not suffer long, as he quickly lost consciousness upon reaching his pain threshold. He woke up several days later, in a plastic bed, a bronze plaque dangling from Police Chief Petunia's supple hands. His name may have been misspelled… but his legend will live on forever.

The crowd outside has reached bedlam. And by that I mean… it hasn't.

I can remember everything about her: her face, her average laugh, her shoe size, what clothes she wore, what movies she liked, how I used to kiss the back of her hand and how much she loved it. Yet none of my memories compare to her as a person, a real-life human being—someone I could hold, kiss, tell stories to, and someone I would die for.

I looked everywhere for her. The first place I checked was her work because that's where she was when everything fell apart, but she wasn't there anymore. I tried calling her, but she didn't pick up. I asked everyone I could, put up fliers, fired flares into the sky—nothing worked.

I haven't stopped looking for her, but I'm out of ideas. Now I just wander around the city, hoping to find anything that might lead me to her. The search has taken its toll on me. My eyes are sunken, I can barely feel my heartbeat, and the soles of my feet are worn out from never leaving the ground. Call it a bad habit. The apocalypse forces you into a lot of those. It also forces you to get focused.

Normally, I was focused on her and how much I still loved her. But at this particular moment, my attention was drawn to something else—a noise far off down the road. It grew louder. I hadn't heard a noise like that in months.

Soon, a car came swerving around the corner and rocketed down the street. It wasn't a sedan or a minivan but a mish-mash of random metal bits with four rogue wheels sticking out of the bottom. It roared down the asphalt, coming toward me, agitating the crowd.

Oh yeah, the crowd. They're the ones responsible for ending the world in the first place, and they've gotten a lot of hostility these days for that, but they're not to be hated. They're just searching for something too. We all are, though we can't say what it is.

And there were so many of them. Like a parade times twelve, they clogged up the road like a fur-ball clogs a shower drain. The car tried to drive straight through them but was diverted almost immediately into a street pole. Whoever was driving must not have been paying much attention.

The door flew open, knocking some of the crowd onto their feet, and the old, familiar sound of a shotgun blast reverberated down the street. A man jumped out—a real action hero type with scars, a bandanna, and a sneer.

From the passenger side rose the most beautiful girl I've ever seen. It was her, with her perfectly straight hair, freckled cheeks, and a high-powered assault rifle. It had to be her, the woman I'd been searching for since I could remember.

What was she doing with this bandanna-wearing jerk?

My legs were moving before I could even think, slapping against the pavement as I sprinted toward her. I had so many questions.

"Get to the alley! Go!" the action hero roared, signaling her to retreat into the alleyway behind them, but I couldn't let her get away. I tried yelling to get her attention, but my mind wouldn't put words together. Overwhelmed by desire, I needed her.

The crowd made maneuvering difficult, and I know it's not dignified, but I had to start climbing on people just to give chase. My foot on someone's head, hand clutching a collar, until finally, I climbed over the tsunami of bodies and fell, face first, into the alleyway. Picking myself up was almost automatic, and once I was on my feet, I saw her. Her gorgeous figure hoisting herself up a fire escape. I knew she was scared, but I also knew that if I could just talk to her, I could make this all make sense.

A group of five people reached the fire escape before me and had the action hero on his ass before he could say a word. Grateful as I was, he wasn't my concern. Instead, I leaped at the fire escape and pulled myself up, booking it to the roof like the Flash. With each step, a new idea of what I should say came to mind, but I didn't settle on anything. Nothing was good enough. It's a good thing my muscles were still forcing me up the stairs; otherwise, I might have just frozen there in shock or nervousness.

I reached the roof, and there she was, standing at the other end, the wind blowing her hair around, hands wrapped around her gun. When I appeared, she spun in place and took aim.

Then she stopped. The barrel of her gun lowered to the ground. Even at this distance, I could see her eyes swell with tears.

"Oh my god," she whimpered. I tried to smile. I think it worked. At least it felt like it did. Still, no words. This is exactly what I was afraid of.

"Michael?" she said with difficulty. It was my name. She's said it a hundred times before. I wondered why it was hard for her. I realized I was standing completely still, which was odd because I'm usually in constant motion.

ETH Zurich, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology, is a leading institution known for its focus on science and technology. Established in 1855, it has become a center of innovation, channeling research into high-tech sectors like computer science, micro and nanotechnology, and medicine. The university boasts an impressive track record, with 21 Nobel laureates having studied, taught, or researched there. ETH Zurich has established its presence beyond Switzerland through initiatives like the Singapore-ETH Centre (SEC).

In 2010, Dr. Remo Burkhard moved to Singapore to build the Singapore-ETH Centre, the first research center established by ETH Zurich outside Switzerland. The center was established in collaboration with the National Research Foundation of Singapore under its Campus for Research Excellence and Technological Enterprise (CREATE) program. It aims to tackle pressing urban challenges in collaboration with Singaporean universities, government agencies, and industry.

Since its founding, the Singapore-ETH Centre has become a vibrant research hub with approximately 200 researchers working under two main programs: Future Cities Laboratory (FCL) and Future Resilient Systems (FRS). FCL, established in 2010, focuses on making cities more sustainable and livable, while FRS, launched in 2014, aims to enhance the resilience of infrastructure systems.

A pioneering project under the Future Cities Laboratory is the Cooling Singapore initiative. Led by SEC director Gerhard Schmitt, the project seeks to mitigate the urban heat island (UHI) effect in Singapore and improve outdoor thermal comfort (OTC) and liveability. The initiative aligns with Singapore's commitment to reduce emission intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030.

"As urban centers like Singapore become more densely populated, more heat is generated, impacting the environment. The Cooling Singapore project aims to address these challenges," says Dr. Burkhard. The project received a grant from Singapore's National Research Foundation in 2017, bringing together expertise from the National University of Singapore (NUS), SMART (Singapore-MIT Alliance for Research and Technology), and TUMCREATE.

The Cooling Singapore project has a multifaceted approach. It seeks to establish an inter-agency task force comprising members from various Singaporean agencies and institutions to exchange knowledge through workshops. This collaboration is crucial as tackling UHI involves economic development, urban planning, and transportation, requiring the collective effort of scientists, agencies, industry, and policymakers.

One of the project's key tasks is applying microscale climate models to study areas like Jurong Lake District, the Central Business District, and Punggol. These case studies help researchers understand how OTC varies and how different urban designs can mitigate UHI. Initial results suggest a need for more scientific research, pointing towards improving efficiency and cost-effectiveness in strategy implementation.

Beyond policy and planning, businesses and individuals also play a role in mitigating urban heating. "Heat is trapped and released from roads and buildings; energy consumption in industry and transportation are significant contributors to UHI," explains Dr. Burkhard. The Cooling Singapore team has developed a catalog of 86 measures to remove heat from the system, offering guidance on building materials, orientation, and clustering for better wind flow.

Meanwhile, the Future Resilient Systems program and the ETH Risk Centre organized the inaugural Infrastructure Resilience Conference in Zurich, fostering knowledge exchange to enhance infrastructure resilience. The upcoming World Congress on Resilience, Reliability and Asset Management will continue these efforts in Singapore.

The Singapore-ETH Centre is also collaborating on the Digital Underground project with the Singapore Land Authority, aiming to develop 3D digital mapping methods for underground utility networks. This is crucial as Singapore explores the use of underground spaces due to limited land mass.

In addition to these projects, the 3for2 Beyond Efficiency project has adapted energy-efficient technologies developed at ETH Zurich for tropical climates. Implemented at United World College Southeast Asia, Dover campus, preliminary results show a significant reduction in energy consumption, making it one of Singapore's most energy-efficient office spaces.

ETH Zurich's initiatives in Singapore exemplify its commitment to global challenges. With a focus on freedom, responsibility, and open-mindedness, ETH Zurich fosters an environment for independent thinking and pioneering solutions. As Lino Guzzella, President of ETH Zurich, notes, "A good university doesn't just teach knowledge but the ability to think." This ethos drives the university's innovative contributions to society and public debate.

6月22日，荷兰警方在鹿特丹南部的伍兹种植园发现了一批可疑货柜，其中有6个被用作牢房，另外1个被改装成了“酷刑室”。里面装有加装了绑带和手铐的牙医椅，以及钳子、手术刀、园艺剪等工具。这个地方据信是犯罪集团用来实施私刑或恐吓的地点，但在启用前就被警方破获，6名嫌犯也因此被捕。

4月，荷兰警方在伍兹种植园发现了7个可疑货柜，这些货柜几乎每天都有男性前来改装。根据手机加密系统EncroChat案的调查和长时间的观察，有关部门推测这起案件涉及大规模贩毒集团，因此决定在货柜接近完工时介入。他们成功于6月22日阻止了犯罪活动，并于7日召开记者会宣布这一案件。

改装的货柜经过隔音处理，天花板和地板上安装了多副手铐，“酷刑室”内还有一张牙医椅，上面装有绑带和手铐。警方还找到了警察制服、防弹背心、园艺剪刀、手术刀、钳子以及蒙面头套。

警方根据预谋绑架、严重伤害、持有枪械等指控逮捕了6名嫌犯，缴获赃车、25支枪支和毒品，并在鹿特丹找到了犯罪集团的另一处基地。调查仍在进行中，嫌犯被法院下令拘留至少90天。

6月22日，法国和荷兰警方成功破获了犯罪集团使用的手机加密系统EncroChat，拦截并解码了数百万条消息。目前，在欧洲各地已经逮捕了800人。荷兰国家警察调查服务负责人克拉格（Andy Kraag）在7日表示，这次行动是EncroChat案调查的重要成果，“避免了许多暴力犯罪”，未来还有望取得更多进展。

La justice britannique a entamé lundi l'examen du mystérieux naufrage du Bugaled Breizh, un chalutier français qui a sombré en moins d'une minute en 2004 au large de l'Angleterre, emportant par le fond ses cinq membres d'équipage.
Près de 18 ans après le drame, cette enquête publique, qui se tiendra devant la Haute Cour jusqu'au 22 octobre à Londres, suscite l'espoir des familles des cinq marins bretons de enfin découvrir la vérité.
Depuis le début, elles soutiennent que le chalutier a coulé après avoir été heurté par un sous-marin militaire: il se trouvait dans une zone où se déroulaient des exercices militaires de l'OTAN et de la Royal Navy.
"Si le ministère de la Défense britannique ou l'OTAN admet +nous avons dissimulé des choses, nous nous excusons et nous réglons l'affaire+, alors je rentre chez moi, je ne dérange plus personne et vous n'entendrez plus jamais parler de moi", a confié Thierry Lemétayer, fils d'un des marins, regrettant que le secret-défense ait toujours été opposé aux familles.
L'hypothèse du sous-marin n'a jamais pu être confirmée par la justice française à l'issue d'une procédure très longue et non concluante.
Parmi les nombreux témoignages prévus durant les trois semaines d'audience - marins, secouristes, experts maritimes, militaires -, celui de l'ancien commandant du sous-marin nucléaire britannique HMS Turbulent, Andrew Coles, est attendu le 12 octobre. Ce navire est soupçonné d'avoir joué un rôle dans le naufrage.
Le 15 janvier 2004, le Bugaled Breizh ("Enfants de Bretagne" en breton), un chalutier de Loctudy (Finistère), avait sombré en moins d'une minute dans des conditions météorologiques plutôt bonnes, au large des Cornouailles (sud-ouest de l'Angleterre). L'équipage avait été emporté par le fond.
Seuls les corps de Patrick Gloaguen, Yves Gloaguen et Pascal Le Floch ont été retrouvés - le premier dans l'épave lors de son renflouement, les deux autres dans les eaux britanniques - et c'est sur la mort de ces deux derniers que se concentre l'enquête britannique. Georges Lemétayer et Eric Guillamet ont été portés disparus en mer.
- "Vérité", pas "vengeance" -
L'objectif de la procédure au Royaume-Uni est d'élucider les causes des décès, inexpliqués, sans toutefois prononcer de condamnations.
"Les familles des victimes sont des familles de marins et elles ne pourront faire leur deuil que lorsqu'elles sauront comment leurs proches sont morts", a déclaré Dominique Tricaud, avocat des familles, à l'AFP.
"On ne peut pas faire son deuil sans savoir et sur la base de mensonges", a-t-il ajouté. "Les familles ne cherchent pas la vengeance, elles cherchent la vérité. Nous ne voulons pas voir quelqu'un en prison, nous ne réclamons pas d'argent de ce procès, nous voulons simplement que soit reconnue la responsabilité de l'armée britannique dans le naufrage du Bugaled Breizh".
Le ministère britannique de la Défense et la Royal Navy ont nié toute implication d'un sous-marin britannique.
En 2016, la justice française avait clôturé définitivement son enquête dans cette affaire, incapable de trancher entre l'hypothèse d'un sous-marin et celle, avancée dix ans plus tôt par le Bureau français d'enquêtes (BEAmer), d'un accident de pêche.

Luck had never been on my side, especially since I was born with cerebral palsy. It took me a while to understand that being handicapped is really just a state of mind, and that I could do anything most people could, too. The voice on the other end was calming, sincere, and, surprisingly, full of guilt. "Walter? This is Gretchen..."

I hung up, throwing my phone as far as I could, and, in that exact moment, I realized that this money would be the perfect way to escape the life my father had left for me.

Lynette looks up from her book and sees a man standing next to her, smiling and holding a coffee. He repeats himself, and she responds, "Sorry?" looking bewildered. 

He nods enthusiastically, as if they are playing charades. "The hammer hits the nail," he says, pointing to her book, "We're birds of a feather." 

She gazes at the cover of her book as if it were written in a foreign language. Slowly, a sense of understanding begins to form. Although she is unsure why he is speaking in this manner, she decides to humor him. 

"You've read it too, haven't you?" she suggests. "You want to discuss it?" 

"The dart hits the bulls-eye," he responds, gesturing to the chair across from her. "A sage under a tree?" 

"Please, have a seat," she invites. 

The man takes the seat, his balding head looming before Lynette as he leans in. A stray wisp of hair stubbornly sticks out. He sighs and smiles, and she returns the smile. 

"How much of the race is left?" he inquires. 

"I'm about three-quarters of the way through," she answers. 

"Ah, the most intense part of the hike," he muses. 

"It is, indeed. I'm just getting to the part where..." 

"Excuse me?" interrupts a college student at the neighboring table. "Could you keep it down, please?" 

"Oh, I apologize. I'm sorry," Lynette says, feeling embarrassed. 

"A dog rips your favorite pillow," the man interjects. 

"What?" the student responds, confused. 

"He's also sorry," the man explains. 

The student, with a puzzled scowl, returns to her book. The stranger, with a sheepish expression, and Lynette, rolling her eyes, exchange a smile. 

"Lynette, by the way. Nice to meet you," she introduces, extending her hand.

I am mainly in favor of the idea of driverless cars for several reasons that I will explain in this discussion.

While concerns about overpopulation and the emotional toll of losing a loved one are valid, the potential to prevent tragic accidents is a significant advantage of driverless cars.

One aspect of driverless cars that I am not fond of is their strict adherence to the speed limit. This might seem like a minor drawback, especially in the context of the safety benefits, but in certain situations, such as the inability to move in the face of danger, the automated adherence to rules could pose a risk.

In the end, the overall benefits of driverless cars outweigh the drawbacks in my opinion. I am a strong advocate of this technology.

That concludes my viewpoint on driverless cars. I genuinely believe in the potential of this innovation, despite the few reservations I have mentioned.

"I'm not going to chase after them; they can escape for all I care!" I cut off his tirade before he could finish. He was going on about some rebel using a thermonuclear warhead to destroy the planet's core. It was just a minor planet, so what if we lost it? I couldn't bear to deal with any more challenges to my driving skills, especially not today of all days.

"I'm parking this hover-car and heading to the VR plaza to take a much-needed break," I declared firmly.

The man in the passenger seat tensed up, his jaw clenching. Our eyes met, and after a moment, he let out a resigned sigh. "Fine," he muttered.

He exited the hover-car and vanished around the corner, heading towards a noodle shack.

I had finally stood up to him and taken charge of my own path. I input the coordinates and relaxed with a drink as the computer guided me to my destination.

Everything felt different, in a good way. I paid the entrance fee, settled into the VR set, and leaned back. The days of chauffeuring this self-proclaimed hero around the universe were behind me.

I was unfazed by the distant flashes in the holo-window or the approaching light. Those were the least of my worries. What truly saddened me was the realization that I couldn't fully savor the remainder of the day.

台湾在世界贸易组织（WTO）贸易政策检讨会议上承诺，未来将以「已开发国家」的身份参与国际谈判。这一决定可能对国内农业产生影响。对此，农委会副主委黄金城表示，此承诺仅影响未来的新谈判项目，对现有的贸易项目没有影响。此外，美牛和美猪的进口早已开放，目前的限制仅针对含莱克多巴胺的肉品，与新的国家定位无关。

台湾在WTO会议上承诺，未来的谈判中将不再主张「开发中国家」的定位，不再争取开发中国家享有的特殊与差别待遇，而是以「已开发国家」的身份参与谈判。这一转变被认为可能影响国内农产品的国际贸易。

黄金城指出，开发中国家在国际谈判中可以获得关税保护的特殊待遇，而已开发国家由于贸易自由化，关税通常较高。目前，我们正努力加入跨太平洋伙伴全面进展协定（CPTPP）及杜哈回合贸易谈判（DDA），未来的新谈判项目才会受到已开发国家定位的影响。

关于以已开发国家身份进行国际贸易谈判可能增加国内农产外销成本的问题，黄金城表示，我国农产品外销除了邦交国，目前仅在纽西兰和新加坡享有关税优惠，其他国家则没有，外销成本本来就高，这是一直需要克服的挑战。

他还提到，农产品出口困难不仅与关税有关，还涉及农产品是否符合外国饮食习惯。目前，国内农产品研发多是以国人口味为主，不一定受到他国欢迎。

Driverless cars offer benefits that human-driven cars simply cannot. Machines are much less likely to commit errors than humans. Autonomous cars can tackle many of our problems today and are a promising technology that we must develop to better our lives and the world.

Through reduction of the threat of distracted driving, compensation for natural human errors when driving, and improvement of our public transportation system, driverless cars can change our world for the better. They offer a vast improvement on human-driven cars today.

Distracted driving is a major problem today that can be remedied through the use of driverless cars. A large percentage of automobile accidents in America occur due to distracted driving, which self-driving cars can fix.

Driverless cars also address issues related to impaired judgment caused by intoxication or fatigue in drivers by eliminating the risk they pose to other roadway users. Machines can take over when human drivers aren't completely focused on the task at hand and correct major errors swiftly.

Moreover, driverless cars provide solutions for texting while driving by incorporating heads-up displays with entertainment and information systems. This innovative technology allows individuals to communicate without taking their eyes off the road, enhancing safety significantly.

Autonomous vehicles have the potential to prevent thousands of deaths each year resulting from distracted driving accidents. They excel in addressing natural human errors that occur during driving since machines have quicker reaction times than humans and are capable of processing information rapidly.

Improving public transportation is another area where driverless cars shine. Sergey Brin envisions fleets of autonomous taxis reducing fuel consumption while offering more flexibility compared to current systems like buses with fixed routes.

Driverless taxis could revolutionize long-distance travel within cities as well as between them by providing efficient transport options tailored to individual needs without compromising convenience or flexibility like traditional public transportation modes do presently.

In conclusion, driverless cars offer a variety of benefits including enhancing public transportation systems, reducing human error on roadways, and eliminating risks associated with distracted driving affecting other users' safety. Automation in vehicles not only improves efficiency but also enhances overall safety standards on roads—ushering in an era where machines drive us towards a safer future for everyone involved.

〔记者佟振国／南投报导〕武汉肺炎（新型冠状病毒病，COVID-19）病毒不断变异，各厂牌疫苗的保护力也出现不确定性。目前，英国的最新研究显示，BNT与AZ疫苗的混合接种效果显著。卫福部草屯疗养院医师沈政男引用医学期刊《Lancet》关于疫苗保护力的文章，指出中和力越高的疫苗在面对变异株时显得尤为重要。根据研究，AZ混合BNT的效果比两剂BNT更强大，他也推测AZ和莫德纳的混打应具可行性，但目前政府仍未开放混打。

沈政男在脸书发文表示，根据《Lancet》最新刊载的研究，2剂AZ和2剂BNT疫苗对各种病毒株的中和力显著下降，这体现了抗体对变异株的作用下降。最近，苏格兰也提供了类似的实证数据，显示2剂BNT在Delta变种上的保护力为73%，而2剂AZ则为60%。这表明中和力数据对于Delta变种依然适用，其中AZ疫苗在面对Delta变种时下降最多，接近科兴疫苗的水平，而2剂BNT仍能在一定程度上抵御这种变种。

此外，《Lancet》另一篇文章比较了只打1剂AZ和AZ加BNT的情况。研究结果显示，AZ加BNT混打比打2剂AZ甚至2剂BNT产生更高的中和抗体效价。沈政男认为，这些研究数据表明混打可能比两剂BNT提供更强的保护力。国内现有的AZ和莫德纳疫苗，如果参照BNT的数据，AZ与莫德纳的混打应具可行性。但由于国内缺乏混打的临床实证，目前仍未开放混打政策。

L'entraîneur de Concarneau, Nicolas Cloarec, anticipe un début d'année crucial pour la suite de la saison. Toutes les rencontres valent trois points, mais certaines peuvent en rapporter le double. On les appelle des matchs « à six points », et le match entre Concarneau (14e) et Béziers (10e) en est un. De même, les rencontres Créteil (12e) - Marseille (11e) et Les Herbiers (15e) - Chambly (13e) s'annoncent disputées ! Ça va chauffer derrière !

Le suspens est aussi présent devant, avec les confrontations Rodez - Grenoble et Red Star - Cholet, opposant les quatre premiers. Au milieu, Sannois SG (5e) affronte Laval (9e) et Pau (6e) joue contre Lyon (8e). Cette 18e journée s'annonce palpitante, à l'exception notable du match entre Avranches (17e) et Dunkerque (7e), ce dernier ayant écopé de trois points de pénalité confirmés en appel par la DNCG.

Cloarec : « Un match décisif »

À l'exception du match Dunkerque - Avranches, cette reprise promet une bataille acharnée entre voisins, pouvant se transformer en défaite cuisante pour les perdants. Par exemple, une victoire des Herbiers les rapprocherait de Chambly, mais une défaite les mettrait à six points de retard. Les Thoniers vivraient une situation similaire. Sous les ordres de Nicolas Cloarec, les joueurs pourraient se rapprocher à deux points de Béziers, mais risquent aussi de se retrouver à huit points derrière. « C'est effectivement un match crucial, un tournant », confirme l'entraîneur concarnois. Il place cette rencontre dans un contexte plus large : « Ensuite, nous affronterons Chambly, Granville en Coupe et Les Herbiers. Nous avons quatre tours de coupe devant nous. Si nous les abordons correctement, nous pourrions atteindre les 8es de finale de la Coupe de France et être au milieu du tableau du championnat de National ».

Double enjeu

Il est crucial de bien entamer cette série en ce début d'année 2018. Du 32e de finale de la Coupe de France à Houilles (0-3) jusqu'à cette 18e journée (la première de la phase retour) du championnat à Guy-Piriou, la rencontre face à Béziers, qui reste sur une série de huit matchs sans victoire (cinq nuls et trois défaites), doit impérativement rapporter trois points à Concarneau. Ces trois points deviendraient six en tenant compte des difficultés de l'adversaire.

Composition des équipes

Concarneau : Guivarch et Demazeau (g), Nsimba, Jannez, Sinquin, Irep, Drouglazet, Edjouma, Gégousse, Idazza, Donisa, Damessi, Koré, Toupin, Geran, Popineau.

El canciller cubano Bruno Rodríguez Parrilla escribió en su cuenta de Twitter un mensaje al presidente Donald Trump, después de que éste utilizara también la red social para expresar su apoyo al pueblo cubano en una fecha tan significativa como el 20 de mayo.

En respuesta a las palabras del inquilino de la Casa Blanca, el Ministro de Relaciones Exteriores contestó desde La Habana: "Alguien debería informar al presidente Trump que el 20/05/1902 la naciente República quedó lastrada con un apéndice a la Constitución que prescribía el derecho de intervención de EE.UU.”

Asimismo, mencionó que “no fue hasta el 1/1/59 que Cuba alcanzó su plena independencia y su pueblo fue dueño absoluto de su destino”.

En este intercambio de frases, poco usual en el naciente “gobierno electrónico” impulsado fundamentalmente por Díaz-Canel, los usuarios de las redes aprovecharon para criticar al canciller cubano y sus palabras.

Oscar Visiedo, desde Miami, le dijo a Rodríguez que lo que escribía era falso. "Un ejemplo: la Base Naval de Guantánamo". Y preguntó: "¿Cómo es que en 60 años no han expulsado a los yaquis de allí, aun contando con la ayuda militar masiva de la URSS? ¿No depende Cuba actualmente para su alimentación de los EEUU?"

Por su parte, desde Cuba, un usuario llamado Cuenca, le dijo al ministro cubano: "‘y su pueblo fue dueño absoluto de su destino’ dice sin inmutarse. Debe usted ser muy bueno jugando al póker".

El periodista cubano Pablo Alfonso, radicado en Miami, le escribió: "Bruno, el lastre de la Enmienda Platt se abolió el 29 de mayo de 1934, por la Revolución del 33." Aclarado el contexto histórico, agregó: "Fueron 32 años de lastre en una República incipiente. ¡El comunismo castrista lleva 60 años y no logró parir una Constitución tan progresista como la del 40!"

Otra persona, llamada Servio Vlanda, le preguntó al canciller: "¿Qué me dices del derecho de intervención de los soviéticos a partir de 1962, cuando no teníamos ni Constitución pues la de 1940 fue abolida en 1959? ¿Te olvidaste de las tropas soviéticas y los misiles nucleares de 1962?" Luego aseguró: "Eso es intervención, peligro y aventura." Y agregó: "Claro, tenías solo 4 añitos."

Al canciller cubano le han respondido no solo con palabras, también con imágenes. El usuario Sr. Rodrigues Cuba posteó una foto con la frase que ha identificado el período de mandato de Díaz-Canel y su gabinete: "Somos continuidad."

Remote sensing image (RSI) analysis and interpretation are crucial in computer vision, involving various tasks like land-cover classification, change detection, object detection, and more. Such analysis aids in monitoring natural phenomena and human activities on Earth's surface for purposes such as land-use surveillance, disaster prevention, precision agriculture, and wildfire detection. RSI captures both natural events and human interventions, playing a vital role in applications across geographic information systems, agriculture, environmental science, and numerous other fields.

In recent decades, the advancement in aerospace technology has led to earth observation satellites producing terabytes of RSIs daily. Despite this abundance, two key challenges remain:

1. High Specialist Manpower Requirement: The need for professional researchers for RSI identification and labeling results in high costs.
2. Presence of Noisy Labels: The complexity of RSIs makes generating accurate labels during data annotation challenging, leading to an abundance of large but noisy labels that can hinder many tasks. To address these challenges, the remote sensing community is shifting its focus to automatic feature extraction and analysis from unlabeled RSIs. Self-supervised learning (SSL), which leverages the inherent data structure, emerges as a crucial method to utilize large-scale unlabeled RSIs effectively.

Early SSL methods relied on pretext tasks like jigsaw puzzles, patch localization, and image inpainting, but these methods have limitations in generalizability. Contrastive learning (CL) has emerged as a superior method, enhancing representation by bringing similar instances closer and separating dissimilar ones. CL captures highly discriminative and generalizable feature representations, standing out among SSL methods.

However, applying CL efficiently in remote sensing faces two main obstacles. Firstly, due to the fundamental laws of geography, data samples with close geographical proximity should exhibit some degree of similarity. Current CL paradigms often misclassify geographically and semantically similar samples as negatives, leading to sample confusion. Secondly, RSIs often lack clear foreground-background distinctions, with key information scattered throughout the image. CL, being a global discriminant task, struggles to capture fine-grained details essential for remote sensing tasks. To overcome these challenges, we propose SwiMDiff, a novel self-supervised pre-training framework tailored for RSIs.

SwiMDiff enhances CL by incorporating a scene-wide matching strategy that recalibrates data based on associated scenes to prevent mislabeling. It considers intra-class similarity, improving the model's ability to extract global discriminative and semantic information. By integrating a diffusion model, SwiMDiff strengthens the CL encoder, creating a unified training framework that emphasizes local and detailed information. SwiMDiff captures global semantic information and focuses on fine-grained features, providing richer information for remote sensing tasks.

Our evaluation of SwiMDiff on change detection and land-cover classification tasks using datasets like OSCD, LEVIR-CD, BigEarthNet, and EuroSAT demonstrates its superior performance, indicating its potential in remote sensing applications.

In conclusion, SwiMDiff has been rigorously tested on change detection and land-cover classification tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results and showcasing its capability to handle complex remote sensing tasks effectively.

Driverless cars still pose potential dangers, as they may malfunction or encounter issues. Trusting a vehicle that relies on technology can be unsettling, as machines inevitably experience failures. The question remains: how can we be certain that these cars are safe and reliable for us to operate? This uncertainty will likely be resolved over time as we gain more experience with these advanced vehicles.

While manufacturers assure us that they will rigorously test these cars, how can we be certain that they are truly safe to drive? The idea of a car autonomously navigating through various scenarios, such as construction or accidents, raises concerns. It seems contradictory that we are required to intervene in such situations, defeating the purpose of a driverless system. If a car is designed to drive itself, it should be fully capable of doing so. The thought of something going awry while we are in control is indeed disconcerting. In the event of a malfunction, such as loss of steering or braking, the consequences could be dire, with little recourse for the driver. Current vehicles, at least, can be taken to a professional, diagnosed, and repaired. The prospect of implementing additional regulations, specifically for the liability of accidents involving driverless cars, seems daunting. Who, then, should be held responsible in the event of a mishap, the driver or the manufacturer, especially when the car is, in theory, capable of steering itself?

The Seagoing Cowboys is a program dedicated to ensuring that animals traveling by sea are healthy and well-cared for. In this text, I will provide some reasons why you should consider joining the program.

One major reason to join the Seagoing Cowboys is the importance of caring for animals to prevent them from getting sick or even dying. This program is responsible for the well-being of horses, young cows, and mules being shipped to Europe, particularly during the time of World War II, when many countries were in desperate need of supplies. For instance, the Seagoing Cowboys took care of 335 horses during another war, as Luke, a participant, mentioned, "We arrived in August 1945, the day the Pacific War ended."

Being a part of the Seagoing Cowboys is a valuable way to ensure the safety of animals on boats, even though the work can be challenging, and the journeys can take weeks or even months.

La construction du premier temple hindou de Fort McMurray commencera dimanche. Ce projet de 6,5 millions de dollars, passant du rêve à la réalité, aura nécessité 10 ans de travail. La société culturelle Sanatan Mandir est à l’origine de cette initiative. Formée en 2010, elle avait pour objectif précis la construction d'un temple hindou à Fort McMurray.

Le projet a connu quelques retards en raison du terrible feu de forêt qui a détruit une partie de la ville en 2016, ainsi que du ralentissement économique qui a touché l’Alberta ces dernières années. Malgré ces défis, Kalpesh Patel, le président de la société culturelle, exprime sa fierté : « C’est un rêve qui devient réalité. Je suis extrêmement fier. »

Il pose fièrement devant l'endroit où le temple hindou sera érigé, sur Abraham Gate. Ce temple sera le plus au nord du monde, un fait dont il est particulièrement fier. Il permettra à la communauté hindoue de pratiquer sa religion et servira également pour des activités culturelles et des rencontres.

Environ 800 familles constituent la communauté hindoue de Fort McMurray et des environs. « Nous avons compté énormément sur nos membres pour financer le projet », explique Kalpesh Patel. Le temple jouera aussi un rôle essentiel dans la transmission des traditions de la communauté aux générations futures.

La fin de la construction du temple hindou est prévue pour octobre 2020, marquant une étape significative pour la communauté locale. Avec des informations de Jamie Malbeuf.
