In many scientific and engineering disciplines, mathematical and computational simulators are employed to gain mechanistic insights. A common challenge is determining the parameter settings of these simulators so that their outputs align with a set of empirical observations. For instance, identifying a distribution of parameters that, when processed through the simulator, generates a distribution of outputs that matches empirical observations is crucial. Suppose we have a stochastic simulator with input parameters \(\theta\) and output \(x\), allowing us to generate samples from the forward model \(p(x|\theta)\), which is typically intractable. We have acquired a dataset \(D = \{x_1, \ldots, x_n\}\) of observations with the empirical distribution \(p_o(x)\) and seek to identify a distribution \(q(\theta)\) over the parameters that, once run through the simulator, produces a "pushforward" distribution of simulations \(q^\#(x) = \int p(x|\theta)q(\theta)\,d\theta\) indistinguishable from the empirical distribution.

This problem, known by different names in various disciplines, is called "unfolding" in high-energy physics, "population of models" in electrophysiology, and "population inference" in gravitational wave astronomy, among others. Following the terminology of Vandegar et al. (2020), we refer to this challenge as "source distribution estimation."

One approach to source distribution estimation is empirical Bayes, which uses hierarchical models, modeling each observation as arising from different parameters, \(p(x_i|\theta_i)\). The hyperparameters of the prior, and, by extension, the source, \(q_\varphi\), are determined by optimizing the marginal likelihood, \(p(D) = \prod_i \int p(x_i|\theta)q_\varphi(\theta)\,d\theta\) over \(\varphi\).

The picture was the proof in the pudding. Therefore, there was no alien monument. Secondly, this face on Mars could be a rock. Depuis plus de 20 ans, l’Union commerciale industrielle et artisanale (UCIA) de Pont-l’Évêque (Calvados) organise une action commerciale pour les fêtes de fin d’année. Face au contexte sanitaire et notamment au confinement, il était impossible d’organiser sa traditionnelle vingtaine ou quinzaine commerciale. À l’approche de la réouverture des commerces le 28 novembre, Michel Lepaisant, président, et Carole Zouheir, du magasin Carol’Chaussures, ont donc mis sur pied une nouvelle formule : une dizaine commerciale.

L’objectif de cette initiative est de booster le commerce de Pont-l’Évêque, participer à son attractivité et gâter les clients. "C’est d’autant plus important en cette période, pour soutenir les commerces qui ont été fermés, et la situation compliquée de certaines familles, à cause du chômage partiel par exemple. Nous voulons que tout le monde ait un joli Noël," explique Carole du magasin Carol'Chaussures.

Comment ça marche ? Du jeudi 10 au dimanche 20 décembre, rendez-vous dans vos commerces participants. Votre commerçant vous remettra un bulletin de participation à remplir que vous pourrez ensuite déposer dans l’une des urnes disposées dans la ville. À noter que les bons sont cumulables : si vous réalisez un achat de 100 €, vous pourrez remplir environ 10 tickets, ce qui augmente vos chances de gagner.

Particularité de cette édition, les gains à la clé sont exclusivement des bons d’achat : de 60, 100, 200 et 500 €. En tout, plus de 7 400 € sont à gagner, répartis entre 103 gagnants. Les gains proviennent des bénéfices réalisés lors des événements organisés par l’UCIA tout au long de l’année. Pour déterminer les heureux gagnants, l’UCIA procédera à quatre tirages. Le samedi 12 décembre à 19 h : 1 gagnant à 200 €, 3 gagnants à 100 €, 30 gagnants à 60 €. Le mercredi 15 décembre à 19 h : 1 gagnant à 200 €, 3 gagnants à 100 €, 30 gagnants à 60 €. When she was on the floor, hand clutching a limp jaw and blood dribbling across pale skin, I knew I'd fucked up. That single blow devastated me and left a wound that would only fester. To think one punch could break everything. I promised her that it would never happen again. But when she looks at me now, her eyes scream fear, and I know I'm the bad guy.

The next day, I wake up in December 2015. The days go by like forgotten streams on a photo reel. Happy smiles, tears, eat-ins and take outs, until we're back where we started, where I made the mistake. The rug in front of my apartment lounge suite is still clean. The walls still have their glow, and the computer is hooked to the TV screen, just like it had been last time.

Then comes the knock, three oppressive thuds on a frail door frame. I shimmy, slide, flick the lock, and slide back the wood. She's there, dangling locks, crop top, and black skirt. Eyes meet for an instant, she's cool, calm, collected, reflecting my own, and I wave her in with a smile. Her gaze lights up like I've flicked the switch, and one, two, three steps later she's on the couch with my laptop in hand. Exactly like it happened then.

"Long day?" She clicks on her favorite show and watches the TV buffer.

"Tiring," I say.

Matter of fact, I was sitting here, on this couch. Wondering if I would be an idiot two times in a row. Second chances worked sometimes -- hopefully.

She smiles and my whole world warms. It's like a drug, and god dammit I'm addicted. "Well, come on then, blankie time?" She pats the seat next to her twice.

I snap open the blanket cupboard and nearly pick the same one, cool blue and supple fur. Brown seems better this time; it's a duvet more than a blanket -- no one cares. "How was your day?" I ask in return.

She shifts her head side to side. "It was alright.... there's been a lot on my mind..."

My head is agreeing, but my eyes take in every second of this moment. The way her maroon lips move, her hand gestures, the shiver of her hair.

أعلنت هيئة تطوير معايير العمل بالشارقة عن إطلاق النسخة الرابعة من بطولة الشارقة الرياضية العمالية، التي ستبدأ اعتباراً من 5 فبراير/شباط المقبل وتستمر حتى 2 إبريل/نيسان 2021. ستُقام المباريات كل يوم جمعة في ملاعب مجلس الشارقة الرياضي بحديقة منتزه الشارقة الوطني، مقابل مطار الشارقة الدولي، من الساعة 8 إلى 11 صباحاً، ومن الساعة 1 ظهراً حتى الساعة 5 عصراً. تُنظّم الهيئة البطولة بالتعاون مع مجلس الشارقة الرياضي وشركة «ريتش تارجت» للخدمات الرياضية.

وأشار سالم يوسف القصير، رئيس هيئة تطوير معايير العمل بالشارقة، إلى أن البطولة تأتي ضمن الخطة الاستراتيجية للهيئة، التي أرسى دعائمها صاحب السمو الشيخ الدكتور سلطان بن محمد القاسمي، عضو المجلس الأعلى، حاكم الشارقة، والتي تهدف إلى ترسيخ الرياضة كأسلوب حياة لدى العمال وإتاحة الفرصة أمامهم للترفيه عن أنفسهم. كما أكد على الالتزام بجميع الإجراءات الاحترازية التي تطبقها الدولة في الأنشطة الرياضية.

وأوضح القصير أنه من المتوقع أن تحظى النسخة الرابعة من البطولة بإقبال ومشاركة عالية من مختلف فئات العمال وموظفي الدوائر والمؤسسات الحكومية والخاصة. تقوم فكرة البطولة على عقد المنافسات الرياضية بين العديد من الفرق العمالية في خمس رياضات، حيث من المتوقع أن يشارك أكثر من 1200 لاعب موزعين على 20 فريقاً في كرة القدم، و12 فريقاً لكل من السلة والطائرة والهوكي، و25 فريقاً للكريكت. وستشهد النسخة الحالية حفلاً ختامياً حافلاً لتكريم الفرق الفائزة بجوائز نقدية وهدايا عينية تصل قيمتها إلى 250 ألف درهم.

أعرب سالم القصير عن رضاه بنجاح فكرة البطولة، مشيراً إلى الإقبال الكبير من الفرق المشاركة وجمهور المشجعين في النسخ الثلاث الأولى.

At every moment in time, the human brain responds dynamically to visual stimuli perceived through the eyes, which can be indirectly measured using functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI). Understanding and categorizing specific patterns of brain activity in response to visual stimuli is vital in unraveling the mysteries of the human brain. One significant approach to achieving this is through inverse modeling, which involves reconstructing the observed image from the fMRI signal. Given the complexity of images, obtaining detailed pixel-level information presents challenges and is not always necessary. As a result, researchers have mainly focused on decoding the semantic content of images. On the other hand, fMRI encoding aims to predict the fMRI signal based on visual stimuli. However, decoding the fMRI signal poses several challenges: 1) Redundancy: Semantic information in the signal is sparsely distributed, with closely related elements showing high correlation, indicating redundancy in the fMRI signal. 2) Instability: The fMRI signal is influenced significantly by changes in domain, meaning signals from one person or scanner may not apply to decoding signals from another person or scanner. 3) Insufficiency: In practical scenarios, the availability of image-signal pairs is limited, making it difficult to utilize deep learning methods that typically rely on large training sets for understanding fMRI data. Recent studies have attempted to decode fMRI signals using pre-trained generative models such as Instance-Conditional GAN, diffusion models, masked autoencoders, and CLIP, among others. Although these methods have shown impressive results in generating high-quality images, they face challenges in ensuring semantic consistency with fMRI signals and reliability in the presence of noise.

This paper introduces a novel framework that addresses the challenges of fMRI signals through joint decoding and encoding tasks. Our framework comprises several key components. First, we introduce an encoder-decoder architecture specifically designed for fMRI signals and images to learn a dense latent representation space for each modality, tackling signal redundancy effectively. Additionally, we demonstrate the advantage of training these architectures independently, eliminating the need for paired fMRI-image data and overcoming data insufficiency. Despite the instability of fMRI signals across individuals, our framework successfully compresses these signals into a unified latent space using a shared encoder. By leveraging self-supervised training principles, we train our architecture to construct a dense latent space without extra supervision. We propose a lightweight alignment module to link the latent spaces learned from fMRI and images, tailored to individual characteristics to address signal instability. Through this alignment, we can assess the reliability of both neural encoding and decoding models by reconstructing images from fMRI signals.

The Latent Embedding Alignment (LEA) framework we present is tailored for fMRI decoding and encoding, incorporating separate encoder-decoder architectures for fMRI signals and images, along with an alignment module for transforming between the latent spaces. Our framework supports image-fMRI-image reconstruction, ensuring the reliability of both encoding and decoding models. Extensive experimentation on benchmark datasets demonstrates the efficiency and effectiveness of LEA in fMRI decoding and encoding.

Our contributions can be summarized as follows:
- Facilitating the training of encoder-decoder architectures for specialized fMRI signal and image latent spaces.
- Establishing a connection between these latent spaces to enable fMRI decoding and encoding within the unified LEA framework.
- Demonstrating the superior performance of LEA through rigorous validation on multiple benchmark datasets, highlighting its efficacy and advancements.

The bridge is a fairly narrow room containing four seats: one for the navigator, one for the pilot, and two others. Currently, Glenn, the pilot/engineer/navigator, and Desmond, the ship’s “security officer”/weapons specialist, occupy two of these seats, while their Captain, Sam, leans against the back wall. Normally, Quinntenn would engage Desmond in some light banter, but Sam cuts him off.

“Well, now that Quinntenn is finally here, we can begin.” Sam pushes off the wall and gestures toward the large, almost phallic-like ship sitting immobile on the edge of a large blue nebula, visible through the Duraglass window in front of them. “That, gentlemen, is a Kelgeorian mining frigate. Normally, we would stay far away from such a beast, but you know what, Glenn,” Sam says, glancing over at the small man in the pilot's seat. “Bring up the distress call.”

Glenn immediately flips a switch on his vast array of lights, buttons, switches, and knobs that make up the labyrinth of the pilot console. The onboard radio starts sputtering garbled words and inaudible sounds amid the static, forcing everyone but Sam to cover their ears from the brutal sounds. After a few seconds, Sam nods at Glenn, who then turns off the radio.

“Jesus, Sam,” Desmond says, rubbing his ears in an attempt to soothe them. “I didn't know you invented a new method of torture! Gee, that's just fuckin' amaz—”

Sam cuts Desmond off. “Glenn and yours truly put that garbled mess through the computer, and we were able to piece together something I think you all will find quite interesting.” Sam turns back to Glenn. “Play it.”

Glenn starts typing, and after a couple of seconds, a voice comes over the intercom: “…..UEC frigate New Charon, ……an SOS………stay…………Please Save……………….”

“That’s it?” Quinntenn asks, looking at Sam, unimpressed. “That message could mean any number of things. Hell, it could have already reached one of the other UEC outposts, or it could be one of the Big Fish trying to catch some idiot hero UEC captain stupid enough to fly into a nebula. I don't need to tell you what happens to electrical equipment there, if—”

“Jesus, Quinntenn,” Sam sighs with disappointment. “Why did you become a pirate in the first place if all you apparently want to do is bitch about danger?” She turns her back to Quinntenn and walks over to the Duraglass observation window. “Glenn, you finish up,” she says, waving her hand toward Glenn, her excitement from the new discovery now drained.

Glenn turns his chair to the rest of the crew and clears his throat in an attempt to hide his young voice. “I was able to gather more information on the distress call. See, I knew I had heard the ship's name before, and it turns out the last cargo drone we scooped up was not only scanning asteroids but looking for a lost ship.” Glenn beckons Quinntenn over to his console and flips another switch to turn on the large computer screen in the middle of it. “Look, Quinntenn, the ship New Charon has been missing for only half of a Galactic week. The Kelgeorian mining company has no idea what happened to it. It left port at Whetham station in the HD 10180 star system, and no one has seen a trace of it since. Guess what it is carrying, Quinntenn?”

“Whetham station,” Quinntenn says, his jaw almost dropping at the name. “Water, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen—the damn thing is carrying resources for terraforming.”

“Exactly, Quinntenn, that ship is carrying everything for terraforming new planets—from the water, plants, and raw materials to key elements of the atmospheric processors. Now, anyone want to guess how much these particular materials go for on the black market?”

Sam turns from her view and comes bounding back into the conversation, her excitement now rejuvenated. “Two million for the gas tanks, five for the water tanks, and three million for plant seeds! We could finally give the Xavier the upgrade she deserves. We could outfit her with stasis pods, a better FTL drive, or better yet, both. Think about it—we could finally get out of the Orion sector. We could finally see the galaxy, see Earth, go to New Mars, see something other than this godforsaken backwater.”

“That’s… good,” Quinntenn says, his eyes fixed on the ship. “Okay, Sam, let's hear the plan.”

“We enter from the half not inside the nebula,” Sam says, “make a beeline for the cargo, pack the Xavier with as much as she can carry, set a course to the Kepler-42 system, and get rich.”

“Hold on, Sam,” Desmond says, holding his hands out to emphasize his point. “What about the people on the ship? Frigates don't just pilot themselves or break down on their own.”

“We did a scan of the ship—no life forms aboard,” Sam replies. “We scanned as much of the ship as we could, and no lifeforms came up. They must have used the escape pods when they crashed after sending out the message. Just makes our job easier.”

“But there is nothing around here,” Desmond says.

La escapada por Málaga Historia junto al mar Interior de la Cueva del Tesoro. / SUR La Cueva del Tesoro y la Casa Fuerte de Bezmiliana son las principales joyas del patrimonio de Rincón de la Victoria JAVIER ALMELLONES Málaga Sábado, 31 agosto 2019, 00:12

Rincón de la Victoria cuenta con una de las franjas litorales más atractivas del litoral andaluz. Desde el arroyo de Totalán hasta el de Santillán, hay algo más de siete kilómetros de cuidadas y equipadas playas. Pero a un paso de estos arenales, aguarda también un importante patrimonio histórico y natural, bien conocido por quienes tienen esta localidad como destino estival.

Lo que hoy es una costa turística como otros enclaves urbanos marengos ha sido, a lo largo de la historia, uno de los enclaves litorales más codiciados por su valor estratégico. Esto se comprueba con la existencia en su territorio de un par de torres vigías y un recinto amurallado, lo que hace que Rincón de la Victoria merezca formar parte de la conocida Ruta de las Torres Vigías de la Axarquía.

Entre sus dos almenaras, la más occidental es la que se levanta en El Cantal, una llamativa formación rocosa bañada por el Mediterráneo. Esta atalaya, como ocurría hace siglos, permite tener una visión amplia de la costa. En la zona oriental del término municipal se encuentra la Torre de Benagalbón, que da nombre a uno de los núcleos urbanos. Tanto esta como la del Cantal fueron levantadas originalmente en el siglo XIV por los árabes, aunque fueron reconstruidas posteriormente por los Reyes Católicos.

Entre ambas torres, como complemento al sistema de vigilancia, se puede visitar la Casa Fuerte de Bezmiliana. Este recinto amurallado, que actualmente alberga una sala de exposiciones, tiene una muralla con dos garitas desde donde se oteaba la línea marítima para evitar posibles ataques de piratas.

Otro gran aliciente para visitar Rincón de la Victoria es su célebre Cueva del Tesoro, que fue habitada por el hombre prehistórico. Está considerada una joya de la geología por ser la única cavidad de origen marino de Europa. De hecho, la acción del Mediterráneo ha contribuido durante milenios –desde el Jurásico– con su efecto erosivo a la formación tanto de esta cueva como de otras situadas bajo el denominado Cantal. En su interior, se encontraron numerosos restos humanos, animales y de cerámica de la época conocida como el 'Neolítico de las Cuevas'. Entre sus salas más importantes, sobresalen la de la Virgen, la del Volcán, la de Marco Craso y la de Noctiluca. Esta última debe su nombre al hallazgo de un templo dedicado a la diosa fenicia del mismo nombre. Como complemento a esta gruta, a tan solo unos metros se puede visitar el Parque Arqueológico del Mediterráneo.

El legado del territorio rinconero se complementa con el núcleo interior de Benagalbón.

You had always believed your guardian angel was either dead or perhaps so dysfunctional that it was better not to be under their care at all.

"I'm sorry," you say. "Sorry for all the times I complained about your absence, for cursing you when Mom or Dad hit me, for envying other kids whose guardian angels whisked them away to better lives."

You walk up to him, stand over him, and gently touch his face.

"I thought I was alone, but I was wrong. You were never allowed to tell me, were you? Not until today."

You trace the old scar on the left side of his face.

"You were always with me, weren't you?"

Your brother closes his eyes and remains silent.

Exploring the realm of egocentric vision (first-person view), the pursuit of refining 3D hand pose estimation stands as pivotal for understanding human activity. This quest not only paves the way for new developments in human-computer interaction (HCI) [31, 34, 38] but also facilitates imitation learning [8, 13, 37]. Additionally, it elevates the immersive experience in augmented/virtual reality (AR/VR) to unprecedented levels [15, 33]. Recent advancements in AR/VR headsets have made egocentric data more prevalent [5, 10], leading to a growing demand for estimating 3D hand poses from egocentric viewpoints.

In recent years, numerous networks with diverse structures have emerged to enhance 3D hand pose estimation performance [7, 39, 44]. However, most existing methods are limited to a single-view setting, which although convenient, comes with drawbacks such as a restricted field-of-view and depth ambiguity. To tackle these issues, one potential solution is to incorporate an additional camera to widen the field-of-view and reduce depth ambiguity by capturing the hand shape from a different angle. Moreover, the integration of multiple cameras aligns with industry trends, evident in the latest AR/VR headsets like the Apple Vision Pro and Meta Quest, which feature multiple egocentric cameras. Consequently, a shift towards multi-view settings in hand pose estimation is inevitable, driven by technological advancements and industry trends.

Presently, several studies have focused on hand pose estimation under multi-view settings [4, 12, 19]. These methods typically process input images from multiple views concurrently, employing a feature fusion module to generate final predictions [22, 41]. However, existing approaches have significant limitations, such as the requirement for costly multi-view labels during training and the necessity to use the same camera parameters during testing as those used in training. In contrast, our proposed method offers a fresh approach that enables adaptation of a single-view estimator to a dual-view setup without the need for multi-view labels or specific camera parameters. By utilizing a pre-trained estimator and unlabeled dual-view inputs, our method can adapt to arbitrary dual-view setups, allowing for flexibility in camera configurations.

Expanding on these advancements, we introduce a novel unsupervised Single-to-Dual-view adaptation framework (S2DHand) for egocentric 3D hand pose estimation. This framework leverages stereo constraints, including cross-view consensus and transformation invariance between camera coordinate systems, to refine pseudo-labels and enhance model accuracy. The cross-view consensus is utilized through an attention-based merging module, while the invariance of transformation is employed via a rotation-guided refinement module.

Our method is evaluated by adapting a pre-trained estimator to various dual-camera pairs placed in different poses. Evaluation across in-dataset and cross-dataset scenarios demonstrates significant enhancements over state-of-the-art adaptation methods. The key contributions of this work include proposing an unsupervised single-to-dual-view adaptation solution, introducing a pseudo-label-based strategy for adaptation, and achieving substantial improvements for arbitrarily placed camera pairs under different settings.

Mental health disorders are recognized as an urgent global health challenge, affecting 10.7% of the population worldwide (Dattani et al. 2021). Despite this prevalence, 70% of people with mental disorders lack access to well-being services (Henderson et al. 2013). The barriers to accessing treatment services include geopolitical resources, insufficient treatment professionals, financial support, and stigma (Weiss and Pollack 2017). Assistive technology for mental health can possibly address these issues. The use of assistive technology could improve the accessibility, participation, effectiveness, and affordability of mental health treatment (Doherty et al. 2008); however, many existing intervention techniques remain limited due to intrinsic factors involving difficulties with being aware of our own internal states (Botella et al. 2012).

In particular, digital mindfulness tools that use visual interactive elements to encourage self-awareness and self-reflection are considered as accessible and effective tools (Patibanda et al. 2017). Various studies have shown that art can have a direct or indirect stimulating effect on brain activity (Altay et al. 2017). When used in a therapeutic context, art allows unconscious feelings to be expressed, identified, and reflected upon to connect and respond to physical symptoms and feelings to increase emotion regulation and self-awareness (Blomdahl et al. 2016). In addition, the use of biofeedback could further enhance self-perception and self-regulation for mental wellbeing, as well as empower empathy and compassion in social biofeedback interaction (Moge et al. 2022).

In this paper, we explore how artistic visualization of physiological signals can improve self-awareness of our body and effectiveness of biofeedback intervention. Our artistic visualization biofeedback interface builds on the literature on biofeedback, mindfulness, and arts for wellbeing. For the rest of this paper, we describe the design process and implementation, and discuss the limitations for future work.

Mathematical modeling of physical processes plays a crucial role in many engineering fields, aiding in both the analysis and prediction of how a process responds to changes in state and control variables. Consequently, a model should accurately represent the underlying process. However, during the modeling process, a balance must be struck between complexity and tractability (Zendehboudi et al., 2018). Generally, increased model complexity results in a more accurate representation of the process but becomes more challenging to solve. Another key trade-off involves determining how much prior knowledge to incorporate into the model versus how much to learn from process data. Mathematical models can typically be placed on a spectrum ranging from mechanistic to data-driven models, often referred to as white-box to black-box models, respectively (see Fig. 1).

Mechanistic models are developed using first-principle equations, potentially supplemented with empirical closure relations, and necessitate a deep understanding of the process's physical behavior. These models are often complex and require simplification to be computationally feasible. In contrast, data-driven models are constructed from generic mathematical equations fitted to process data, requiring no prior process knowledge. These models offer high flexibility, allowing them to adapt to complex patterns in data. As a result, data-driven models can capture unmodeled or unknown process behaviors, provided these are reflected in the available data. However, data-driven models are data-intensive and require sufficiently rich data to accurately represent process behavior. Without caution, overfitting is a common issue, leading to poor extrapolation to future process conditions (Solle et al., 2016). Due to the use of first-principle equations, mechanistic models typically excel in extrapolation.

Hybrid modeling combines mechanistic and data-driven techniques, aiming to leverage the strengths while minimizing the weaknesses of each approach. Several methods exist for constructing hybrid models, and there is extensive literature on the topic (e.g., Psichogios and Ungar, 1992; Kramer et al., 1992; Xu et al., 2011; Zendehboudi et al., 2018; Bikmukhametov and Jäschke, 2020; Hotvedt et al., 2020). Hybrid modeling can be approached from either end of the spectrum shown in Fig. 1.

Models on the white end of the spectrum typically offer greater interpretability than those on the black end. Interpretability has numerous definitions and aspects within the literature. According to Roscher et al. (2020), interpretability is the ability to present a model in understandable terms to a human. This article focuses on physical interpretability. A model is considered physically interpretable if 1) its output behavior aligns with existing physical principles and 2) any model parameters representing physical quantities have physically plausible values.

La Cámara en lo Contencioso Administrativo, con el voto de sus integrantes Hugo Rubén González Elías y Gisela Nerea Schumacher, rechazó un planteo hecho por la Asociación de Defensa de Consumidores Entrerrianos (Adecen) contra el aumento de la tarifa eléctrica autorizado por el Ente Provincial Regulador de la Energía (EPRE) a comienzos de año, que representó un incremento promedio del 137%. Se trata de la última batalla judicial por la readecuación tarifaria; antes, el Superior Tribunal de Justicia (STJ) había cerrado la discusión sobre una docena de amparos presentados por empresas y particulares.

Adecen promovió una medida cautelar y solicitó a la Justicia que se "suspendieran" los efectos de las sucesivas resoluciones adoptadas por el Ente Regulador a comienzos del año, que autorizaron los aumentos en la tarifa eléctrica. El abogado Raúl Muñoz, impulsor de la presentación judicial, denunció un aumento promedio del 184% para la tarifa eléctrica en el primer bimestre, resuelto, según él, "a puertas cerradas entre el EPRE y Enersa".

Con el mismo argumento que utilizaron las empresas y particulares para combatir el aumento tarifario, Adecen reprochó el hecho de que la suba se haya resuelto sin permitir la participación de los usuarios mediante el sistema de audiencia pública.

En su presentación judicial, Adecen destacó que en la autorización de los aumentos tarifarios hubo una "violación de derechos de incidencia colectiva referentes a intereses individuales homogéneos, consistentes en el derecho de consumidores y usuarios del servicio público de electricidad a participar en el proceso de determinación de una tarifa justa, razonable y transparente para el suministro de energía eléctrica". Según el resumen hecho por el juez Baridón al emitir su voto, esto fue violado por el EPRE al aprobar modificaciones excesivas a los cuadros tarifarios sin convocatoria a audiencia pública previa.

Al promover la cautelar el 8 de agosto pasado, Adecen invocó "la representación de usuarios y consumidores entrerrianos del servicio eléctrico sin efectuar distinciones". Durante la audiencia convocada a pedido del EPRE el 13 de septiembre de 2016, Adecen perfiló su representación a los usuarios domiciliarios, categoría que detalló aún más en la respuesta al traslado conferido por Presidencia el 14 de octubre de 2016, centrando sus esfuerzos en los usuarios residenciales urbanos y rurales. Desde la fecha de publicación del último de los actos administrativos que modificaron la tarifa eléctrica, la Resolución 12/16 en el Boletín Oficial del 24 de febrero de 2016, hasta la delimitación de la clase representada, transcurrieron ocho meses.

Aunque Baridón consideró admisible la acción, los otros dos miembros del Tribunal, González Elías y Schumacher, la rechazaron.

Subas
En Entre Ríos, el Ente Regulador puso en vigencia a principios de año el aumento aprobado en la audiencia pública de enero de 2014 en Villaguay, del 19,8%, además de la actualización inflacionaria de los dos años de congelamiento y el aumento registrado en el mercado mayorista eléctrico. Es decir, a aquel 19,8% se le sumó un 37%, un 43% y otro 57%. Así, entre diciembre de 2015 y febrero de 2016, la tarifa se incrementó en un 137%.

En 2017 se esperan más aumentos. El Ente Regulador autorizó, a través de la resolución Nº 168, un incremento tarifario para el próximo año del 32%, en tres fases: un 23% en la tarifa media más un 9% como consecuencia de la actualización trimestral por mayores costos prevista en el contrato de concesión.

El pedido fue hecho por la distribuidora estatal Energía Entre Ríos SA (Enersa) en la audiencia pública de revisión quinquenal del cuadro tarifario que se desarrolló el 31 de agosto en Villaguay. Entonces, solicitó que la tarifa aumentara un 23%, más el 9% por actualización trimestral.

Las subas se aplicarán así: un 15% a partir de enero de 2017, un 8% en marzo de 2017 y un 9% en mayo del mismo año.

Presentaciones y disputa en los Tribunales
El fallo adverso a Adecen ocurrió luego de una disputa en los tribunales respecto de la vigencia de la última reimposición de la tarifa eléctrica. La recomposición tarifaria se dio después de dos años seguidos de congelamiento, producto de un acuerdo con la Nación y la disminución sustancial de los subsidios, lo que generó una serie de presentaciones judiciales para obligar al Gobierno a revertir la situación.

Self-supervised learning, as explored by Doersch et al. (2015) and Wang & Gupta (2015), has significantly advanced in developing robust representations for downstream tasks, particularly in the fields of computer vision (Chen et al., 2020a; He et al., 2020) and natural language processing (Lan et al., 2019; Brown et al., 2020). However, most studies have focused on well-curated datasets like ImageNet (Deng et al., 2009), which tend to be balanced across categories. In contrast, real-world data often exhibit long-tailed, or even heavy-tailed, distributions (Reed, 2001), posing a challenge for current machine learning methods. Notably, recent research (Jiang et al., 2021b) indicates that self-supervised learning under long-tailed distributions still requires further exploration to achieve satisfactory performance (Van Horn et al., 2018).

Existing approaches to self-supervised long-tailed learning primarily focus on either the loss or model perspective. The loss perspective involves techniques such as loss reweighting, including focal loss for hard example mining (Lin et al., 2017) or the SAM method, which considers the sharpness of the loss surface (Liu et al., 2021), to emphasize tail samples during training. However, the effectiveness of these methods heavily relies on the accurate identification of tail samples, which can be challenging. The model perspective, on the other hand, involves specific model designs, such as the divide-and-contrast ensemble (Tian et al., 2021) or self-damaged contrast via pruning (Jiang et al., 2021b), to better capture the semantics of tail samples. These designs, however, often depend on empirical heuristics, making the underlying dynamics difficult to understand, which, in turn, complicates further improvements (Zhang et al., 2021).

One way the FAC System can be beneficial is by recognizing when students become confused while attempting a test question. Instead of seeking help from the teacher, the computer can guide the students through problem-solving steps and then present a new question to reinforce the concept. This can lead to improved concentration and the students' ability to perform to the best of their capabilities.

In the educational setting, the integration of the FAC System in classroom computers can significantly benefit students by addressing the challenges of confusion, boredom, and distraction. One of the most renowned and enduring problems in computer science is the question of whether P equals NP. Solving this problem would have profound implications across various fields, from economics to cybersecurity. Over the years, many have claimed to have proven whether P equals NP or P does not equal NP. However, to date, none of these claims have been validated. 

There are multiple approaches to attempting such a proof. One approach involves using lower bounds on the complexity of circuits. By demonstrating that a known NP-complete problem has a circuit complexity that is exponentially lower-bounded, one could prove that P does not equal NP. In the paper "A Solution of the P versus NP Problem Based on a Specific Property of the Clique Function" [Sim19], Sima endeavors to do precisely this. Sima examines the clique function, aiming to show that its circuit complexity is exponential, thereby proving that P does not equal NP. 

In this paper, we will first introduce the relevant definitions and the prior work that Sima builds upon. We will then present Sima's argument, highlighting the points where it fails, due to the improper generalization and the oversight of the relationship between a Boolean variable and its negation. Finally, we will provide an example that illustrates the flaw in the algorithm.

Deep neural networks (DNN) have shown remarkable progress in various computer vision tasks, including image classification and object detection. However, these models are susceptible to adversarial examples (AEs), which are deliberately manipulated to introduce perturbations that lead to incorrect outputs. This vulnerability poses a serious threat to real-world applications like self-driving cars and facial recognition systems. To enhance the robustness of DNN models and facilitate their practical implementation, researchers have extensively explored adversarial attack algorithms aimed at understanding how to create AEs to deceive DNN models.

Adversarial attacks can be classified based on the magnitude of perturbations as l p norm-based attacks or unrestricted attacks. In l p norm-based attacks, the perturbation's l p norm must not exceed a specified threshold to ensure imperceptibility. Common l p norm-based attack methods include the fast gradient sign method (FGSM), projection gradient descent (PGD) attack, and Carlini & Wagner (C&W) attack. However, AEs generated by l p norm-based attacks may not be feasible in real-world physical applications, particularly in complex tasks like object detection.

Unrestricted adversarial attacks, which do not impose constraints on perturbation magnitude or area, are more widely employed in physical-world scenarios. Balancing adversarial performance and naturalness to human observers presents a significant challenge in these attacks. Several strategies have been explored in image classification and object detection tasks to achieve this balance, such as altering image color or simulating natural weather conditions like fog and snow. Camouflage-based methods have also been developed for object detection, including patch-based and camouflage-based approaches.

Efforts to generate AEs that effectively deceive both human observers and object detectors simultaneously remain challenging. Existing approaches face limitations in transferring stationary AEs from classification tasks to object detection and ensuring the naturalness of camouflages in dynamic environments. To address these challenges, a novel end-to-end differential evolution-based dual adversarial camouflage (DE DAC) pipeline is proposed. This approach leverages a two-stage training method based on neural render to optimize global and local textures for effective camouflage generation.

The DE DAC method integrates differential evolution (DE) algorithm to enhance attack success rates and introduces adaptive DE DAC for context-aware camouflage generation. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in fooling both human observers and object detectors while adapting to different environmental settings. The contributions and methodology of DE DAC are detailed, emphasizing its advantages in achieving a balance between deceiving human observers and evading object detection. The paper concludes by outlining future research directions and implications.

Si resolver el café instantáneo o el azúcar en tu bebida preferida con una cucharita es mucho trabajo, este dispositivo puede satisfacer tus necesidades. La firma de diseño Gemini presentó una taza tecnológica que se ocupa de revolver el café de forma autónoma. Denominada Aumix, el recipiente con esta particular función manos libres posee un rotor interno que realiza todo el trabajo y, lo más sorprendente, es que no requiere de una batería o una conexión a una fuente eléctrica.

Este mecanismo es posible gracias a la reacción que genera el calor del líquido en el aire utilizado por el rotor para generar el movimiento necesario para mezclar el café instantáneo o el azúcar en la bebida caliente. De esta forma, unos 320 mililitros de agua en su punto de ebullición bastan para transformarse en una cantidad de energía cinética suficiente para revolver el líquido, dijeron sus creadores, citados por el sitio Sora News 24.

La taza autónoma Aumix comenzó como un proyecto de financiación colectiva presentado en el sitio japonés Campfire y recaudó más de cinco millones y medio de yenes, unos 50 mil dólares, con un precio estimado de 38 dólares por unidad.

El dispositivo cuenta con un rotor que se activa ante el calor del líquido, sin necesidad de baterías ni cables que impulsen el mecanismo interno de la taza. De esta forma, los perezosos podrán obtener su bebida caliente, sea un café, té, leche chocolatada o una sopa, sin necesidad de mover un dedo.

Named Data Networking (NDN) is one of five projects funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation under its Future Internet Architecture Program. NDN builds upon the results of an earlier project called Content-Centric Networking (CCN). Both NDN and CCN are instances of a broader network research direction known as Information-Centric Networking (ICN), from which different future network architecture designs have emerged. CCN originally proposed a transition from today's connection-oriented IP networks to content-centric architectures, and NDN further develops these ideas. Currently, NDN exists as a testbed prototype built as an overlay network on top of the IP network, with active research underway to explore possibilities to replace the IP stack with the NDN stack.

The main design principle of NDN, distinguishing it from IP networks, is that IP networks are communication networks where packets address nodes as communication endpoints in the network. In contrast, NDN is a distribution network that focuses on solving the content distribution problem, as solving this problem over a communication network is complex and error-prone.

The main innovation of NDN lies in changing the transport layer in the network protocol stack so that packets name content objects instead of communication endpoints. This shift in semantics transforms the network's role from delivering packets to specific destinations to fetching data identified by given names. This change is theorized to help solve not only end-to-end communications but also content distribution and control problems.

In NDN, two types of packets are exchanged: interest packets and data packets. Based on their roles in the network, three types of nodes are distinguished. Producer nodes (or publishers) produce content, while consumers request content from producers. Consumers send interest packets containing the name of the desired content, prompting producers to respond with data packets routed back to the consumers along the same path as the interest packet. NDN routers, the forwarding nodes, are responsible for routing packets between producers and consumers. Each NDN router maintains three tables: the Pending Interest Table (PIT), the Forwarding Information Base (FIB), and a Content Store (CS).

When an interest packet arrives, the forwarding node first checks its content store for matches. If the content store contains the requested data, the router serves it to the consumer. Otherwise, the router searches its PIT for matches. The PIT stores all forwarded interest requests that have not received corresponding data packets yet. Each PIT entry includes the requested content name, incoming and outgoing interfaces, grouping incoming interest requests by content name to enable efficient multicast data delivery. If a matching record is found in the PIT, the router updates the entry with the incoming interface. Otherwise, the router forwards the interest packet toward the content producers based on its FIB and forwarding strategy. Upon receiving a data packet, the router forwards it back via all incoming interfaces listed in the PIT entry, removes the PIT entry, and caches the data packet in its content store. Routers forward packets based on content names, without information about hosts or interfaces. Since each data packet is signed by the producer, routers can serve content from their cache to expedite interest request satisfaction.

The NDN design relies on names within a hierarchical namespace that avoids address space exhaustion and can evolve independently of the network. While flat naming schemes are supported, structured naming schemes are preferred in the NDN framework.

Dans les années soixante-dix, Alain Arnaud renoue avec sa passion pour l’écriture et publie quatre recueils de poèmes. Il collabore à plusieurs revues de poésie et contribue à l’organisation des « Journées de la poésie » à Hyères, de 1978 à 1984. Au cours de cette période, il écrit cinq manuscrits qui restent inédits.

Au terme d’une carrière professionnelle principalement tournée vers l’international, avec plusieurs postes à l’étranger, Alain Arnaud publie en novembre 2018 son premier roman : « Le festin des lanternes ».

Dans son dernier roman, « Le vieux pressoir », Mylène, enseignante, vit dans les souvenirs de ses moments heureux en tant qu’épouse et mère. Alors que sa fille Océane gagne en indépendance, Mylène est en quête de la vérité sur les événements qui ont brisé leur foyer familial. Elle s’emploie à démêler le passé de son mari Julien, cadre dans une entreprise de décoration, et s’interroge sur les liens étranges qu’il établit avec un client particulier, Charles, un marchand de biens sans scrupule.

Pour cela, Mylène doit reconstituer et comprendre des faits qui se sont déroulés à Paris, en Provence et en Turquie, souvent en son absence. Au-delà de la passion des protagonistes pour la vigne et des motivations secrètes de leurs actes, parviendra-t-elle à retrouver sérénité et soif de vivre ?

Alain Arnaud sera présent le samedi 28 septembre de 10 h à 12 h 30 et de 14 h à 17 h à l’espace culturel du centre Leclerc pour présenter et dédicacer son dernier roman, « Le vieux pressoir ».

Music performance is a complex and nuanced activity that involves the interplay of various expressive features such as timing, dynamics, and articulation. Research in expressive performance within the field of music information retrieval (MIR) aims to model these expressive aspects by analyzing how performers utilize nuances in timing, dynamics, and articulation to convey their musical intentions. The goal is to develop computational models that can analyze, recognize, or synthesize expressive performances.

Recent research, particularly in Western classical piano, has embraced data-driven approaches for both performance generation and data creation, resulting in large-scale MIDI performance data transcribed from audio recordings. While these datasets can be valuable for tasks like comparative performance analysis, performer identification, and performance style transfer, they often lack the precision and alignment with the musical score necessary to accurately map expressive intentions and parameters to the underlying score features.

Compared to these large-scale, transcribed MIDI datasets, precise MIDI data, recorded on computer-controlled grand pianos such as the Yamaha Disklavier or Bösendorfer SE/Ceus, and their corresponding score alignments, are somewhat limited in both quantity and size. These datasets typically feature performances from advanced piano students or piano competitions, and the digital scores are often sourced from open, user-curated, online libraries, such as MuseScore.

Un incendie a ravagé un hôpital privé traitant des patients atteints de coronavirus en périphérie du Caire. La catastrophe a causé au moins sept décès et plusieurs blessés.

L'incendie s'est déclaré vers 9 heures du matin, heure locale, à l'hôpital Misr Al Amal d'El Obour, situé à environ 35 km au nord-est de la capitale égyptienne. Il aurait débuté dans le service de soins intensifs, au deuxième étage de l'établissement.

Plusieurs camions de pompiers ont été dépêchés sur les lieux et ont rapidement maîtrisé et éteint l'incendie. En parallèle, les patients ont été évacués puis transférés dans un hôpital public situé ailleurs dans la ville.

D'après les résultats d'une enquête préliminaire, l'incendie aurait été déclenché par un court-circuit électrique, ont rapporté des sources sécuritaires aux médias locaux.

Un incident similaire s'était déjà produit en Égypte en juin, où sept personnes avaient perdu la vie dans un incendie survenu dans le service dédié aux patients atteints du coronavirus, dans un hôpital de la ville méditerranéenne d'Alexandrie.

La pandemia pasará. Tardará más o menos, tendrá su impacto, pero esa batalla terminará. Sin embargo, otra batalla, a la que quiero referirme aquí, lleva años desarrollándose de manera silenciosa, en un crescendo que, si el país no enfrenta, nos afectará gravemente.

Me refiero a la seguridad social, el problema más serio y grave que enfrenta Uruguay. La batalla más relevante y difícil de todas.

Consciente de ello, el gobierno creó una comisión para estudiar el asunto y puso al frente a una de las personas más idóneas: Rodolfo Saldain.

Es interesante conocer algunos de los elementos del diagnóstico que está produciendo esa comisión:

- "El único grupo etario que crece en Uruguay es el de mayor edad" (léase: el costo jubilatorio seguirá aumentando).
- "Los crecientes requerimientos de transferencias desde generaciones activas más reducidas hacia generaciones mayores cada vez más grandes, impondrán sobre las primeras un esfuerzo que se irá incrementando cada vez más" (léase: se hará insoportable).
- Además, "es esperable que al menos se relativice una de las formas de vínculo sobre las que se desarrolló el seguro social: el empleo en relación de dependencia de larga duración" (léase: menos aportantes).
- "Todos los esquemas que conforman el sistema previsional uruguayo requieren revisión" (léase: están desfinanciados).
- "Cada peso aportado al sistema genera beneficios en diferentes cuantías y características, según el sector de afiliación o régimen previsional" (léase: además de todo, es injusto).
- "Existen circunstancias que comprometen el mantenimiento de tasas de reemplazo del orden de las entregadas actualmente" (léase: va camino a reventar).
- "El gasto previsional es de los más altos del mundo. La evolución y la tendencia que el gasto previsional viene mostrando hace necesario reformar el sistema con la mayor celeridad posible" (léase: la economía uruguaya está al borde de desfondarse).
- "Es necesario corregir la trayectoria que presentan las erogaciones destinadas a jubilaciones, retiros y pensiones, de manera de alcanzar niveles de gasto compatibles con el desarrollo de otras políticas públicas y asegurar los fundamentos de la prosperidad económica y social" (más claro...).
- "El valor presente de los beneficios que paga el BPS prácticamente duplica el valor presente de los aportes" (fórmula para una quiebra).
- "Los beneficios otorgados por todos los subsistemas (militar, policial, bancario, profesional, notarial) exceden a las contribuciones" (más claro...).
- "La edad mínima de retiro resulta baja cuando se la compara con la de países de similar situación demográfica y nivel de desarrollo. Supone para los jubilados del BPS una sobrevida de 21 años en hombres y de casi 27 en las mujeres. En poblaciones como las cajas paraestatales, estos lapsos son aún mayores" (léase: vivimos en un mundo irreal).
- "Las tasas de aportación sobre el trabajo resultan elevadas en la comparación internacional" (léase: costos no competitivos).
- "La subida de las tasas presenta restricciones, dado su actual nivel" (léase: no da para más).
- "La diversidad de tasas distorsiona la asignación de recursos de la economía, generando pérdidas de eficiencia" (más claro...).
- "La necesidad de revisar todos o algunos de los parámetros del régimen previsional administrado por el BPS está presente desde hace más de una década" (léase: basta de arrastrar los pies y de mirar para otro lado).

Y hay mucho más, pero lo enumerado ya es suficiente para entender que el problema es, a la vez, muy serio y muy complejo.

Can you believe that there is a face on Mars? The Face on Mars, while intriguing, is not actually a face but a natural landform. There are several reasons supporting this conclusion: the facial features are merely shadows, there is no concrete evidence of alien involvement, and scientific research has debunked the idea of extraterrestrial creation.

Firstly, the facial features are nothing more than shadows cast by rock formations. While it may be enticing to imagine an alien origin for such an enigmatic image, reality dictates otherwise. Research has confirmed that it is simply a large rock formation. In fact, "The authors proposed using this as a means to engage public interest in Mars" (Paragraph 3).

Secondly, there is no definitive proof that aliens were responsible for creating this formation. Speculation about alien involvement lacks substantial evidence since the existence of aliens itself remains unproven. As stated in one article: "Some skeptics suggest that any alleged alien markings might be obscured by haze" (Paragraph 8).

Lastly, scientists have conducted studies discrediting the notion of extraterrestrial intervention in shaping the Martian face. A photograph taken during April 1998 winter showed how challenging it would have been to capture such an image through wispy clouds (Paragraph 8).

The allure behind attributing the Martian face to aliens stems from humanity's desire to believe in otherworldly beings. It serves as a testament to our curiosity about potential life beyond Earth's boundaries but leaves us uncertain about its authenticity.

While opinions may vary on this subject, I personally believe that the Martian face is simply a geological feature based on concrete evidence: shadow-like facial characteristics, scientific scrutiny debunking alien theories and lack of conclusive proof regarding extraterrestrial involvement. Ultimately, one must decide whether they prefer reality over fiction when considering these mysteries.

In recent years, the computer vision community has witnessed significant success with Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) on various image classification benchmark datasets like ImageNet [1] and MS-COCO [22]. However, acquiring large-scale data with accurate labels is both costly and time-consuming. When noisy labels are introduced into the training data, it's widely recognized that the performance of deep models can be significantly compromised [2, 36, 3, 23], hindering their quick deployment in real-world noisy scenarios.

A common approach is to gather a considerable amount of image-related side information (such as surrounding texts, tags, and descriptions) from the internet and use them directly as ground truth for model training. While this method is more efficient than manual annotation, the labels obtained often contain noise due to their diverse sources. Hence, enhancing the robustness of deep learning models against noisy labels has emerged as a critical challenge.

To assess label noise, some studies have introduced new layers [26, 27] or loss functions [28, 29, 30, 18] to rectify noisy labels during training. However, these approaches rely on the strict assumption of a single transition probability between noisy labels and ground-truth labels. Consequently, while these methods may perform well on artificially noisy datasets, they prove less effective on real noisy datasets like Clothing1M [36]. In certain cases, annotating a small portion of training samples as additional supervision can improve the resilience of deep networks against label noise, as demonstrated in works like [31, 11, 32]. Nevertheless, the reliance on clean samples makes them less adaptable for large-scale real-world applications.

Numerous data cleaning algorithms [33, 34, 35] have been developed to filter out incorrectly labeled samples prior to training. The primary challenge with these algorithms lies in distinguishing informative but difficult samples from harmful mislabeled ones. CleanNet [11] has achieved state-of-the-art performance on the real-world noisy dataset Clothing1M [36] by generating a single representative sample (class prototype) for each class to assess the label correctness. On the other hand, SMP [20] employs multiple prototypes to represent a noisy class, deviating from CleanNet's single prototype approach. Both CleanNet and SMP require additional clean supervision for model training.

In many previous studies, image-related side information or annotations (such as titles and tags) from the web are often viewed as noisy labels without fully leveraging their potential benefits. Our analysis suggests that these side information sources reveal underlying similarities among images and classes, offering significant help in addressing label noise. By scrutinizing label structures and text descriptions, we propose a weakly supervised learning strategy to handle noisy samples more effectively. For instance, the label "apple" could encompass both a fruit and an Apple mobile phone, leading to misclassification issues. Titles or descriptions related to the images can indicate such misplacements. In this paper, we introduce an efficient weakly supervised learning strategy that evaluates the correctness of each image sample in each class by utilizing label structures and descriptions. Additionally, we present a large-scale fine-grained product dataset to facilitate further research in visual recognition. Notably, this product dataset boasts the largest number of product categories available to date.

Our contributions in this paper are outlined as follows: Images from the WebVision 2019 dataset [37] representing categories like phalarope, horseman, candied apple, tulipa, and gesneriana. This dataset was sourced from the internet using textual queries generated from 5,000 semantic concepts in WordNet. Notably, each category includes numerous noisy images as depicted above.

1) We propose a weakly supervised learning strategy utilizing a Side Information Network (SINet) for classifying images with noisy labels.

Al had walked in first, knowing his friend, Tritius, was following close behind. He sat down in front of the bartender, who greeted him with a dull, rehearsed question, "What would you like?" The bartender was weary from the endless stream of gloomy patrons and their dreary stories. However, this time, something other than a depressed middle-aged man piqued his interest.

"I'll have a H2O," Al replied. The bartender struggled to suppress a giggle, noticing their lab coats. "H2O, too," Tritius chimed in, sounding bored and annoyed. The bartender had been waiting for this moment. He retrieved a bottle of hydrogen peroxide and water, poured them into separate glasses, and served them to his customers. "Your, uh, H2O2, sir," he announced, biting his lip to stifle his laughter.

Everything seemed to pause as Tritius glared at the bartender with disgust. The bartender expected laughter but was met with confusion. Standing to the left behind Al, Tritius revealed a green, glowing ball from his pocket. The bartender's eyes widened in shock. What is this? he thought. The ball illuminated the dimly lit room, casting an eerie glow. Al facepalmed, realizing this was not how he wanted things to unfold. Tritius took Al's water and held it in his hand.

"Look, man," the bartender began nervously, "this is a joke! You saw the bottle of hydrogen peroxide! You know I'm not trying to kill you!" But Tritius remained unfazed. "Look, we aren't fools. Just hand over some cash, credit works too. Al! Where are you going?" Tritius called as Al wandered towards the door. Reluctantly, Al returned. "Geez, this was a bad idea in the first place. It's not going to work!" Al whined.

Despite Al's protest, it was too late to stop the plan. The bartender, terrified of the glowing ball's ominous presence, emptied the cash register. "Nope! We want ALL of the cash," Tritius demanded. "This is a ball of sodium, locked within an argon chamber held together by a mix of tritium and phosphorus. If you don't give us all the cash, I'll smash the ball, expose the sodium, and then put it in the water, causing a deadly explosion," Tritius snarled.

"Okay, okay!" the bartender cried, handing over the cash. Al felt relieved by their success, grabbing the drink in front of him to save for later. Once Tritius had the money, Al stood beside him, tipping his hat as a farewell gesture. But Tritius, having a bad day, was not satisfied. "This place is a bust. I'd rather let the Higgs field experience false vacuum decay than be here." In frustration, Tritius smashed the dreadful ball on the countertop, dropped it into the water, and hurled it into the corner farthest from the exit. As smoke began to billow, Tritius and Al dashed out the door.

Statistical shape modeling (SSM)/morphological analysis [28] is an important resource for medical and biological applications. SSM broadly involves two distinct parts. The first part is shape representation, which involves describing the anatomy/shape of interest by providing an implicit or explicit representation of the shape. The second part involves using the shape representation to perform subsequent analysis on shape population. 

Classical approaches traditionally relied on representing shape via landmark points, often corresponding to distinct anatomical features. However, there have been many automated approaches for dense correspondence discovery that capture the underlying shape statistics [10, 26]. An alternative approach to shape representation is to leverage coordinate transformations between images or geometries, typically members of a population or to a common atlas [19]. This set of transformations implicitly captures the population shape statistics for the objects/anatomies contained in the images. 

Automated shape representation via dense correspondences has its drawbacks. Most such methods rely heavily on preprocessed data, including segmentation, smoothing, alignment, and cropping, which often necessitate manual parameter settings and quality control. This preprocessing, heavy on human resources, may require a level of specific anatomical, clinical, or biological expertise, making shape analysis more challenging. Additionally, automated landmark placement or registration relies on computationally expensive optimization methods, often requiring additional parameter tuning and quality control, which can be a barrier, especially for nonexperts, when the data consists of primarily images/volumes.

In this paper, we explore embeddings of graphs where vertices are mapped to points in \( \mathbb{R}^d \), for \( d \geq 3 \), and edges are represented by line segments on the \( d \)-dimensional axis-parallel planes. A 3-dimensional network, for instance, can be visualized inside a cube, with edges drawn on the walls of the cube through the projection of points.

One motivation for studying these embeddings is their connection to two classical graph parameters: thickness and geometric thickness. The thickness of a graph \( G \) is defined as the smallest number of planar subgraphs into which the edges of \( G \) can be decomposed. This concept was introduced by Tutte [18], and further explored in a survey on thickness [16]. Geometric thickness introduces an additional constraint that requires all subgraphs to be embedded simultaneously, with a common vertex embedding. This was investigated for complete graphs in [4]. The relationship between geometric thickness and other parameters such as maximum degree and tree-width has been studied in several papers, including [8], [2], and [7]. While using standard coordinate planes in high dimensions is more restrictive than thickness, it appears to be less so than geometric thickness (discussed further in Section 3).

Book embeddings, as defined by Ollmann [17], are a restriction of geometric drawings where vertices are positioned in a convex manner. The book thickness, or stack number, of a graph \( G \), is the minimum number of subgraphs needed to cover all the edges of \( G \) in such a drawing. This concept is explored in [6], with a comprehensive survey available in [5].

A broader survey on simultaneous embedding of graphs can be found in [3].

**Spinach and Barley Risotto**

Serves 4 to 6.

**Ingredients:**

- 2 tbsp. sunflower or olive oil  
- 1 1/2 c. barley (hulless or pearled)  
- 1/4 c. minced shallots  
- 1 small bunch green onions, trimmed and chopped  
- 1/4 c. white wine  
- 4 to 5 c. vegetable or chicken stock  
- 3/4 to 1 lb. spinach, rinsed, dried, and sliced into 1/4-in. strips  
- 1/4 c. chopped fresh parsley  
- Generous pinch of grated nutmeg  
- 1/4 c. shredded aged Parmesan cheese  
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste  
- Pinch of red pepper flakes  

**Directions:**

1. Heat the oil in a large deep heavy saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the barley, shallots, and green onions, tossing to coat with the oil. Cook until the shallots are tender, about 3 minutes.

2. Stir in the wine, then add the stock 1/2 cup at a time, allowing the barley to absorb the liquid as you stir. Cook until the barley is tender, about 30 minutes for the pearled barley and 40 to 45 minutes for the hulled barley.

3. Toss in the spinach, parsley, and nutmeg, and stir. Then, fold in the cheese. Season to taste with salt, pepper, and red pepper flakes.

**Nutritional Information per Serving** (for 6 servings):

- Calories: 290  
- Fat: 8 g  
- Saturated Fat: 2 g  
- Cholesterol: 0 mg  
- Sodium: 210 mg  
- Carbohydrates: 46 g  
- Dietary Fiber: 10 g  
- Added Sugars: 0 g  
- Protein: 12 g  

**Exchanges per Serving:** 3 starch, ½ medium-fat protein, ½ fat.

**Notes:**  
You can prepare the risotto a day in advance. Reheat and add the spinach and cheese just before serving.

The utilization of renewable energy sources (RES) presents a significant challenge for energy system operators in Australia and globally due to their variability. Maximizing the utilization of RES requires energy storage. However, large-scale battery storage is costly and pumped-hydro storage faces limitations based on geographical constraints. A promising long-term solution to integrate Variable Renewable Energy (VRE) involves establishing a new infrastructure for transporting VRE in the form of electricity and/or hydrogen (H2).

Creating large-scale renewable energy hubs connected to H2 production hubs can bring substantial economies of scale by building a cost-effective VRE transport infrastructure. Designing such infrastructure requires addressing key questions like whether VRE hubs and electrolysers should be co-located, the best means to transport VRE (H2 pipelines or electricity transmission lines), and the factors influencing investment decisions. This task necessitates an integrated electricity and hydrogen system (IEHS) modeling framework to evaluate costs and benefits of various investment options.

Existing knowledge and modeling tools are insufficient for such a comprehensive infrastructure design exercise. Current literature either focuses solely on the H2 supply chain or has limited consideration of infrastructure technologies. A holistic approach considering a range of transport and storage technologies within an integrated framework is crucial. This is particularly vital for large-scale renewable energy hubs, where wind and solar farms might be distant from H2 utilization sites.

Important factors often overlooked in the literature include voltage and pressure drops in infrastructure, compressor sizing, and water availability for electrolysers. Linepack modeling is critical for assessing VRE storage capacity in the H2 pipeline network, influencing the sizing of pipelines and compressors. In gas transmission networks, the modeling of time-varying accumulation rates, and the network's topology, are essential and often omitted in existing works.

This paper introduces a novel mathematical optimization model to determine the optimal integrated infrastructure for transporting large-scale VRE. The model incorporates the essential infrastructure technologies and nonlinearities, and the impact of RES variability. A mixed-integer quadratically constrained programming (MIQCP) model, a tractable alternative to the computationally intractable large-scale nonconvex problem, is proposed. The model is applied to a range of studies and a real-world case study in Australia, and the outcomes and the methodology of the model are detailed in the subsequent sections.

In recent years, smarter cars have emerged and gained popularity as word of their capabilities has spread. Many believe that these advanced vehicles offer a fresh perspective on the automobile industry. However, others argue that they pose a hazard and could potentially harm drivers. I believe that the development of smarter cars should be halted, and the focus should shift to improving conventional, fully drivable cars.

The development of driverless cars should be stopped because, if allowed to continue, they would necessitate the creation of new traffic laws. Consequently, all drivers would have to alter their driving habits. Many states currently prohibit computer-driven cars, prioritizing the safety of their residents. Those who choose to drive smarter cars would have to comply with new regulations. However, drivers of traditional cars may view learning these new rules as a waste of time, potentially endangering themselves and others. Furthermore, the implementation of new laws for driverless cars would require many years for global adaptation, given the vast number of drivers worldwide.

Driverless cars are not safe, as they rely on computers, which are prone to technical difficulties and failures. An important topic of discussion among manufacturers is, how is a passenger's safety ensured? While some trust the technology, considering the vital role it plays in our daily lives, a driverless car, to them, would simply be another technological advancement.

نشرت صفحات الغش على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي اليوم إجابات امتحانات الجيولوجيا والتفاضل والتكامل وعلم النفس بعد بدء اللجان بدقائق قليلة.

كشفت وزارة التربية والتعليم أن ما تم تداوله على المواقع الإلكترونية من إجابات الامتحانات لا صحة له، وأنه لا يمت بصلة للامتحانات التي يجريها طلاب الثانوية العامة اليوم، موضحةً أنها صور لامتحانات الأعوام السابقة.

ضبط المتهمين:
أعلنت وزارة التربية والتعليم اليوم الأحد عن ضبط المتهمين في واقعة تسريب الامتحانات، حيث قام الطالب (م.أ.أ) بمحاولة غش ونشر امتحان مادة الجيولوجيا وعلوم البيئة على الإنترنت، والطالب (ش. أ. س) بمحافظة الدقهلية لمحاولته الغش باستخدام الهاتف المحمول في مادة التفاضل والتكامل، كما تم ضبط الطالب (أ. أ.ك) بإدارة "أبو تيج" بمحافظة أسيوط لمحاولته الغش والنشر على الإنترنت في مادة علم النفس والاجتماع، وجاري اتخاذ كافة الإجراءات القانونية.

سهولة امتحاني الجيولوجيا وعلم النفس:
أكد الطلاب أن امتحان مادة الجيولوجيا لطلاب شعبة العلمي علوم بالثانوية العامة جاء في مستوى الطالب المتوسط، كما أن امتحان علم النفس لطلاب القسم الأدبي جاء سهلاً.

Two-sided marketplaces have increasingly grown in popularity in recent years due to the accelerating growth of the sharing economy, which is estimated to reach a total combined revenue of $335 billion by 2025 (Osztovits A. and B. 2014). These platforms can be found in various areas such as labor (Upwork, TaskRabbit), accommodation (Airbnb, HomeAway), dating (Match.com, eHarmony), and ride-sharing (Uber, Lyft, Netlift). Extensive research has been conducted on two-sided markets over the last decade, with specific focus on applications such as those mentioned above (Rochet and Tirole 2003, Rysman 2009, Filistrucchi et al. 2014, Duch-Brown 2017; Hitsch et al. 2010, Horton 2010, Fradkin 2015, Banerjee et al. 2015, Marx and Schummer 2019).

Broadly speaking, two types of agents participate in these platforms: customers and suppliers. The platform facilitates transactions or matches when a customer and a supplier select each other based on their preferences. Unlike traditional marketplaces, modern platforms like Airbnb are increasingly taking agents' preferences into account when designing their systems (DeAmicis 2015, Tu et al. 2014, Horton 2017, Shi and Zhang 2019). By considering both sides' preferences, the platform can reduce frictions between agents' choices and improve overall outcomes (Fradkin 2015, Halaburda et al. 2016, Arnosti et al. 2018, Kanoria and Saban 2021).

Congestion among agents' choices is a common challenge in decentralized two-sided markets. Platforms benefit from understanding the preferences of customers and suppliers to mitigate congestion by limiting the information agents observe, thereby improving the final outcome (Kanoria and Saban 2021, Shi 2022b). One critical trade-off platforms face is balancing the information customers receive to prevent everyone choosing the same suppliers, while still providing enough options to keep customers engaged and avoid congestion.

The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) is rapidly emerging as a crucial framework that utilizes interconnected sensors, actuators, and devices not just for automation but also to enhance interconnectivity within the industrial ecosystem. This interconnectedness aids in decision-making processes by facilitating seamless communication between different parts of the network. Unlike traditional data collection methods, IIoT focuses on streamlining operations and improving communication between network components, driving digital transformation, automation, and efficiency in various sectors such as water, manufacturing, energy, infrastructure management, and healthcare.

Authors Keivan Faghih Niresi and Olga Fink are affiliated with the Intelligent Maintenance and Operations Systems (IMOS) Lab at EPFL, Switzerland, and can be reached via email at keivan.faghihniresi@epfl.ch and olga.fink@epfl.ch. Meanwhile, Hugo Bissig and Henri Baumann are associated with the Swiss Federal Institute of Metrology (METAS).

The reliability of IIoT heavily relies on the quality of data gathered from sensor networks integrated into complex systems. Challenges in achieving highly reliable measurements in IIoT include issues such as the high costs of installing numerous sensors, retrofitting existing systems with sensors, sparse sensor deployment, malfunctioning sensors, energy constraints related to deploying dense sensor networks, and harsh environmental conditions that may impede sensor installation. To address these challenges effectively, computational sensing techniques can be employed to unleash the full potential of intelligent systems powered by IIoT.

Soft sensing, a promising method, enhances the capabilities of physical sensors, improves data quality, and boosts the effectiveness of IIoT in monitoring complex system operations. Soft sensors, acting as mathematical models, estimate desired variables in new locations using data collected from physical sensors, particularly in places where physical sensors are unavailable. Soft sensing primarily employs two approaches: data-driven and physics-based modeling.

While traditional methods like the Kalman filter have been used for model parameter estimation, the limitations of these approaches, such as presuming linearity in system and observation model equations, can hinder their effectiveness in real-world industrial processes characterized by nonlinearity. Alternative methods like the unscented Kalman filter (UKF), squareroot UKF (SR-UKF), and extended Kalman filter (EKF) have been developed to address these challenges. Data-driven soft sensing approaches, utilizing statistical and machine learning techniques, offer effective solutions for scenarios where physical processes pose challenges for state estimation.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have emerged as effective tools in capturing complex interactions and interdependencies among nodes in sensor networks. Despite their potential, research gaps remain, particularly in scenarios with limited sensor coverage and challenges in interpretability and generalizability. Integrating physics principles with GNNs is a promising approach to enhance the interpretability, accuracy, and generalization of soft sensors.

To bridge these gaps, a novel approach is proposed to integrate physics principles into GNNs by augmenting graph structures with additional nodes derived from physics-based equations. This augmentation aims to enhance the interpretability and accuracy of soft sensor estimation by providing crucial information for inferring unobserved variables.

A case study of district heating networks is used to evaluate this methodology, focusing on estimating pressure and temperature values across the network using existing mass flow rate sensors. The study aims to improve the efficiency and safety of district heating networks by leveraging characteristic parameters of the network's components to estimate virtual sensors beyond raw sensor measurements. The proposed physics-enhanced model for soft sensing demonstrates improved performance, even in scenarios with noisy sensor readings and inaccuracies in physical parameters.

In summary, the contributions of this work include proposing a novel soft sensing model based on physics-enhanced GNNs, conducting experiments to evaluate its performance, and creating a new dataset for district heating networks.

Driverless cars are coming and are closer than we think. This essay will discuss three reasons why driverless cars are a phenomenal idea: innovation, adoption by major car companies, and safety.

Firstly, driverless cars are overwhelmingly innovative. Initially, many futurists doubted the possibility of self-driving cars, believing that smarter roads, not cars, were the key. However, the founder of the Google Car project, a pioneer in the field, has stated that the technology has finally caught up to the dream, showcasing the level of innovation achieved since the project's inception in 2009.

Secondly, major car companies are actively pursuing the development of driverless cars. For instance, Tesla, known for its innovation, has announced plans to release a car capable of driving on autopilot 90% of the time by 2016. Additionally, luxury brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Audi, and Nissan are aiming to introduce their own self-driving cars by 2020, indicating a widespread industry shift towards autonomous vehicles.
